senses.meaning_zh: 很大的；数量多的；程度高的
senses.meaning_en: large in size, amount, extent, or degree
senses.english_definition: You use great to describe something that is large in size or amount, or strong in degree.
senses.collocation_en: a great deal of; great difficulty
senses.collocation_zh: 大量的；很大的困难
senses.sentence_en: They went to great lengths to make us feel welcome.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们尽心尽力地让我们感受到欢迎。

senses.meaning_en: very good, enjoyable, or pleasing
senses.english_definition: If you describe something as great, you mean that it is very good or that you enjoy it very much.
senses.collocation_en: a great idea; have a great time
senses.collocation_zh: 一个好主意；玩得很开心
senses.sentence_en: We had a great time at the beach.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们在海滩玩得很开心。

senses.meaning_en: outstanding in ability or achievement, or very important
senses.english_definition: A great person is admired for exceptional abilities or achievements, and a great event or change has major importance.
senses.collocation_en: a great writer; a great achievement
senses.collocation_zh: 一位伟大的作家；一项重大成就
senses.sentence_en: She is widely regarded as one of the greatest scientists of her generation.
senses.sentence_zh: 她被广泛认为是她那一代最伟大的科学家之一。

senses.meaning_en: enthusiastic or habitual in a role, or very skilled at something
senses.english_definition: You can describe someone as a great admirer or reader to emphasize their enthusiasm or habits, or say they are great at something to praise their skill.
senses.collocation_en: a great admirer; great at cooking
senses.collocation_zh: 一位热情的仰慕者；很擅长烹饪
senses.sentence_en: I've always been a great admirer of her work.
senses.sentence_zh: 我一直非常欣赏她的作品。

senses.meaning_zh: 伟人；杰出人物（常用复数）
senses.meaning_en: a person recognized as outstanding in a particular field
senses.english_definition: The greats in a particular activity are the people considered among the best or most important in its history.
senses.collocation_en: the jazz greats; one of the all-time greats
senses.collocation_zh: 爵士乐大师们；历史上最杰出的人物之一
senses.sentence_en: She is remembered as one of the greats of world cinema.
senses.sentence_zh: 她作为世界电影史上的杰出人物之一而被人们铭记。

senses.meaning_zh: 很好地；很出色地（非正式，尤用于美式英语）
senses.meaning_en: very well, especially in informal American English
senses.english_definition: In informal English, especially American English, if someone does great, they perform or manage very well.
senses.collocation_en: do great; work great
senses.collocation_zh: 表现出色；运作得很好
senses.sentence_en: The new app works great on my phone.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个新应用在我的手机上运行得很好。

senses.meaning_zh: 太好了！；真棒！（也可反讽地表示不满）
senses.meaning_en: an expression of approval or pleasure, sometimes used sarcastically
senses.english_definition: You say Great! to show that you are pleased, or sarcastically to show that you are annoyed by unwelcome news.
senses.collocation_en: Great! Thanks!; Oh, great!
senses.collocation_zh: 太好了！谢谢！；噢，真够好的！（可表示反讽）
senses.sentence_en: Great! We can leave as soon as you're ready.
senses.sentence_zh: 太好了！你一准备好，我们就可以出发。

etymology_story.zh: great 来自古英语 grēat，早期主要表示“粗大的、厚实的、体积大的”。“大”的概念后来扩展到程度、重要性和成就，并在口语中发展为“极好的”。
etymology_story.en: Great comes from Old English grēat, whose early meanings included coarse, thick, and large. The idea of largeness extended to degree, importance, and achievement, and later developed the conversational meaning very good.

morphology_enriched.zh: great 是基本词；比较级 greater，最高级 greatest。直接派生词：greatly（大大地；非常）、greatness（伟大；卓越）；相关形式有 greats（杰出人物们）及 the greatest（最杰出者）。常见合成形式包括 great-grandparent（曾祖父母；曾外祖父母）和 great-grandchild（曾孙辈）；亲属称谓中的 great- 表示再隔一代，可重复使用。
morphology_enriched.en: Great is a base word; its comparative is greater and its superlative greatest. Direct derivatives include greatly (to a large degree) and greatness (outstanding importance or excellence); related forms include greats and the greatest. Common compounds include great-grandparent and great-grandchild. In kinship terms, great- marks an additional generation and can be repeated.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: excellent（极好的）明确评价质量优异，比口语 great 更具体；outstanding（杰出的）强调明显超过同类；large（大的）主要描述大小或数量，通常不包含 great 的赞赏或重要性含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Excellent specifically evaluates very high quality and is more precise than conversational great; outstanding emphasizes standing above others; large mainly describes size or quantity and usually lacks the admiration or importance conveyed by great.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“大”向外扩展：体积大是巨大，影响大是重大，成就大是伟大，满意程度高就是“太棒了”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Expand from 'big': big in size, big in impact, big in achievement, and big in approval—'Great!'

senses.meaning_en: a mathematical value or a symbol representing it
senses.english_definition: A number is a value used in counting or calculating, or a written symbol representing that value.
senses.collocation_en: an even number; a whole number
senses.collocation_zh: 偶数；整数
senses.sentence_en: Six is an even number.
senses.sentence_zh: 六是一个偶数。

senses.meaning_en: the total quantity of people or things
senses.english_definition: The number of people or things is how many of them there are.
senses.collocation_en: a large number of people; an increasing number of applications
senses.collocation_zh: 大量的人；越来越多的申请
senses.sentence_en: The number of visitors has doubled this year.
senses.sentence_zh: 今年的游客人数增加了一倍。

senses.meaning_en: a numerical label used to identify something
senses.english_definition: A number is a set of digits used to identify a particular person, place, or thing.
senses.collocation_en: a reference number; a room number
senses.collocation_zh: 参考编号；房间号
senses.sentence_en: Please write your booking number at the top of the form.
senses.sentence_zh: 请在表格顶部填写你的预订编号。

senses.meaning_en: a telephone number
senses.english_definition: Someone's number is the set of digits you use to call them on the telephone.
senses.collocation_en: a mobile number; the wrong number
senses.collocation_zh: 手机号码；错误的电话号码
senses.sentence_en: Can I have your number?
senses.sentence_zh: 可以给我你的电话号码吗？

senses.meaning_zh: 一期；一册，指连续出版物
senses.meaning_en: a particular issue of a regularly published magazine or journal
senses.english_definition: A number of a magazine or journal is one particular issue of it.
senses.collocation_en: the latest number; a back number
senses.collocation_zh: 最新一期；过刊
senses.sentence_en: The article appeared in the June number of the journal.
senses.sentence_zh: 这篇文章刊登在该期刊的六月刊上。

senses.meaning_zh: 一首歌曲；一段歌舞节目
senses.meaning_en: a song, dance, or other short performance
senses.english_definition: A number is a song, dance, or other short piece performed as part of a show.
senses.collocation_en: the opening number; a musical number
senses.collocation_zh: 开场节目；一段歌舞节目
senses.sentence_en: The band finished with a lively jazz number.
senses.sentence_zh: 乐队以一首欢快的爵士乐结束了演出。

senses.meaning_zh: 数，指语法中的单数、复数等类别
senses.meaning_en: the grammatical distinction between singular, plural, and related categories
senses.english_definition: In grammar, number shows whether a word refers to one person or thing, more than one, or another quantity category.
senses.collocation_en: grammatical number; agreement in number
senses.collocation_zh: 语法数；数的一致
senses.sentence_en: In English, a subject and its verb normally agree in number.
senses.sentence_zh: 在英语中，主语和谓语动词通常在数上保持一致。

senses.meaning_zh: 某件款式特别的东西，尤指衣服，属非正式用法
senses.meaning_en: a particular item, especially a distinctive piece of clothing, used informally
senses.english_definition: You can informally call a distinctive item of clothing a number, usually with words describing its appearance.
senses.collocation_en: a little black number; a slinky little number
senses.collocation_zh: 一件漂亮的小黑裙；一件贴身的小礼服
senses.sentence_en: She wore a little black number to the party.
senses.sentence_zh: 她穿了一件漂亮的小黑裙去参加聚会。

senses.meaning_en: to label things with numbers
senses.english_definition: If you number things, you give each of them a number so that they can be identified or put in order.
senses.collocation_en: number the pages; number consecutively
senses.collocation_zh: 给页面编号；连续编号
senses.sentence_en: Please number the pages from one to ten.
senses.sentence_zh: 请给这些页面编上一到十的页码。

senses.meaning_en: to amount to a particular total
senses.english_definition: If a group numbers a particular amount, it contains that many people or things.
senses.collocation_en: number in the thousands; number more than a hundred
senses.collocation_zh: 数以千计；总数超过一百
senses.sentence_en: The organization now numbers over five thousand members.
senses.sentence_zh: 该组织目前拥有五千多名成员。

senses.meaning_en: to include or classify someone or something in a group
senses.english_definition: If you number someone among a group, you regard them as belonging to that group.
senses.collocation_en: number among the best; be numbered among
senses.collocation_zh: 列入最优秀者之列；被列入……之中
senses.sentence_en: She is numbered among the country's finest writers.
senses.sentence_zh: 她被列为该国最优秀的作家之一。

senses.meaning_en: to count people or things, in relatively formal usage
senses.english_definition: If you number people or things, you count how many there are.
senses.collocation_en: too many to number; number the stars
senses.collocation_zh: 多得数不清；数星星
senses.sentence_en: The problems were too many to number.
senses.sentence_zh: 问题多得数不清。

etymology_story.zh: number 经古法语 nombre 进入中古英语，最终源自拉丁语 numerus，意为“数、数量”。它后来发展出“识别号码、出版物的一期、表演节目”等名词义，并转用为表示“计数、编号”的动词。
etymology_story.en: Number entered Middle English through Old French nombre, ultimately from Latin numerus, meaning 'number' or 'quantity.' It later developed noun senses such as an identifying label, an issue, and a performance piece, and became a verb meaning to count or label.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：number 是不可再按常用英语词素拆分的基础词，不能拆成 numb + -er。屈折形式：numbers（复数名词或动词第三人称单数）、numbered（过去式、过去分词）、numbering（现在分词或“编号”名词）。主要派生及复合词：numberless = number + -less（无数的），outnumber = out- + number（数量超过），renumber = re- + number（重新编号），numbered（有编号的），unnumbered = un- + numbered（未编号的），numbering（编号、编号系统），numberplate（车牌），number-crunching（大量数字运算）。历史同源词包括 numeral（数词、数字符号）、numerical（数字的）、numeric（数值的）、numerous（众多的）、enumerate（列举）和 innumerable（无数的）；这些不是在现代英语中直接给 number 添加词缀得到的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: number is a base word with no useful smaller English morphemes; it is not numb + -er. Inflections: numbers, numbered, and numbering. Principal derivatives and compounds include numberless = number + -less, outnumber = out- + number, renumber = re- + number, numbered, unnumbered = un- + numbered, numbering, numberplate, and number-crunching. Historical relatives include numeral, numerical, numeric, numerous, enumerate, and innumerable; these are not formed by directly adding modern English affixes to number.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quantity（数量）强调多少，可用于可数或不可数事物；number（数量）通常计算可数个体。figure（数字、数值）常指报告或统计中的具体数据。digit（数位符号）是 0—9 中的单个符号，一个 number 可以包含多个 digits。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quantity concerns how much or how many and can apply to countable or uncountable things; number usually counts separate items. Figure often means a particular reported or statistical value. A digit is one symbol from 0 to 9, while a number may contain several digits.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“数”：名词是数或号码；动词是数一数、编上号，或总计有多少。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to counting: a number is a value or label; to number is to count, label, or total.

senses.meaning_en: to go away from a person or place
senses.english_definition: If you leave a place or person, you go away from them.
senses.collocation_en: leave home; leave for work
senses.collocation_zh: 离开家；出发去上班
senses.sentence_en: We need to leave for the airport at six.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们需要六点出发去机场。

senses.meaning_zh: 离职；退学；退出；结束与某人的关系
senses.meaning_en: to stop belonging to an organization or being in a relationship
senses.english_definition: If you leave a job, school, organization, or partner, you stop working, studying, belonging, or living with them.
senses.collocation_en: leave a job; leave school
senses.collocation_zh: 离职；离校或结束学业
senses.sentence_en: She left her job to start her own business.
senses.sentence_zh: 她辞去了工作，开始自己创业。

senses.meaning_en: to let someone or something remain in a place
senses.english_definition: If you leave someone or something somewhere, they remain there when you go away, either deliberately or by accident.
senses.collocation_en: leave a message; leave something behind
senses.collocation_zh: 留言；把某物留下或忘带
senses.sentence_en: I left my keys on the kitchen table.
senses.sentence_zh: 我把钥匙落在厨房的桌子上了。

senses.meaning_zh: 让……保持某种状态；使……处于某种状态
senses.meaning_en: to keep or cause someone or something to be in a particular state
senses.english_definition: If you leave someone or something in a particular state, you allow that state to continue or cause it to exist.
senses.collocation_en: leave the door open; leave someone speechless
senses.collocation_zh: 让门开着；使某人说不出话来
senses.sentence_en: The news left everyone speechless.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个消息让所有人都说不出话来。

senses.meaning_en: to give someone responsibility for a task or decision
senses.english_definition: If you leave something to someone, you allow them to deal with it or decide what should happen.
senses.collocation_en: leave it to me; leave the decision to someone
senses.collocation_zh: 交给我处理；把决定权交给某人
senses.sentence_en: I'll leave the final decision to you.
senses.sentence_zh: 我会把最终决定权交给你。

senses.meaning_zh: 留到以后再做；暂不处理
senses.meaning_en: to delay dealing with something until a later time
senses.english_definition: If you leave something until later, you wait until that time before dealing with it.
senses.collocation_en: leave it until tomorrow; leave something until the last minute
senses.collocation_zh: 留到明天再处理；把某事拖到最后一刻
senses.sentence_en: Let's leave the washing-up until after dinner.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们吃完晚饭再洗碗吧。

senses.meaning_en: to stop disturbing, touching, or interfering with someone or something
senses.english_definition: If you leave someone or something alone, you do not disturb, touch, or interfere with them.
senses.collocation_en: leave someone alone; leave something alone
senses.collocation_zh: 别打扰某人；别碰或别干涉某事物
senses.sentence_en: Please leave the controls alone.
senses.sentence_zh: 请不要碰这些控制装置。

senses.meaning_zh: 剩下；余下；留下可用的时间或空间
senses.meaning_en: to result in something remaining or being available
senses.english_definition: If an action or situation leaves a particular amount of something, that amount remains or is available afterwards.
senses.collocation_en: leave enough time; leave room for improvement
senses.collocation_zh: 留出足够时间；留有改进余地
senses.sentence_en: Paying the rent leaves me very little money for anything else.
senses.sentence_zh: 付完房租后，我几乎没有钱用于其他开销。

senses.meaning_en: to give property to someone after one's death or leave surviving relatives
senses.english_definition: If someone leaves money or property to another person, that person receives it after their death; someone who dies may also leave surviving relatives.
senses.collocation_en: leave someone a fortune; leave something in a will
senses.collocation_zh: 给某人留下一大笔遗产；通过遗嘱留下某物
senses.sentence_en: Her aunt left her a small house in the country.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的姨妈给她留下了一栋乡间小屋。

senses.meaning_en: an authorized period away from work or duty
senses.english_definition: Leave is a period when you are officially allowed to be away from work or duty.
senses.collocation_en: annual leave; maternity leave
senses.collocation_zh: 年假；产假
senses.sentence_en: He is on annual leave this week.
senses.sentence_zh: 他这周在休年假。

senses.meaning_en: permission to do something, in formal usage
senses.english_definition: Leave is formal permission to do something.
senses.collocation_en: without leave; seek leave to appeal
senses.collocation_zh: 未经许可；申请上诉许可
senses.sentence_en: No one may enter the room without leave.
senses.sentence_zh: 未经许可，任何人不得进入该房间。

senses.meaning_zh: 告别，主要用于 take one's leave
senses.meaning_en: a departure or farewell, chiefly in the expression take one's leave
senses.english_definition: If you take your leave, you say goodbye and go away.
senses.collocation_en: take one's leave; take leave of someone
senses.collocation_zh: 告辞；向某人告别
senses.sentence_en: After thanking our hosts, we took our leave.
senses.sentence_zh: 向主人道谢后，我们便告辞了。

etymology_story.zh: 动词 leave 源自古英语 lǣfan，原义包括“让其留下、遗留”，后来也发展为“离开”。名词 leave 源自另一个古英语词 lēaf，意为“许可”；“休假”即获准暂离工作或职责。
etymology_story.en: The verb leave comes from Old English lǣfan, meaning to let remain or leave behind, and later also developed the sense of departing. The noun comes from a different Old English word, lēaf, meaning permission; its holiday sense refers to authorized absence from work or duty.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：leave 是基础词，无可实用拆分的前后缀。动词屈折：leaves（第三人称单数）、left（过去式、过去分词）、leaving（现在分词）；left 在此为不规则形式。名词表示“休假、许可”时通常不可数，特定语境中可说 leaves of absence（多次或多人的获准休假）。主要词族及复合词：leaver（离开者、离校生），school-leaver（中学毕业生），leavings（剩余物），leave-taking（告别）。leaf（树叶）及其复数 leaves 不属于这里的现代词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: leave is a base word without a useful prefix–suffix breakdown. Verb inflections are leaves, left, and leaving; left is irregular. The noun meaning permission or authorized absence is normally uncountable, though leaves of absence occurs for separate authorized absences. Principal family members and compounds include leaver, school-leaver, leavings, and leave-taking. Leaf and its plural leaves do not belong to this modern word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: depart（离开、启程）比 leave 正式，通常聚焦出发；abandon（抛弃）强调不再照顾或支持，语气比 leave 强；permission（许可）对应正式名词 leave 的许可义，但不直接表示一段假期。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Depart is more formal than leave and usually focuses on going away. Abandon suggests withdrawing care or support and is stronger than leave. Permission corresponds to the formal authorization sense of the noun leave, but does not itself mean a period away from work.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 动词抓住“人走、物留”；名词另记“获准离岗”：leave 是许可，也是假期。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the verb, picture someone going away while something remains. For the separate noun, think of permission to be away: leave is authorization or time off.

senses.meaning_en: small in size
senses.english_definition: A little thing is small in size.
senses.collocation_en: a little house; a little village
senses.collocation_zh: 一栋小房子；一个小村庄
senses.sentence_en: They live in a little house by the river.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们住在河边的一栋小房子里。

senses.meaning_en: young or younger
senses.english_definition: A little child is young, and someone's little brother or sister is younger than they are.
senses.collocation_en: a little girl; my little brother
senses.collocation_zh: 一个小女孩；我的弟弟
senses.sentence_en: My little sister has just started school.
senses.sentence_zh: 我的妹妹刚开始上学。

senses.meaning_zh: 微小的；不重要的；不严重的
senses.meaning_en: minor in importance, extent, or seriousness
senses.english_definition: A little problem, mistake, or detail is not very important or serious.
senses.collocation_en: a little mistake; a little problem
senses.collocation_zh: 一个小错误；一个小问题
senses.sentence_en: One little mistake won't ruin the whole project.
senses.sentence_zh: 一个小错误不会毁掉整个项目。

senses.meaning_zh: 带感情色彩的“小”，可表示亲昵、怜爱或轻蔑
senses.meaning_en: used to express affection, sympathy, or contempt
senses.english_definition: You can use little before a noun to show affection, sympathy, or contempt, rather than simply to describe size.
senses.collocation_en: a dear little thing; a nasty little man
senses.collocation_zh: 一个可爱的小家伙；一个讨厌的家伙
senses.sentence_en: Come here, you poor little thing.
senses.sentence_zh: 过来吧，你这个可怜的小家伙。

senses.meaning_zh: 少得几乎没有；a little 表示有一些，用于不可数名词前
senses.meaning_en: hardly any; with a, a small but existing amount
senses.english_definition: Little before an uncountable noun means hardly any, while a little means some, even if the amount is small.
senses.collocation_en: little evidence; a little time
senses.collocation_zh: 几乎没有证据；一点时间
senses.sentence_en: We have little time, but there is still a little hope.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们的时间所剩无几，但仍有一点希望。

senses.meaning_zh: 很少的量；a little 表示少量、一些
senses.meaning_en: a very small amount; with a, some
senses.english_definition: Little can stand for a very small amount without a following noun, while a little stands for some.
senses.collocation_en: little of it; a little of everything
senses.collocation_zh: 其中很少的一部分；各种都来一点
senses.sentence_en: There was plenty of food, but he ate very little.
senses.sentence_zh: 食物很多，但他吃得很少。

senses.meaning_en: not much or hardly at all
senses.english_definition: If something happens little or affects you little, it happens or affects you only to a small degree.
senses.collocation_en: little known; little changed
senses.collocation_zh: 鲜为人知；变化很小
senses.sentence_en: The village has changed little in fifty years.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个村庄五十年来变化很小。

senses.meaning_zh: 有点；稍微，通常用于 a little
senses.meaning_en: slightly or to a small degree, usually in a little
senses.english_definition: If something is a little different or changes a little, the difference or change is small.
senses.collocation_en: a little tired; a little better
senses.collocation_zh: 有点累；好一点
senses.sentence_en: I feel a little better today.
senses.sentence_zh: 我今天感觉好一点了。

etymology_story.zh: little 源自古英语 lȳtel，意为“小的、少量的”，与表示“小、少”的古日耳曼语词族有关。它以“规模小”为核心，逐渐广泛用于年龄、数量、程度，以及亲昵或轻蔑等态度表达。
etymology_story.en: Little comes from Old English lȳtel, meaning small or slight in amount, and belongs to an old Germanic family associated with smallness. Its central idea of small scale extends to age, quantity, degree, and expressions of affection or contempt.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：little 通常作为整体基础词学习，不把结尾 -le 当作现代可自由使用的后缀。表示数量或程度时，比较级和最高级通常为 less（较少、更少）和 least（最少）；表示尺寸时通常用 smaller（更小）和 smallest（最小），也有 littler、littlest，尤用于非正式或带感情色彩的表达。主要词族及复合词：littleness = little + -ness（微小、渺小），belittle = be- + little（贬低），belittling（贬低的；贬低行为），little-known（鲜为人知的）。a little（一些、稍微）和 little by little（一点一点地）是短语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: little is normally learned as a whole base; its ending -le is not treated as a freely productive modern suffix. For quantity or degree, the usual comparative and superlative are less and least. For size, smaller and smallest are usual alternatives; littler and littlest also occur, especially in informal or expressive language. Principal family members and compounds include littleness = little + -ness, belittle = be- + little, belittling, and little-known. A little and little by little are phrases.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: small（小的）较中性，主要陈述尺寸或规模；little（小的）还常带亲昵、轻蔑等态度。tiny（极小的）强调尺寸非常小。few（很少的）用于可数名词复数，little 的数量义用于不可数名词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Small is relatively neutral and mainly describes size or scale; little often also conveys affection or contempt. Tiny means extremely small in size. Few modifies plural countable nouns, while little in its quantity sense modifies uncountable nouns.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一条“小尺度”贯通：东西小、年龄小、数量少、程度低；little 偏“几乎没有”，a little 偏“还有一点”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think small scale: small size, young age, small quantity, or slight degree. Little stresses near absence; a little stresses that some remains.

senses.meaning_en: to see and become acquainted with someone for the first time
senses.english_definition: If you meet someone, you see and speak to them for the first time.
senses.collocation_en: meet new people; pleased to meet you
senses.collocation_zh: 结识新朋友；很高兴认识你
senses.sentence_en: I met my closest friend at university.
senses.sentence_zh: 我在大学里认识了我最亲密的朋友。

senses.meaning_en: to come together with someone by arrangement or chance
senses.english_definition: If you meet someone, you come together with them, either because you have arranged it or by chance.
senses.collocation_en: meet for lunch; meet by chance
senses.collocation_zh: 见面吃午饭；偶然相遇
senses.sentence_en: Let's meet outside the station at noon.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们中午在车站外见面吧。

senses.meaning_en: to go to a place to welcome someone arriving
senses.english_definition: If you meet someone at a station, airport, or similar place, you go there to welcome them when they arrive.
senses.collocation_en: meet someone at the airport; meet someone off the train
senses.collocation_zh: 到机场接某人；接某人下火车
senses.sentence_en: My brother will meet us at the airport.
senses.sentence_zh: 我哥哥会到机场接我们。

senses.meaning_zh: 达到；满足，指要求、标准或需求
senses.meaning_en: to satisfy a requirement, standard, or need
senses.english_definition: If something meets a requirement, standard, or need, it is good enough or suitable enough to satisfy it.
senses.collocation_en: meet the requirements; meet someone's needs
senses.collocation_zh: 满足要求；满足某人的需求
senses.sentence_en: The new system meets all our requirements.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个新系统满足了我们的全部要求。

senses.meaning_zh: 按时完成；实现，指期限、目标等
senses.meaning_en: to achieve a target or finish something by the required time
senses.english_definition: If you meet a target or deadline, you achieve the required result or finish by the required time.
senses.collocation_en: meet a deadline; meet a target
senses.collocation_zh: 赶上截止期限；达到目标
senses.sentence_en: We worked through the weekend to meet the deadline.
senses.sentence_zh: 为了按期完成，我们整个周末都在工作。

senses.meaning_en: to pay or provide the money for a cost
senses.english_definition: If you meet a cost or expense, you provide the money needed to pay it.
senses.collocation_en: meet the cost; meet expenses
senses.collocation_zh: 承担费用；支付开支
senses.sentence_en: The grant will meet the cost of the equipment.
senses.sentence_zh: 这笔补助金将用于支付设备费用。

senses.meaning_en: to encounter a situation, reaction, or difficulty
senses.english_definition: If you meet resistance, difficulty, or a particular reaction, you experience it while trying to do something.
senses.collocation_en: meet resistance; meet with approval
senses.collocation_zh: 遇到阻力；得到赞同
senses.sentence_en: The proposal met with strong opposition.
senses.sentence_zh: 这项提议遭到了强烈反对。

senses.meaning_en: to join, touch, or cross
senses.english_definition: If two lines, roads, or other things meet, they touch, join, or cross at a particular point.
senses.collocation_en: where two roads meet; where the rivers meet
senses.collocation_zh: 两条路的交会处；河流汇合处
senses.sentence_en: The hotel stands where the two rivers meet.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家酒店位于两条河流的交汇处。

senses.meaning_en: to compete against an opponent
senses.english_definition: If one player or team meets another, they compete against each other.
senses.collocation_en: meet in the final; meet a strong opponent
senses.collocation_zh: 在决赛中相遇；遇上强劲对手
senses.sentence_en: The two teams will meet in the final on Sunday.
senses.sentence_zh: 两支球队将于星期日在决赛中交锋。

senses.meaning_zh: 体育比赛；运动会，尤见于美式英语
senses.meaning_en: an organized sporting competition, especially in American English
senses.english_definition: A meet is an organized event at which people compete in a sport such as athletics, swimming, or gymnastics.
senses.collocation_en: a track meet; a swim meet
senses.collocation_zh: 田径运动会；游泳比赛
senses.sentence_en: She won three medals at the swim meet.
senses.sentence_zh: 她在这次游泳比赛中获得了三枚奖牌。

etymology_story.zh: meet 源自古英语 mētan，意为“遇见、碰到”，与 moot 等表示集会的日耳曼语词在历史上有关。“相遇”的含义延伸为线条相接、与对手交锋，以及能力或结果与要求相匹配；体育赛事的名词义由动词转化而来。
etymology_story.en: Meet comes from Old English mētan, meaning to encounter, and is historically related to Germanic gathering words such as moot. The idea of coming together extends to lines joining, opponents competing, and results matching requirements; the sporting noun developed from the verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：meet 是基础词，无需拆分。动词屈折：meets（第三人称单数）、met（过去式、过去分词）、meeting（现在分词）；名词复数为 meets。主要词族及复合词：meeting（会议、会面），unmet = un- + met（未满足的），meetup 或 meet-up（聚会），meeting place（会面地点），meeting point（集合点、交会点）。meeting 可指会议；meet 作名词主要用于体育赛事，两者不能随意替换。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: meet is a base word without a useful smaller breakdown. Verb inflections are meets, met, and meeting; the noun plural is meets. Principal family members and compounds include meeting, unmet = un- + met, meetup or meet-up, meeting place, and meeting point. Meeting can mean a conference or arranged gathering, whereas the noun meet chiefly names a sporting event; they are not freely interchangeable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: encounter（遇到、遭遇）常强调偶然相遇或遇到困难，比 meet 正式；satisfy（满足）强调要求或需求得到充分满足，对应 meet requirements 中的 meet；fulfil（履行、实现）常用于义务、承诺或愿望，强调完成其内容。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Encounter often suggests an unplanned meeting or a difficulty and is more formal than meet. Satisfy emphasizes adequately meeting a need or requirement. Fulfil commonly concerns carrying out an obligation or promise, or realizing a wish.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“碰到一起”：人碰面、线相交；结果碰到标准，就是“达到要求”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of two things coming together: people meet, lines meet, and a result meets the standard it reaches.

senses.meaning_en: to assist someone in doing something
senses.english_definition: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something by giving assistance.
senses.collocation_en: help someone with something; help someone do something
senses.collocation_zh: 在某事上帮助某人；帮助某人做某事
senses.sentence_en: Could you help me carry these boxes?
senses.sentence_zh: 你能帮我搬这些箱子吗？

senses.meaning_zh: 有帮助；有助于；改善或缓解
senses.meaning_en: to make a situation better, easier, or less painful
senses.english_definition: If something helps, it improves a situation or makes a problem less serious.
senses.collocation_en: help reduce stress; help relieve pain
senses.collocation_zh: 有助于减轻压力；帮助缓解疼痛
senses.sentence_en: A short break may help you concentrate.
senses.sentence_zh: 短暂休息可能有助于你集中注意力。

senses.meaning_zh: 给……盛取食物或饮料；自行取用
senses.meaning_en: to serve food or drink, or take it for oneself
senses.english_definition: If you help someone to food or drink, you serve them some; if you help yourself, you take some for yourself.
senses.collocation_en: help yourself to some cake; help someone to another serving
senses.collocation_zh: 自己取些蛋糕；再给某人盛一份
senses.sentence_en: Please help yourself to some bread.
senses.sentence_zh: 请自己取些面包吃。

senses.meaning_zh: 避免；控制；忍住，通常用于否定结构
senses.meaning_en: to avoid or control something, usually in negative constructions
senses.english_definition: If you cannot help doing something, you cannot stop yourself from doing it; if something cannot be helped, it cannot be avoided.
senses.collocation_en: can't help laughing; it can't be helped
senses.collocation_zh: 忍不住笑；这也没有办法
senses.sentence_en: I couldn't help laughing at his expression.
senses.sentence_zh: 看到他的表情，我忍不住笑了。

senses.meaning_en: assistance given to someone
senses.english_definition: Help is assistance that makes it easier for someone to do something or deal with a problem.
senses.collocation_en: ask for help; with the help of someone
senses.collocation_zh: 寻求帮助；在某人的帮助下
senses.sentence_en: With your help, we finished the work on time.
senses.sentence_zh: 在你的帮助下，我们按时完成了工作。

senses.meaning_en: a person or thing that provides useful assistance
senses.english_definition: If someone or something is a help, they make a task or situation easier.
senses.collocation_en: a great help; a real help
senses.collocation_zh: 很大的帮助；真正有帮助的人或事物
senses.sentence_en: The checklist was a great help during the move.
senses.sentence_zh: 搬家时，这份清单帮了大忙。

senses.meaning_zh: 帮工；受雇提供帮助的人，尤指家务帮手
senses.meaning_en: people employed to provide assistance, especially with housework
senses.english_definition: Help can mean someone employed to assist with work, especially cleaning or other household tasks.
senses.collocation_en: domestic help; hire some help
senses.collocation_zh: 家务帮工；雇人帮忙
senses.sentence_en: They hired some help to clean the house twice a week.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们雇人每周来打扫两次房子。

senses.meaning_zh: 帮助信息；使用说明，尤指软件中的帮助功能
senses.meaning_en: instructions or guidance, especially within software
senses.english_definition: Help in a computer program is information that explains how to use the program or solve problems with it.
senses.collocation_en: the Help menu; online help
senses.collocation_zh: 帮助菜单；在线帮助
senses.sentence_en: Open the Help menu for instructions.
senses.sentence_zh: 打开“帮助”菜单查看操作说明。

senses.meaning_en: a cry asking for urgent assistance
senses.english_definition: You shout 'Help!' when you urgently need someone to assist or rescue you.
senses.collocation_en: Help! Help!; Help, I'm stuck!
senses.collocation_zh: 救命！救命！；帮帮我，我被困住了！
senses.sentence_en: Help! Someone has fallen into the river!
senses.sentence_zh: 救命！有人掉进河里了！

etymology_story.zh: help 源自古英语 helpan，意为“帮助、援助”，属于古老的日耳曼语词族。现代的规则过去式 helped 取代了较早的不规则变化；“无法控制或避免”的用法保留在 cannot help 等结构中。
etymology_story.en: Help comes from Old English helpan, meaning to assist or aid, and belongs to an old Germanic word family. The modern regular past form helped replaced earlier irregular forms; the sense of being unable to control or avoid something survives in constructions such as cannot help.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：help 是基础词。动词屈折：helps（第三人称单数）、helped（过去式、过去分词）、helping（现在分词）；表示一般“帮助”的名词通常不可数，a help 可指有帮助的人或事物。主要词族：helper = help + -er（帮手），helpful = help + -ful（有帮助的），helpfully（有帮助地、热心地），helpfulness（有帮助、热心），unhelpful（无帮助的），unhelpfully（无帮助地），unhelpfulness（无帮助），helpless = help + -less（无助的），helplessly（无助地），helplessness（无助）。其他常用形式：helping（食物的一份），helpings（多份食物），self-help（自助），helpdesk（服务台、技术支持台），help out（帮忙解决困难）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: help is a base word. Verb inflections are helps, helped, and helping. The noun meaning general assistance is normally uncountable, while a help can identify a useful person or thing. Principal derivatives include helper = help + -er, helpful = help + -ful, helpfully, helpfulness, unhelpful, unhelpfully, unhelpfulness, helpless = help + -less, helplessly, and helplessness. Other common forms include helping, meaning a serving of food, its plural helpings, self-help, helpdesk, and the phrasal verb help out.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: assist（协助）比 help 正式，常指参与某项具体任务；aid（援助）较正式，常用于救援、医疗或物资支持；support（支持）强调持续提供情感、资金或实际保障。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Assist is more formal than help and often refers to participation in a specific task. Aid is relatively formal and common in rescue, medical, or material assistance. Support emphasizes continuing emotional, financial, or practical backing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“让事情更容易”：帮人、改善情况、递食物；can't help 则单记为“控制不住、无法避免”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The core is making things easier: assist a person, improve a situation, or serve food. Remember can't help separately as being unable to control or avoid something.

senses.meaning_zh: 自己的；本人特有的；亲自完成的
senses.meaning_en: belonging specifically to someone or done personally by them
senses.english_definition: You use own after a possessive to emphasize that something belongs to a particular person or that they do something themselves.
senses.collocation_en: your own home; in your own words
senses.collocation_zh: 你自己的家；用你自己的话
senses.sentence_en: Please explain the idea in your own words.
senses.sentence_zh: 请用你自己的话解释这个想法。

senses.meaning_en: something belonging to the person mentioned
senses.english_definition: Your own is something that belongs to you, rather than something that you borrow or share.
senses.collocation_en: a place of your own; one of my own
senses.collocation_zh: 属于你自己的住处；我自己的一个
senses.sentence_en: I borrow my sister's bike because I don't have one of my own.
senses.sentence_zh: 我借姐姐的自行车骑，因为我自己没有自行车。

senses.meaning_en: to have something as your property
senses.english_definition: If you own something, it belongs to you.
senses.collocation_en: own a house; privately owned
senses.collocation_zh: 拥有一套房子；私人所有的
senses.sentence_en: Her parents own a small restaurant.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的父母拥有一家小餐馆。

senses.meaning_zh: 承认；承担责任；坦然接受
senses.meaning_en: to acknowledge something and accept responsibility for it
senses.english_definition: If you own a mistake or decision, you accept that it is yours and take responsibility for it.
senses.collocation_en: own your mistakes; own up to something
senses.collocation_zh: 承认并承担自己的错误；坦白承认某事
senses.sentence_en: A good leader owns their mistakes and learns from them.
senses.sentence_zh: 优秀的领导者会承认自己的错误、承担责任，并从中吸取教训。

senses.meaning_en: to defeat someone decisively or take complete control
senses.english_definition: If someone owns an opponent or a situation, they perform so well that they clearly dominate them.
senses.collocation_en: own the stage; own the competition
senses.collocation_zh: 掌控全场舞台；在竞争中占据绝对优势
senses.sentence_en: From her first song, she owned the stage.
senses.sentence_zh: 从第一首歌开始，她就掌控了整个舞台。

etymology_story.zh: own 源自古英语 āgen，原为 āgan（拥有）的过去分词，表示“被拥有的、属于自己的”。这一所有关系后来发展出动词“拥有”，并引申为承认责任以及非正式用法中的完全掌控。
etymology_story.en: Own comes from Old English āgen, originally the past participle of āgan, meaning 'to possess,' and described something possessed or belonging to someone. This relationship developed into the verb meaning 'possess' and later extended to accepting responsibility and, informally, exercising complete control.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 own 是不可再作常用词素切分的基础词，可作形容词、代词和动词；动词词形为 owns、owned、owning。常用词族：own + -er → owner（所有者），owner + -ship → ownership（所有权），owner + -less → ownerless（无主的），dis- + own → disown（否认关系；断绝关系），co- + owner → co-owner（共同所有者）；常见复合词还有 homeowner（房主）、homeownership（住房所有权）和 owner-occupier（自住房业主）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, own is a base word without a useful division into smaller common morphemes and functions as an adjective, pronoun, and verb; its verb forms are owns, owned, and owning. Its common family includes own + -er → owner, owner + -ship → ownership, owner + -less → ownerless, dis- + own → disown, and co- + owner → co-owner; compounds include homeowner, homeownership, and owner-occupier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: possess（拥有）较正式，也可指拥有能力或品质；have（有）范围最广，不一定表示所有权；belong to（属于）从物品的角度说明归属，如 The house belongs to her 对应 She owns the house。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Possess is more formal and can also describe having abilities or qualities; have is broader and does not necessarily imply ownership; belong to expresses the same ownership relationship from the item's perspective, as in 'The house belongs to her' versus 'She owns the house.'

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“归自己”：自己的东西 → 拥有它；自己的错误 → 承担它。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'belongs to me': my own things are things I own; my own mistakes are mistakes I must own.

senses.meaning_en: to say or write something in order to obtain information
senses.english_definition: If you ask someone a question, you say or write something because you want them to give you information.
senses.collocation_en: ask a question; ask for directions
senses.collocation_zh: 提问；问路
senses.sentence_en: I asked a passer-by for directions to the station.
senses.sentence_zh: 我向一位路人打听去车站的路。

senses.meaning_en: to request something or request that someone do something
senses.english_definition: If you ask for something or ask someone to do something, you tell them what you would like them to give you or do.
senses.collocation_en: ask for help; ask someone to do something
senses.collocation_zh: 求助；请某人做某事
senses.sentence_en: She asked me to check the figures before the meeting.
senses.sentence_zh: 她请我在开会前核对这些数字。

senses.meaning_en: to invite someone to a place or event
senses.english_definition: If you ask someone to dinner or ask them over, you invite them to join you.
senses.collocation_en: ask someone over; ask someone out
senses.collocation_zh: 邀请某人到家里来；邀请某人约会
senses.sentence_en: We asked our new neighbors over for dinner.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们邀请新邻居到家里吃晚饭。

senses.meaning_en: to state the price wanted for something being sold
senses.english_definition: If someone asks a particular price for something, that is the amount of money they want you to pay for it.
senses.collocation_en: ask a high price; ask too much
senses.collocation_zh: 要价很高；要价过高
senses.sentence_en: They're asking £300 for the old desk.
senses.sentence_zh: 这张旧书桌他们要价三百英镑。

senses.meaning_zh: 〔非正式〕请求；要求；需要完成的艰巨任务
senses.meaning_en: a request or demand, especially one that is difficult to meet
senses.english_definition: An ask is something that someone requests or expects, especially when providing or achieving it may be difficult.
senses.collocation_en: a big ask; a tough ask
senses.collocation_zh: 很高的要求；难以完成的要求
senses.sentence_en: Finishing the whole report by tomorrow is a big ask.
senses.sentence_zh: 要求明天之前完成整份报告，确实很难做到。

etymology_story.zh: ask 源自古英语 āscian，也有 āxian 等词形，核心意思就是询问或请求。现代的邀请、要价以及名词“请求”等用法，都从向别人提出某种要求这一核心发展而来。
etymology_story.en: Ask comes from Old English āscian, with variants including āxian, meaning 'inquire' or 'request.' Its uses for inviting someone, stating a price, and naming a request all developed from the central idea of putting something to another person.

morphology_enriched.zh: ask 是基础动词，现代构词不宜强拆；词形为 asks、asked、asking。派生词 asker（提问者；请求者）由 ask + -er 构成；asking 可作动名词或分词，并用于 asking price（要价）。常用短语动词包括 ask for（请求）、ask about（询问有关情况）、ask around（四处打听）、ask out（邀请约会）和 ask over（邀请到家中）；名词 ask 由动词直接转类而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Ask is a base verb without a useful smaller morphological breakdown; its forms are asks, asked, and asking. Ask + -er forms asker; asking functions as a gerund or participle and occurs in asking price. Common combinations include ask for, ask about, ask around, ask out, and ask over; the noun ask is formed by conversion from the verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inquire（询问）较正式，侧重获取信息；request（请求）较正式，侧重希望得到某物或某种行动；demand（要求）语气强硬，通常表示认为对方有义务满足要求。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inquire is more formal and focuses on obtaining information; request is more formal and focuses on obtaining something or having an action performed; demand is forceful and usually implies that compliance is expected.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 开口向别人要：要信息是“问”，要帮助是“请求”，要价钱是“开价”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ask reaches toward another person: for information, it means question; for assistance, request; for payment, name a price.

senses.meaning_en: a portion or section of a whole
senses.english_definition: A part of something is one of the portions or sections that together make up the whole.
senses.collocation_en: part of the problem; the first part
senses.collocation_zh: 问题的一部分；第一部分
senses.sentence_en: The first part of the report explains our methods.
senses.sentence_zh: 报告的第一部分说明了我们采用的方法。

senses.meaning_en: a component of a machine, object, or body
senses.english_definition: A part is a piece or section of a machine, object, or body that has a particular place or function.
senses.collocation_en: spare parts; body parts
senses.collocation_zh: 备用零件；身体部位
senses.sentence_en: We need to order a replacement part for the washing machine.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们需要为洗衣机订购一个替换零件。

senses.meaning_zh: 角色；台词；声部；演奏部分
senses.meaning_en: a dramatic role or a performer's portion of a work
senses.english_definition: A performer's part is the character they play or the words or music they are responsible for performing.
senses.collocation_en: play the leading part; learn your part
senses.collocation_zh: 担任主角；熟悉自己要表演的部分
senses.sentence_en: She played the part of a young doctor in the series.
senses.sentence_zh: 她在这部连续剧中饰演一位年轻医生。

senses.meaning_en: someone's involvement, contribution, or responsibility
senses.english_definition: Your part in an activity is what you do to help carry it out or influence its result.
senses.collocation_en: take part in; play a part in
senses.collocation_zh: 参加；在……中起作用
senses.sentence_en: Everyone has a part to play in keeping the neighborhood clean.
senses.sentence_zh: 保持社区整洁，人人都有一份责任。

senses.meaning_en: to separate, move apart, or leave one another
senses.english_definition: If people or things part, or if you part them, they separate or move away from one another.
senses.collocation_en: part company; part ways
senses.collocation_zh: 分开；分道扬镳
senses.sentence_en: We parted at the station and promised to keep in touch.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们在车站分别，并答应保持联系。

senses.meaning_zh: 给头发分缝；把头发分向两边
senses.meaning_en: to divide hair with a line so that it falls in different directions
senses.english_definition: If you part your hair, you arrange it on either side of a line on your head.
senses.collocation_en: part your hair; part your hair in the middle
senses.collocation_zh: 给头发分缝；把头发梳成中分
senses.sentence_en: He parts his hair on the left.
senses.sentence_zh: 他把头发的分缝留在左侧。

senses.meaning_en: involving only a portion of something
senses.english_definition: You use part before certain nouns to show that something involves only a share of the whole.
senses.collocation_en: part payment; part owner
senses.collocation_zh: 部分付款；共同所有者之一
senses.sentence_en: She is part owner of a small publishing company.
senses.sentence_zh: 她是一家小型出版公司的共同所有者之一。

senses.meaning_en: partly or to some extent
senses.english_definition: You use part before a description to say that it is true to some extent, often alongside another description.
senses.collocation_en: part funded; part science, part art
senses.collocation_zh: 得到部分资助的；既有科学成分，也有艺术成分
senses.sentence_en: The book is part memoir and part travel guide.
senses.sentence_zh: 这本书一部分是回忆录，一部分是旅行指南。

etymology_story.zh: 名词 part 经古法语 part 进入英语，最终源自拉丁语 pars、属格 partis，意为部分或份额。动词与古法语 partir（划分；离开）有关，因此“整体的一部分”与“分开、分别”共享同一个历史核心。
etymology_story.en: The noun part entered English through Old French part, ultimately from Latin pars, with the stem partis, meaning 'portion' or 'share.' The verb is connected with Old French partir, meaning 'divide' or 'leave,' linking a portion of a whole with the act of separating.

morphology_enriched.zh: part 在现代英语中是基础词，可通过直接转类作名词、动词、形容词和副词；动词词形为 parts、parted、parting。常用派生与复合形式包括 part + -ly → partly（部分地）、parting（离别；分缝）、partway（在中途；部分地）、part-time（兼职的／地）、part-timer（兼职者）、counterpart（对应的人或物）和 spare part（备用零件）；partial、partition、partner 属于历史上相关的词，不能都按现代 part 加普通后缀机械拆解。
morphology_enriched.en: Part is a modern base word used as a noun, verb, adjective, and adverb through conversion; its verb forms are parts, parted, and parting. Common family members and compounds include part + -ly → partly, parting, partway, part-time, part-timer, counterpart, and spare part; partial, partition, and partner are historically related words rather than uniformly transparent combinations of modern part with ordinary suffixes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: portion（部分；一份）常强调数量、分配或食物份量；section（部分；区段）强调边界或组织结构清楚的一段；component（组成部件）强调构成整体并具有特定功能的单元。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Portion often emphasizes quantity, allocation, or a serving of food; section emphasizes a clearly bounded or organized division; component emphasizes a functional unit that helps make up a larger whole.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整体分开，就得到 part；人彼此分开，就是 part；只占一部分，就是 part 或 partly。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Separate a whole and you get a part; separate from someone and you part; describe only a portion and you use part or partly.

senses.meaning_en: a nation with its own government and territory
senses.english_definition: A country is an area of land that has its own government and is recognized as a political unit.
senses.collocation_en: a foreign country; developing countries
senses.collocation_zh: 外国；发展中国家
senses.sentence_en: She has worked in three different countries.
senses.sentence_zh: 她曾在三个不同的国家工作。

senses.meaning_en: rural areas outside towns and cities
senses.english_definition: The country is land outside towns and cities, where there are fields, farms, or natural landscapes.
senses.collocation_en: live in the country; move to the country
senses.collocation_zh: 住在乡下；搬到乡下
senses.sentence_en: They moved to the country to enjoy a quieter life.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们搬到乡下，享受更安静的生活。

senses.meaning_zh: 具有某种自然特征的地区；地带
senses.meaning_en: land or a region with a particular physical character
senses.english_definition: Country of a particular kind is land that has the features you describe.
senses.collocation_en: open country; mountainous country
senses.collocation_zh: 开阔地带；多山地区
senses.sentence_en: The road runs through miles of open country.
senses.sentence_zh: 这条路穿过绵延数英里的开阔地带。

senses.meaning_en: the people of a nation considered collectively
senses.english_definition: You can refer to the people of a nation collectively as the country.
senses.collocation_en: the whole country; unite the country
senses.collocation_zh: 全国人民；团结全国人民
senses.sentence_en: The whole country celebrated the team's victory.
senses.sentence_zh: 全国人民都在庆祝这支球队获胜。

senses.meaning_en: a style of popular music originating in the southern United States
senses.english_definition: Country is a style of popular music that developed in the southern United States and often features guitars and songs about everyday life.
senses.collocation_en: listen to country; country and western
senses.collocation_zh: 听乡村音乐；乡村与西部音乐
senses.sentence_en: She listens to country on long drives.
senses.sentence_zh: 长途开车时，她会听乡村音乐。

senses.meaning_zh: 乡村的；乡间的；具有乡村特色的
senses.meaning_en: relating to rural places or rural life
senses.english_definition: Country things are found in rural areas or have qualities associated with rural life.
senses.collocation_en: a country cottage; country life
senses.collocation_zh: 乡间小屋；乡村生活
senses.sentence_en: They spent the weekend in a country cottage.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们在一间乡间小屋里度过了周末。

etymology_story.zh: country 经古法语 contree 进入英语，追溯到中世纪拉丁语 contrata，通常解释为“位于对面的土地”，与拉丁语 contra（对面；相对）有关。它先表示地区或土地，后来发展出国家、乡村等意义。
etymology_story.en: Country entered English through Old French contree, tracing back to Medieval Latin contrata, commonly explained as 'the land lying opposite' and related to Latin contra, meaning 'opposite.' A meaning centered on land or territory developed into the senses of a nation and rural areas.

morphology_enriched.zh: country 在现代英语中是不可按 coun-、-try 拆解的基础名词，也有形容词用法；复数为 countries，遵循辅音字母加 y 结尾变 y 为 ies 的规则。常用复合词与派生形式包括 countryside（乡村地区）、countrywide（全国性的／地）、countryman／countrymen（同胞；乡下人）、countrywoman／countrywomen（女同胞；乡村妇女）、countryfolk（乡下人）和 cross-country（越野的／地；横跨全国的／地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Country is a modern base noun, also used adjectivally, and should not be divided into coun- and -try; its plural countries follows the consonant-plus-y to -ies spelling rule. Common compounds and derived forms include countryside, countrywide, countryman/countrymen, countrywoman/countrywomen, countryfolk, and cross-country.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nation（民族；国家）常强调共同身份、历史和人民；state（国家）强调政治与法律组织；countryside（乡村）只指乡间地区，不表示一个主权国家。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nation often emphasizes a people with a shared identity and history; state emphasizes political and legal organization; countryside refers specifically to rural land and does not mean a sovereign nation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“土地与地域”：有政府的一片土地是国家，城镇之外的土地是乡村。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor country to land: land organized under a government is a nation; land outside towns is the country.

senses.meaning_en: to move something into a particular place or position
senses.english_definition: If you put something somewhere, you move it into that place or position.
senses.collocation_en: put something down; put something in place
senses.collocation_zh: 放下某物；把某物放到合适的位置
senses.sentence_en: Please put the keys on the table.
senses.sentence_zh: 请把钥匙放在桌上。

senses.meaning_zh: 使处于某种状态或境地
senses.meaning_en: to cause someone or something to enter a particular state or situation
senses.english_definition: If something puts someone in a particular situation, it causes them to be in that situation.
senses.collocation_en: put someone at risk; put pressure on someone
senses.collocation_zh: 使某人面临风险；给某人施加压力
senses.sentence_en: The delay put us under considerable pressure.
senses.sentence_zh: 这次延误给我们带来了相当大的压力。

senses.meaning_en: to express something in a particular way
senses.english_definition: When you put something a particular way, you use certain words to express it.
senses.collocation_en: put it simply; put something into words
senses.collocation_zh: 简单地说；用语言表达某事
senses.sentence_en: It is difficult to put these feelings into words.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些感受很难用语言表达。

senses.meaning_en: to present a question, proposal, or issue for consideration
senses.english_definition: If you put a question or proposal to someone, you present it so that they can consider or respond to it.
senses.collocation_en: put a question to someone; put something to a vote
senses.collocation_zh: 向某人提出问题；将某事付诸表决
senses.sentence_en: The committee put the proposal to a vote.
senses.sentence_zh: 委员会将这项提案付诸表决。

senses.meaning_en: to estimate an amount, value, or level
senses.english_definition: If you put a quantity at a particular figure, you estimate that it is that amount.
senses.collocation_en: put the cost at; put the figure at
senses.collocation_zh: 估计成本为；估计数字为
senses.sentence_en: Engineers put the repair cost at around £20,000.
senses.sentence_zh: 工程师估计维修费用约为两万英镑。

senses.meaning_en: to devote time, effort, or money to something
senses.english_definition: If you put time, effort, or money into something, you use those resources to develop or support it.
senses.collocation_en: put effort into; put money into
senses.collocation_zh: 投入精力于；投入资金于
senses.sentence_en: She put a lot of effort into preparing the lesson.
senses.sentence_zh: 她为备这节课投入了大量精力。

senses.meaning_en: an option giving its holder the right to sell an asset at a specified price
senses.english_definition: A put is a financial contract that gives its holder the right, but not the obligation, to sell an asset at an agreed price within a specified period or on a specified date.
senses.collocation_en: buy a put; a put option
senses.collocation_zh: 买入看跌期权；卖出期权
senses.sentence_en: The investor bought a put to help protect against a fall in the share price.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位投资者买入了一份看跌期权，以帮助防范股价下跌的风险。

etymology_story.zh: put 可追溯到中古英语 putten，早期有放置、推送等意思，更早的来源并不确定。具体的“放到某处”后来扩展为置于某种状态、把思想表达出来以及投入资源；金融名词则指允许持有人按约定条件卖出资产的期权。
etymology_story.en: Put can be traced to Middle English putten, with early meanings involving placing or pushing; its earlier origin is uncertain. Physical placement broadened into placing someone in a situation, expressing an idea, and committing resources, while the financial noun denotes an option allowing its holder to sell an asset on agreed terms.

morphology_enriched.zh: put 是基础词，过去式和过去分词均为 put；第三人称单数为 puts，现在分词为 putting，需双写 t。常见转类与复合形式包括名词 put（看跌期权）、put-down（贬低人的话）、put-on（装模作样；骗局）、put-off（令人反感的事物）和 putaway（入库；收存）；常用短语动词有 put on（穿上；上演）、put off（推迟）、put away（收好）、put out（扑灭；发布）、put up（搭建；张贴）和 put up with（忍受）。
morphology_enriched.en: Put is a base word whose past tense and past participle are both put; its third-person singular is puts, and its present participle is putting, with a doubled t. Common converted or compound forms include the financial noun put, put-down, put-on, put-off, and putaway; common phrasal verbs include put on, put off, put away, put out, put up, and put up with.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: place（放置）比 put 稍正式，常暗示有意识地选择位置；set（放置；安置）常暗示使物体稳当地处于某个位置；lay（平放）通常强调把某物横着或平着放下。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Place is slightly more formal than put and often suggests choosing a position deliberately; set often suggests positioning something securely or in a particular arrangement; lay usually emphasizes placing something flat or horizontally.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“放进去”：把物放进位置，把人置于状态，把想法放进语言，把精力投入事情。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'place into': put an object into a location, a person into a situation, an idea into words, or effort into a task.

senses.meaning_en: an idea, argument, or important detail

senses.chinese_definition: point 指一个人在说话或写作时表达的观点、论点或细节。
senses.collocation_en: make a point; the main point

senses.meaning_en: the purpose or usefulness of something

senses.chinese_definition: 一件事的 point 是做这件事的理由或它能带来的益处。
senses.collocation_en: the point of doing something; there is no point in

senses.english_definition: A point is a small mark, including the dot that separates the whole-number and decimal parts of a number.
senses.chinese_definition: point 指一个小点，也可指将数字的整数部分与小数部分分开的小数点。

senses.meaning_en: the sharp or narrow end of something

senses.chinese_definition: 物体的 point 是它尖锐或细窄的一端。
senses.collocation_en: the point of a knife; a sharp point
senses.collocation_zh: 刀尖；尖锐的尖端
senses.sentence_en: Be careful with the sharp point of that pencil.
senses.sentence_zh: 小心那支铅笔尖锐的笔尖。

senses.meaning_en: a particular place, moment, stage, or degree
senses.english_definition: A point is a particular position in a place, a period of time, or a process.
senses.chinese_definition: point 指空间中的某个位置、时间中的某一刻，或过程中的某个阶段。
senses.collocation_en: a meeting point; at this point
senses.collocation_zh: 集合地点；在这一时刻或阶段
senses.sentence_en: At this point, we need more information before deciding.

senses.meaning_zh: 分；计分单位；数值变化单位
senses.meaning_en: a unit used in scoring or measuring numerical changes
senses.english_definition: A point is a unit used to express a score or a change on a numerical scale.
senses.chinese_definition: point 是表示得分或某种数值尺度上变化幅度的单位。
senses.collocation_en: score points; percentage points
senses.collocation_zh: 得分；百分点

senses.sentence_zh: 我们队以三分的优势获胜。

senses.meaning_en: to indicate a direction or position with a finger or object
senses.english_definition: If you point at something, you show where it is by directing your finger or an object towards it.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果你 point at 某物，就是用手指或其他物体朝向它，指出它的位置。
senses.collocation_en: point at something; point to something
senses.collocation_zh: 指着某物；指向某物
senses.sentence_en: She pointed to an empty seat beside the window.
senses.sentence_zh: 她指了指窗边的一个空座位。

senses.meaning_en: to aim or turn something in a particular direction
senses.english_definition: If you point something in a direction, you turn it so that its front or end faces that way.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果你将某物 point 朝某个方向，就是转动它，使其前部或一端朝向那里。
senses.collocation_en: point a camera at; point in the right direction

senses.meaning_en: to indicate a conclusion or draw attention to a fact
senses.english_definition: If evidence points to something, it suggests that it is true; if you point something out, you draw attention to it.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果证据 point to 某事，就表示它暗示该事属实；如果你 point something out，就是提醒别人注意某件事。

etymology_story.zh: point 的名词源头包括古法语 point 和 pointe，可追溯至拉丁语 punctum 和 puncta，与 pungere“刺、戳”有关，早期意象是刺出的点或尖端。这个意象后来扩展为位置、论述中的要点和计分单位，相关动词则发展出“指向、表明”等意义。
etymology_story.en: The noun point comes through Old French point and pointe from Latin punctum and puncta, related to pungere, meaning 'to prick'; its early imagery involved a pricked mark or a sharp tip. These meanings expanded to positions, points in an argument, and scoring units, while the related verb developed meanings such as directing and indicating.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：point 是不可再按常用词缀拆分的自由词根，名词与动词同形；屈折形式为 points、pointed、pointing。主要词族：pointer（指示物、指针、提示）、pointed（尖的；尖锐明确的）、pointedly（直截了当地）、pointedness（尖锐；明确）、pointy（尖的）、pointless（无意义的，point + -less）、pointlessly（无意义地）、pointlessness（无意义）、point-scoring（争取得分；为压倒对方而争辩）；常见复合词有 pinpoint（精确指出；精确位置）、viewpoint（观点）、standpoint（立场）、endpoint（终点）、midpoint（中点）、checkpoint（检查站）、turning point（转折点）和 point of view（看法）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: point is a free base with no useful everyday prefix–root–suffix division, and the noun and verb share the same form; its inflections are points, pointed, and pointing. The main family includes pointer (an indicator, cursor, or helpful suggestion), pointed (sharp or deliberately direct), pointedly (in a deliberately direct way), pointedness (sharpness or directness), pointy (having a sharp tip), pointless (point + -less, without purpose), pointlessly, pointlessness, and point-scoring (gaining points or arguing to gain an advantage). Common compounds include pinpoint, viewpoint, standpoint, endpoint, midpoint, checkpoint, turning point, and point of view.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: indicate（表明）较正式，可表示用证据、符号或动作传达信息；point（指向）突出方向或具体目标。aim（瞄准、对准）更强调有意朝向目标。argument（论点）通常包含支持某种主张的理由，而名词 point 可以只是一个观点或细节。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Indicate is more formal and can involve evidence, signs, or gestures, whereas point emphasizes direction or a specific target. Aim stresses deliberately directing something towards a target. An argument usually includes reasons supporting a claim, while a point may be just one idea or detail.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“尖端锁定一个点”：手指指向点，讨论抓住要点，比赛逐点得分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a tip picking out one point: a finger points, a discussion has a main point, and a game awards points.

senses.meaning_en: to begin or cause something to begin
senses.english_definition: If you start something, or if it starts, you begin doing it or it begins to happen.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果你 start 某事，就是开始做它；如果某事 starts，就是它开始发生。
senses.collocation_en: start work; start doing something
senses.collocation_zh: 开始工作；开始做某事
senses.sentence_en: We started preparing dinner at six.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们六点开始准备晚饭。

senses.meaning_en: to make a machine operate or begin operating
senses.english_definition: If you start a machine, you make it operate; if it starts, it begins to operate.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果你 start 一台机器，就是使它运转；如果机器 starts，就是它开始运转。
senses.collocation_en: start the engine; start the car
senses.collocation_zh: 启动发动机；发动汽车
senses.sentence_en: The car would not start this morning.
senses.sentence_zh: 今天早上汽车怎么也发动不起来。

senses.meaning_en: to establish a business, organization, or activity
senses.english_definition: If you start a business or organization, you create it and arrange for it to operate.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果你 start 一家企业或一个组织，就是创办它并安排其运作。
senses.collocation_en: start a business; start a family
senses.collocation_zh: 创业、创办企业；开始生儿育女
senses.sentence_en: She started a small business selling handmade bags.
senses.sentence_zh: 她创办了一家销售手工包的小企业。

senses.meaning_en: to make a sudden movement because of surprise or fear
senses.english_definition: If you start, you move suddenly because something surprises or frightens you.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果你 start，就是因为惊讶或害怕而突然动了一下。
senses.collocation_en: start at a noise; start in surprise
senses.collocation_zh: 听到声响猛地一惊；惊得突然一动
senses.sentence_en: He started when the phone rang beside him.
senses.sentence_zh: 身旁的电话响起时，他猛地一惊。

senses.meaning_en: the beginning of an event, activity, or period
senses.english_definition: The start of something is the time or place at which it begins.
senses.chinese_definition: 某事物的 start 是它开始的时间或地点。

senses.collocation_zh: 在……开始时；新的开始
senses.sentence_en: We met at the start of the course.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们在课程开始时认识了。

senses.meaning_zh: 起步优势；提前出发的优势
senses.meaning_en: an advantage gained by beginning earlier or from a better position
senses.english_definition: A start is an advantage you have because you begin earlier or in a better position than someone else.
senses.chinese_definition: start 可以指因比别人更早开始或起始位置更有利而获得的优势。
senses.collocation_en: a head start; a good start in life
senses.collocation_zh: 领先优势；良好的人生起点
senses.sentence_en: Reading at home gives children a head start at school.
senses.sentence_zh: 在家阅读能让孩子在学校学习中获得起步优势。

senses.meaning_en: a sudden movement caused by surprise or fear
senses.english_definition: A start is a quick, sudden movement you make when you are surprised or frightened.
senses.chinese_definition: start 指人在惊讶或害怕时突然作出的快速动作。

etymology_story.zh: start 源自古英语 styrtan，原意是“跳起、猛冲”，最初强调突然的动作。词义后来从“猛地动起来”扩展为“使运转、开始”，而“惊得一动”的旧义仍保留在动词及 with a start 等表达中。
etymology_story.en: Start comes from Old English styrtan, meaning 'to leap up or rush', originally emphasizing sudden movement. The meaning broadened from springing into motion to setting something going or beginning, while the older sense survives in the verb and expressions such as with a start.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：start 是独立词根，名词与动词同形；屈折形式为 starts、started、starting。主要词族：starter（启动装置；初学者；开胃菜）、starting（开始的；起始的）、restart（重新开始，re- + start）、nonstarter／non-starter（无望成功的人或事）、startup／start-up（初创企业；启动）、jump-start（借外接电源启动；推动开展）、kick-start（用脚踏启动；促使开始）、upstart（骤然得势者，常含贬义）、self-starter（主动做事的人）；常见组合有 starting point（起点）、starting line（起跑线）和 false start（抢跑；失败的开端）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: start is an independent base used as both noun and verb; its inflections are starts, started, and starting. The main family includes starter (a starting device, beginner, or first course), starting (initial), restart (re- + start, begin again), nonstarter/non-starter (someone or something with no prospect of success), startup/start-up (a new business or the process of starting), jump-start (start with an external battery or stimulate progress), kick-start (start with a kick mechanism or get something going), upstart (a newly successful person regarded as presumptuous), and self-starter (someone who acts without prompting). Common combinations include starting point, starting line, and false start.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: begin（开始）与 start 常可互换，但通常不用来表示发动汽车或机器；commence（开始）更正式，常见于公告和正式程序；launch（发起、推出）强调有计划地启动项目、产品或活动。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Begin often overlaps with start, but it is not normally used for switching a car or machine into operation. Commence is more formal and common in announcements or official procedures. Launch emphasizes deliberately introducing a project, product, or activity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“猛地动起来”记住 start：人一惊、机器发动、事情开始，都从静止进入动作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the original burst into motion: a person jumps, an engine starts, and an activity begins.

senses.meaning_zh: 学校；上学；学校教育；全校师生
senses.meaning_en: an educational institution, its community, or the education it provides
senses.english_definition: A school is a place where people, especially children, are taught; school can also mean attending lessons or the people belonging to that institution.
senses.chinese_definition: school 指人们尤其是儿童接受教学的学校，也可指上学这件事或该校的师生。

senses.meaning_zh: 专业学校；大学中的学院
senses.meaning_en: an institution or university division teaching a particular subject
senses.english_definition: A school is an institution or part of a university where people study a particular subject or profession.

senses.collocation_en: medical school; business school

senses.meaning_en: a group sharing particular ideas, methods, or artistic styles
senses.english_definition: A school is a group of thinkers or artists whose ideas, methods, or styles are similar.
senses.chinese_definition: school 可以指思想、方法或风格相近的一群思想家或艺术家所形成的学派或流派。
senses.collocation_en: a school of thought; the Impressionist school

senses.sentence_en: There are two main schools of thought on this issue.

senses.meaning_zh: 鱼群；成群游动的水生动物
senses.meaning_en: a group of fish or certain other aquatic animals moving together
senses.english_definition: A school of fish is a group of fish swimming together.
senses.chinese_definition: a school of fish 指一起游动的一群鱼。
senses.collocation_en: a school of fish; a school of dolphins
senses.collocation_zh: 一群鱼；一群海豚
senses.sentence_en: A school of fish swam beneath the boat.

senses.english_definition: If you school someone in something, you teach or train them to understand it or do it well.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果你 school someone in something，就是教导或训练某人，使其理解或掌握某方面的知识、技能或行为方式。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“学校”的 school 经拉丁语 schola 追溯至希腊语 skholē，原指“闲暇”，后来指用于讨论、学习的闲暇活动，再发展为教学和学校。表示“鱼群”的 school 是另一个来源不同的词，来自中古荷兰语 schole“群体”，与 shoal“鱼群”同源。
etymology_story.en: School meaning an educational institution ultimately comes through Latin schola from Greek skholē, originally 'leisure', then leisure devoted to discussion and learning, and eventually teaching and its setting. School meaning a group of fish has a separate origin in Middle Dutch schole, 'a group', and is related to shoal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：school 是不可按常用词缀继续拆分的词根，教育义名词可零派生为动词；鱼群义属于另一个同形词。屈折形式为 schools、schooled、schooling。主要词族：schooling（学校教育；训练；鱼类聚群）、schooled（受过教育或训练的）、unschooled（未受正规教育的）、preschool（学前教育；学前的）、preschooler（学龄前儿童）、homeschool／home-school（在家教育）、homeschooling（在家教育）、homeschooler（在家受教育者或实施在家教育者）；常见复合词有 schoolchild／schoolchildren（学童）、schoolboy（男学生）、schoolgirl（女学生）、schoolteacher（学校教师）、schoolmate（同学）、schoolwork（学校作业）、schoolbook（课本）、schoolhouse（校舍）、schoolroom（教室）、school-leaver（离校生）、schoolmaster／schoolmistress（男／女教师或校长，较传统用法）和 old-school（传统派的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: school is a base with no useful everyday affix division, and the education noun also functions as a verb through conversion; the fish-group meaning belongs to a separate homonym. Inflections are schools, schooled, and schooling. The main family includes schooling (education, training, or fish grouping), schooled (educated or trained), unschooled (without formal education), preschool (education before ordinary school, or relating to it), preschooler (a child below school age), homeschool/home-school (educate at home), homeschooling, and homeschooler (a home-educated learner or someone providing home education). Common compounds include schoolchild/schoolchildren, schoolboy, schoolgirl, schoolteacher, schoolmate, schoolwork, schoolbook, schoolhouse, schoolroom, school-leaver, schoolmaster/schoolmistress (traditional terms for teachers or school heads), and old-school (traditional in outlook or style).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: academy（专门学校、学院）常强调特定领域的培养，也可属于特定教育制度中的校名；educate（教育）强调知识、能力和人格的整体培养，而动词 school 常突出某方面的训练；shoal（鱼群）与鱼群义 school 常可互换，但较严格的区分中 school 更强调协调一致的游动。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Academy often suggests specialized instruction, though it can also name a school within a particular education system. Educate emphasizes developing knowledge, abilities, and character broadly, while the verb school often highlights particular training. Shoal often overlaps with the fish-group noun school, although stricter usage associates school with coordinated swimming.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 教育义串成“学校教人，训练成派”；鱼群义另记“一群鱼一起游”，它与学校义来源不同。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the education senses as 'a school teaches, training shapes a school of thought'; remember the separate fish word as 'a group swimming together'.

senses.meaning_en: every individual member of a group, considered separately
senses.english_definition: You use each before a singular noun to refer to every person or thing in a group separately.
senses.chinese_definition: each 放在单数名词前，表示分别看待一个群体中的每个人或每件事物。
senses.collocation_en: each student; each time
senses.collocation_zh: 每个学生；每次
senses.sentence_en: Each student received a copy of the book.
senses.sentence_zh: 每个学生都领到了一本这本书。

senses.meaning_en: every person or thing in a group individually
senses.english_definition: You use each on its own to refer separately to all the people or things in a group.
senses.chinese_definition: each 单独使用时，分别指代一个群体中的所有人或事物。
senses.collocation_en: each of us; each of them
senses.collocation_zh: 我们每个人；他们中的每一个
senses.sentence_en: Each of the rooms has a private bathroom.
senses.sentence_zh: 每个房间都有独立浴室。

senses.meaning_en: for or to every individual person or thing
senses.english_definition: You use each after an amount to say that the amount applies to every person or thing separately.
senses.chinese_definition: each 放在数量或金额后，表示这一数量或金额分别适用于每个人或每件物品。
senses.collocation_en: five pounds each; two tickets each
senses.collocation_zh: 每个五英镑；每人两张票
senses.sentence_en: The notebooks cost three pounds each.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些笔记本每本三英镑。

etymology_story.zh: each 源自古英语 ælc，其较早的构成与表示“总是”的 ā 和表示“相同、一样”的 ġelīc 有关。它逐渐固定为逐一指称群体成员的词，核心始终是“每一个都分别算”。
etymology_story.en: Each comes from Old English ælc, whose earlier formation is associated with ā, meaning 'ever', and ġelīc, meaning 'alike'. It became the regular word for considering the members of a group individually, preserving the idea that every single one counts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：each 是不可再分析的功能词，没有现代英语中可用的“词根＋词缀”拆分，也没有复数、比较级或常用派生词。主要语法组合：each + 单数名词（每个……）、each of + 复数名词或代词（……中的每一个）、each other（互相）、each and every（每一个，强调无一例外）；each time（每次）和 each day（每天）是短语，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: each is an unanalyzable function word, with no productive root-plus-affix breakdown, plural, comparative, or common derivational family. Its main constructions are each + singular noun, each of + plural noun phrase or pronoun, each other (reciprocally), and each and every (emphasizing that there are no exceptions). Each time and each day are phrases rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: every（每个）更常把全部成员作为一个整体来概括，通常用于三个或以上成员，而 each 突出逐个看待，也可用于两个成员；all（所有）强调总量，常接复数名词或不可数名词；apiece（每个、每人）接近表示分配数量的副词 each，但不能代替名词前的限定词 each。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Every more often generalizes about the whole group and normally concerns three or more members, while each emphasizes individuals and can refer to just two. All stresses the total and commonly accompanies plural or uncountable nouns. Apiece resembles each when distributing amounts, but cannot replace each as a determiner before a noun.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把一组成员逐个点名：each 就是“一个一个，每个都算”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture counting a group one member at a time: each means every individual counts separately.

senses.meaning_en: to begin to be something or enter a new state
senses.english_definition: If someone or something becomes a particular thing or becomes a particular way, they change and begin to be that thing or have that quality.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果某人或某物 become 某种身份或状态，就是经过变化后开始具有该身份或特征。
senses.collocation_en: become a teacher; become clear
senses.collocation_zh: 成为教师；变得清楚
senses.sentence_en: The problem became clear after we checked the figures.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们核对数字后，问题就清楚了。

senses.meaning_en: to suit someone or be appropriate to their appearance or character
senses.english_definition: If something becomes someone, it makes them look attractive or is appropriate to their character or position.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果某物或某种行为 become 某人，就是它使这个人显得好看，或与其品格、身份相称。
senses.collocation_en: a color that becomes someone; conduct that becomes someone
senses.collocation_zh: 衬托某人气色的颜色；与某人身份相称的行为
senses.sentence_en: Such rude behavior does not become you.
senses.sentence_zh: 这样粗鲁的行为与你的身份不相称。

etymology_story.zh: become 源自古英语 becuman，由前缀 be- 与 cuman“来”构成，早期有“来到、到达、发生”等意义，后来发展为“进入某种状态、成为”。其“适合、相称”的意义则由“合宜、适当”的语义支线发展而来。
etymology_story.en: Become comes from Old English becuman, formed from the prefix be- and cuman, 'to come', with early meanings including arriving and happening; it later developed the sense of entering a state or turning into something. Its meaning 'to suit' arose through a related sense of being fitting or appropriate.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：可辨认为 be- + come，但 become 是意义已固定的整体动词，不能把 be- 简单解释为独立动词 be“是”。不规则变化：become—became—become；其他形式为 becomes、becoming。主要派生词：becoming（合适的；好看的）、unbecoming（不得体的；不相称的，un- + becoming）、becomingly（得体地）、unbecomingly（不得体地）；名词 becoming 表示“形成、生成的过程”，主要见于哲学或较抽象的语境。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: be- + come remains recognizable, but become is a lexicalized verb, and its prefix should not simply be interpreted as the independent verb be. Its irregular forms are become—became—become, with becomes and becoming as the other inflections. The main derivatives are becoming (suitable or attractive), unbecoming (un- + becoming, inappropriate or unworthy), becomingly (appropriately), and unbecomingly (inappropriately). The noun becoming refers to the process of coming into being, mainly in philosophy or other abstract contexts.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: get（变得）通常更口语化，常接形容词，如 get tired；turn（变成）常突出明显变化，尤其是颜色或状态变化；suit（适合、使好看）对应 become 的正式及物义，日常表达中更常用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Get is generally more conversational and often introduces adjectives, as in get tired. Turn often highlights a noticeable change, especially in color or condition. Suit corresponds to the formal transitive meaning of become and is more usual in everyday speech.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 come“来到”连接到新状态：来到某种状态，就是“变得、成为”；进入合适状态，则联系“相称、适合”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect come with arriving at a new state: arriving there means becoming something; arriving at a fitting state helps recall the sense 'to suit'.

senses.meaning_en: curiosity or attention
senses.english_definition: If you have an interest in something, you want to learn about it or give it your attention.
senses.collocation_en: show an interest in; take an interest in
senses.collocation_zh: 对……表现出兴趣；开始关注……
senses.sentence_en: She showed an interest in astronomy at an early age.
senses.sentence_zh: 她很小就对天文学表现出了兴趣。

senses.meaning_zh: 爱好；感兴趣的活动或领域
senses.meaning_en: an activity or subject that someone enjoys
senses.english_definition: Your interests are the activities and subjects that you enjoy spending time on.
senses.collocation_en: a wide range of interests; shared interests
senses.collocation_zh: 广泛的爱好；共同的兴趣爱好
senses.sentence_en: His interests include cooking, photography, and cycling.
senses.sentence_zh: 他的爱好包括烹饪、摄影和骑自行车。

senses.meaning_en: money paid for borrowing money or earned on savings
senses.english_definition: Interest is extra money that you pay when you borrow money or receive when you keep money in certain accounts.
senses.collocation_en: pay interest; earn interest
senses.collocation_zh: 支付利息；获得利息
senses.sentence_en: You will pay less interest if you repay the loan early.
senses.sentence_zh: 如果提前还清贷款，你支付的利息就会减少。

senses.meaning_en: a financial share or personal involvement
senses.english_definition: If you have an interest in a business or situation, you own part of it or have something to gain or lose from it.
senses.collocation_en: a controlling interest; a vested interest
senses.collocation_zh: 控股权；既得利益或切身利益
senses.sentence_en: The family owns a controlling interest in the company.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个家族拥有该公司的控股权。

senses.meaning_en: someone's benefit or well-being
senses.english_definition: Something that is in your interests helps you or protects what matters to you.
senses.collocation_en: in someone's best interests; protect someone's interests
senses.collocation_zh: 最符合某人的利益；保护某人的利益
senses.sentence_en: The decision was made in the children's best interests.
senses.sentence_zh: 作出这一决定是为了最大限度地保障孩子们的利益。

senses.meaning_en: to attract someone's curiosity or attention
senses.english_definition: If something interests you, it makes you want to know more about it or pay attention to it.
senses.collocation_en: particularly interest someone; interest someone in something
senses.collocation_zh: 使某人格外感兴趣；使某人对某事产生兴趣
senses.sentence_en: The course interested her in environmental science.
senses.sentence_zh: 这门课程使她对环境科学产生了兴趣。

etymology_story.zh: interest 经中古英语和盎格鲁法语形式传入，最终源自拉丁语 inter esse，字面意为“处于……之间”，并引申为“有关系、有重要性”。英语早期涉及法律上的权益和损失补偿，后来发展出“金钱收益”和“引起关注的事物”等意义。
etymology_story.en: Interest entered through Middle English and Anglo-French forms, ultimately from Latin inter esse, literally 'to be between' and, by extension, 'to concern or matter'. Early English uses involved legal rights and compensation for loss; later meanings included financial returns and things that attract attention.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 interest 通常视为不可再拆的词基，不能按现代前后缀机械切分；名词与动词同形。主要词族：interests（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、interested（感兴趣的；动词过去式及过去分词）、interesting（有趣的；现在分词）、interestingly（有趣地；有意思的是）、uninteresting（无趣的）、uninterested（不感兴趣的）、disinterest（无兴趣；不偏私）、disinterested（公正无私的；也可指不感兴趣的）、disinterestedly（公正无私地）、disinterestedness（公正无私）；常见复合词有 interest-free（免息的）和 interest-bearing（计息的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, interest is normally treated as an indivisible base, with the same form used as a noun and verb. Main family: interests; interested, the past tense and past participle and an adjective meaning engaged; interesting, the present participle and an adjective meaning engaging; interestingly; uninteresting; uninterested; disinterest, meaning lack of interest or impartiality; disinterested, meaning impartial and also sometimes uninterested; disinterestedly; and disinterestedness. Common compounds include interest-free and interest-bearing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: curiosity（好奇心）强调想知道未知事物；attention（注意力、关注）强调把心思集中于某事，不一定喜欢它；stake（权益、利害关系）对应 interest 的利益义，强调个人在结果中的得失。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Curiosity emphasizes wanting to discover something unknown; attention emphasizes mental focus without necessarily implying enjoyment; stake matches the involvement sense of interest and emphasizes what someone stands to gain or lose.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 与你“有关系”的事会引起兴趣；与你的钱“有关系”的份额和收益就是权益、利息。
mnemonic_anchor.en: What concerns you attracts your interest; what concerns your money becomes a financial interest or interest earned.
