senses.meaning_zh: 重要的；有重大影响的；很有价值的
senses.meaning_en: having great significance, value, or influence
senses.english_definition: Something that is important matters greatly because it has a strong effect or is valuable to someone.
senses.collocation_en: an important decision; play an important role
senses.collocation_zh: 一项重要决定；发挥重要作用
senses.sentence_en: Sleep plays an important role in learning.
senses.sentence_zh: 睡眠在学习中起着重要作用。

senses.meaning_zh: 有地位的；有权势的；有影响力的
senses.meaning_en: having high status, power, or influence
senses.english_definition: An important person has a high position or considerable power or influence.
senses.collocation_en: an important person; an important official
senses.collocation_zh: 一位要人；一位重要官员
senses.sentence_en: Several important officials attended the meeting.
senses.sentence_zh: 几位重要官员出席了会议。

etymology_story.zh: important 经法语 important 进入英语，追溯到拉丁语 importare，原义为“带入、运入”，后来也表示“具有意义、关系重大”。语义由“带来某种分量或影响”发展为现代的“重要的”。
etymology_story.en: Important entered English through French important and ultimately goes back to Latin importare, originally 'to bring in' and later also 'to signify or matter.' The meaning developed toward having significance, weight, or consequence.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习中以 important 为形容词词基，不应把 im- 当作表示否定的前缀；其中的 im- 历史上来自表示“向内”的 in-，port 与“携带”有关。常用词族：importance（重要性）、importantly（重要地；用于补充重要信息）、unimportant（不重要的）、self-important（自命不凡的）、self-importance（自命不凡）；比较级和最高级为 more important、most important。importance 与 important 存在 -ant／-ance 的形式对应。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, treat important as an adjective base; its initial im- is not the negative prefix. Historically, im- represents in-, 'inward,' and port relates to carrying. Common family members are importance, importantly, unimportant, self-important, and self-importance; the comparative and superlative are more important and most important. Important and importance show the corresponding endings -ant and -ance.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: significant（有重大意义的）强调值得注意的影响或含义；essential（必不可少的）强调缺少便无法正常进行；crucial（至关重要的）强调对结果成败具有决定性作用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Significant emphasizes a noteworthy effect or meaning; essential means necessary for something to function or happen; crucial emphasizes a decisive effect on success or the final outcome.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“重要”理解为“有分量”：能给结果带来明显影响，就 important；开头 im- 不是“不”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of importance as carrying weight: something important makes a real difference. The opening im- does not mean 'not.'

senses.meaning_en: on every occasion
senses.english_definition: If something always happens, it happens every time or whenever the relevant situation occurs.
senses.collocation_en: always arrive early; always remember
senses.collocation_zh: 总是早到；每次都记得
senses.sentence_en: She always checks the door before leaving.
senses.sentence_zh: 她每次离开前都会检查门是否关好。

senses.meaning_en: throughout a period or for all future time
senses.english_definition: If something has always been true or will always be true, it continues throughout the time being considered.
senses.collocation_en: have always known; will always remember
senses.collocation_zh: 一直都知道；将永远记得
senses.sentence_en: I will always remember your kindness.
senses.sentence_zh: 我会永远记得你的善意。

senses.meaning_zh: 老是；不断地，常带抱怨或其他情绪
senses.meaning_en: very frequently, often with emotional emphasis
senses.english_definition: If you say someone is always doing something, you mean they do it very often, sometimes in a way that annoys you.
senses.collocation_en: always complaining; always losing things
senses.collocation_zh: 老是抱怨；老是丢东西
senses.sentence_en: You're always leaving your shoes in the doorway.
senses.sentence_zh: 你老是把鞋子放在门口。

senses.meaning_zh: 总还可以；至少可以，表示一个可用的备选办法
senses.meaning_en: as an available alternative if needed
senses.english_definition: You use always with can or could to suggest an option that remains available if it is needed.
senses.collocation_en: can always ask; could always try
senses.collocation_zh: 总还可以问问；还可以试试
senses.sentence_en: If the bus doesn't come, we can always take a taxi.
senses.sentence_zh: 如果公交车不来，我们总还可以打车。

etymology_story.zh: always 源于古英语短语 ealne weg，字面意思是“整条路、一路上”，后来发展为“在所有时间”。词尾 -s 是后来形成的副词性结尾，并不是现代名词复数的意思。
etymology_story.en: Always developed from Old English ealne weg, literally 'all the way,' which came to mean 'at all times.' The final -s developed as an adverbial ending rather than carrying the meaning of a modern noun plural.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 always 是固定副词，不再按能产的词根加词缀结构使用；历史记忆上可联系 all + way + 副词性 -s。它没有常用的屈折变化或直接派生词；all、way 和 ways 是帮助理解历史结构的相关形式，不是由 always 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, always is a fixed adverb rather than a productive root-and-affix formation; historically, it can be associated with all + way + adverbial -s. It has no common inflections or direct derivatives. All, way, and ways help explain its historical structure but are not derivatives of always.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: invariably（无一例外地）较正式，强调每次结果都相同；constantly（不断地）强调持续发生或极其频繁；forever（永远）强调无限延续的时间，也可在口语中表示“老是”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Invariably is more formal and stresses an outcome with no exceptions; constantly emphasizes continuous activity or very frequent repetition; forever emphasizes unlimited duration and can also informally mean 'repeatedly.'

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“一路上”想到“全程如此”：每次都如此是“总是”，整个时间都如此是“一直”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from 'all the way' to 'all the time': every occasion gives 'always,' and the whole stretch of time gives 'continually' or 'forever.'

senses.meaning_en: someone you know well, like, and trust
senses.english_definition: A friend is someone you know and like, usually someone you enjoy spending time with and can trust.
senses.collocation_en: a close friend; make friends
senses.collocation_zh: 一位亲密的朋友；交朋友
senses.sentence_en: I've been friends with Maya since school.
senses.sentence_zh: 我从上学时起就和玛雅是朋友。

senses.meaning_zh: 支持者；赞助者；友好的一方
senses.meaning_en: a supporter of a person, organization, or cause
senses.english_definition: A friend of a person, organization, or cause supports them and wants them to succeed.
senses.collocation_en: a friend of the arts; a friend of the family
senses.collocation_zh: 艺术事业的支持者；与某一家人交好的朋友
senses.sentence_en: She has long been a friend of the museum.
senses.sentence_zh: 她长期以来一直支持这家博物馆。

senses.meaning_zh: 社交平台上建立好友关系的用户
senses.meaning_en: someone connected to you as a friend on a social networking service
senses.english_definition: An online friend is someone whose account is connected to yours through a social network's friendship feature.
senses.collocation_en: a Facebook friend; a friend request
senses.collocation_zh: 一位脸书好友；好友请求
senses.sentence_en: Only my friends can see these photos.
senses.sentence_zh: 只有我的好友能看到这些照片。

senses.meaning_zh: 在社交平台上加……为好友
senses.meaning_en: to add someone as a friend on a social networking service
senses.english_definition: If you friend someone online, you add them to your list of friends on a social networking service.
senses.collocation_en: friend someone on Facebook; friend a classmate
senses.collocation_zh: 在脸书上加某人为好友；加一位同学为好友
senses.sentence_en: She friended me after we met at the workshop.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们在研讨活动中认识后，她加了我为好友。

etymology_story.zh: friend 来自古英语 frēond，原本是 frēogan“爱、喜爱”的现在分词，字面意思是“喜爱他人的人”。它后来固定为表示“朋友”的名词，现代又常转作动词，表示在社交平台上“加为好友”。
etymology_story.en: Friend comes from Old English frēond, originally the present participle of frēogan, 'to love or show affection,' literally someone who loves. It became established as the noun for a friend and is now also commonly used as a verb for adding a social-network connection.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 friend 是基本词，名词转作动词时不增加词缀。常用词族：friends（复数或第三人称单数）、friended（加为好友的过去式及过去分词）、friending（加好友）、friendship（友谊）、friendly（友好的，通常为形容词）、friendliness（友好）、friendlier／friendliest（更友好的／最友好的）、unfriendly（不友好的）、unfriendliness（不友好）、friendless（没有朋友的）、friendlessness（没有朋友的状态）、befriend（与……交朋友；友善帮助）、befriended／befriending（befriend 的变化形式）、unfriend（解除好友关系）、unfriended／unfriending（unfriend 的变化形式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Friend is a basic modern word, and its noun becomes a verb without an added affix. Common family members are friends, friended, friending, friendship, friendly, friendliness, friendlier/friendliest, unfriendly, unfriendliness, friendless, friendlessness, befriend, befriended/befriending, unfriend, and unfriended/unfriending. Friendly is normally an adjective despite its -ly ending.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: companion（同伴）强调陪伴或共同活动，不一定有深厚感情；acquaintance（熟人）指认识但关系通常不亲密的人；ally（盟友、支持者）强调共同目标和相互支持，不一定存在私人友谊。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Companion emphasizes spending time or doing activities together without necessarily implying emotional closeness; acquaintance means someone you know but usually not closely; ally emphasizes shared goals and support rather than personal friendship.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史核心是“喜爱你的人”：现实中是朋友，支持你时是友好的一方，网络上建立连接就是加好友。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the historical idea 'someone who cares for you': a personal friend, a supportive friend of a cause, or someone you friend online.

senses.meaning_en: nevertheless; despite what has just been said
senses.english_definition: You use however to introduce a fact or opinion that contrasts with what you have just said.
senses.collocation_en: however, this does not mean; it is, however, possible
senses.collocation_zh: 不过，这并不意味着；然而，这是可能的
senses.sentence_en: The journey was long. However, the views made it worthwhile.
senses.sentence_zh: 旅途很漫长。不过，沿途的景色让这一切都值得。

senses.meaning_zh: 无论多么；不管多大程度
senses.meaning_en: no matter how; to whatever degree
senses.english_definition: You use however before an adjective or adverb to say that its degree does not change the situation you are describing.
senses.collocation_en: however difficult; however hard you try
senses.collocation_zh: 无论多么困难；无论你多么努力
senses.sentence_en: However busy she is, she always calls her parents on Sunday.
senses.sentence_zh: 无论多忙，她总会在星期天给父母打电话。

senses.meaning_zh: 无论用什么方式；以任何方式
senses.meaning_en: in whatever way; regardless of how
senses.english_definition: If you can do something however you like, you can do it in any way you choose.
senses.collocation_en: however you like; however you choose
senses.collocation_zh: 以你喜欢的任何方式；以你选择的任何方式
senses.sentence_en: You can arrange the furniture however you like.
senses.sentence_zh: 你可以按照自己喜欢的任何方式摆放家具。

etymology_story.zh: however 由 how（如何）与 ever（曾经；在任何时候）在中古英语时期组合而成，早期表达“无论如何、无论以何种方式”。表示方式或程度不受限制的意义，后来发展出“尽管如此、然而”的转折用法。
etymology_story.en: However developed in Middle English from how and ever, initially expressing an unrestricted manner or degree: 'in whatever way' or 'no matter how.' This concessive meaning later developed into the contrasting use meaning 'nevertheless.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：how + ever → however，属于复合词，整体不发生屈折变化。直接构词成分为 how、ever；平行构式有 whatever、whoever、wherever、whenever，均利用 ever 表示“不论……”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: how + ever → however, an uninflected compound. Its immediate components are how and ever; parallel formations include whatever, whoever, wherever, and whenever, which also use ever to express unrestricted choice or circumstances.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nevertheless（尽管如此）更突出前述情况未能阻止后述结果；but（但是）是直接连接对立成分的并列连词，而表示转折的 however 通常是连接副词；no matter how（无论多么）对应 however 表示程度让步的用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nevertheless emphasizes that the preceding circumstance does not prevent the following result; but is a coordinating conjunction directly linking contrasting elements, whereas contrastive however is normally a linking adverb; no matter how matches however when it introduces a concession about degree.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: how + ever：不管“怎么”都成立 → 无论如何；承接上文时 → 尽管如此，然而。
mnemonic_anchor.en: How + ever: whatever the 'how,' the statement still holds → no matter how → nevertheless.

senses.meaning_en: put something in a particular position
senses.english_definition: If you set something somewhere, you put it there carefully or deliberately.
senses.collocation_en: set something down; set something aside
senses.collocation_zh: 放下某物；把某物放到一边
senses.sentence_en: She set the box gently on the floor.
senses.sentence_zh: 她把盒子轻轻地放在地板上。

senses.meaning_en: adjust a device or control to a chosen value
senses.english_definition: If you set a device, you adjust it so that it works at a particular time, temperature, or level.
senses.collocation_en: set an alarm; set the temperature

etymology_story.zh: 动词 set 来自古英语 settan，基本意思是“使坐下、放到某处”，与 sit 同源，后来扩展为使事物处于某个位置、状态或标准。现代名词义并非全出自同一路径，其中“组、套”的发展也受到古法语 sette 等相关形式的影响。
etymology_story.en: The verb set comes from Old English settan, meaning 'cause to sit' or 'put in place,' and is historically related to sit; it expanded to putting things into particular states or establishing standards. The modern noun has more than one historical strand, with its grouping meanings also influenced by Old French forms such as sette.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：set 是不可再作常规词缀切分的基本词；动词变化为 set–set–set，第三人称单数 sets，现在分词 setting。常见派生与词族包括 setter（设置者；塞特猎犬）、setting（设置；环境；背景；镶托）、reset（重置）、preset（预设）、unset（取消设置；未凝固的）；常见复合词包括 setup／set-up（安排；配置）、setback（挫折）、setoff／set-off（抵消；衬托）、setpoint（设定值）、typeset（排版）、typesetter（排字工；排版设备）、mindset（思维模式）、sunset（日落）和 subset（子集）。set 的主要词形完全同音，多词性转换通常不改变读音。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: set is a base word without a regular internal affix division. Its verb forms are set–set–set, with sets and setting. Common derivatives and family members include setter, setting, reset, preset, and unset; common compounds include setup/set-up, setback, setoff/set-off, setpoint, typeset, typesetter, mindset, sunset, and subset. The principal forms of set used as a verb, noun, and adjective have the same pronunciation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: put（放）是最宽泛的放置动词，set 常突出有意识地摆好或使处于某状态；establish（确立）对应 set 制定规则、标准等的用法，但更正式；collection（收藏；集合）强调汇集的事物，而名词 set 更常暗示成员相关、配套或构成完整单位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Put is the broadest placement verb, while set often suggests deliberate positioning or bringing something into a state; establish matches the rule- or standard-making sense of set but is more formal; collection emphasizes things brought together, while the noun set often implies related members, matching items, or a complete unit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心画面：把东西“放到位”。位置到位＝放置，数值到位＝设定，规则到位＝确立，材料状态到位＝凝固；另记名词 set＝配成一组。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture putting something 'in place': an object is placed, a value is selected, a rule is established, and a material becomes firm. Separately anchor the noun set as things grouped together.

etymology_story.zh: hand 来自古英语 hand／hond，属于日耳曼语继承词，最初指身体部位“手”。由于手用于劳动、给予和掌控，它逐渐产生“工人、帮助、控制、递交”等引申义，钟表指针也因形状和指示作用而被称为 hands。
etymology_story.en: Hand comes from Old English hand/hond, an inherited Germanic word for the body part. Because hands perform work, give things, and exercise control, the word developed meanings involving workers, assistance, possession, and passing things; clock pointers also became hands through their shape and pointing function.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：hand 为基本词，名词复数 hands；名词直接转为动词 hand，变化为 hands、handed、handing。常见派生词包括 handy（方便的；手巧的）、handily（轻松地；方便地）、handiness（方便；灵巧）、handful（一把；少数；难管的人）、handedness（用手偏好）；常见复合词包括 handbag（手提包）、handbook（手册）、handwriting（笔迹）、handwritten（手写的）、handmade（手工制作的）、handshake（握手）、handout（讲义；救济品）、handover（移交）、handheld（手持的）、handwork（手工劳动）、handyman（杂务修理工）、second-hand（二手的）、left-handed（左撇子的）、right-handed（右撇子的）和 hands-on（亲身实践的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hand is a base word, with the noun plural hands. Conversion produces the verb hand, inflected as hands, handed, and handing. Common derivatives include handy, handily, handiness, handful, and handedness; common compounds include handbag, handbook, handwriting, handwritten, handmade, handshake, handout, handover, handheld, handwork, handyman, second-hand, left-handed, right-handed, and hands-on.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pass（递）侧重把东西传到另一人或另一位置，hand 更明确地体现交给对方；give（给）范围更广，可表示赠送或抽象给予，而 hand 通常突出交接动作；assistance（协助）对应名词 hand 的“帮助”义，但更正式，hand 多用于 give／lend someone a hand。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pass emphasizes moving something to another person or position, while hand more specifically presents it to a recipient; give is broader and can describe gifts or abstract benefits, while hand usually highlights the act of transfer; assistance matches the help sense of the noun but is more formal, whereas hand commonly appears in give/lend someone a hand.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一只手串起词义：手做事→人手、帮助；手拿着→掌握；手递出→交给；指针像手指→钟表指针。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let the body part connect the meanings: hands work → workers and help; hands hold → control; hands pass things → give; pointers resemble pointing fingers → clock hands.

senses.meaning_en: state or require something in a law, contract, or formal document

senses.collocation_zh: 法律规定；规定赔偿安排

senses.sentence_zh: 合同规定必须在三十天内付款。

etymology_story.zh: provide 源自拉丁语 providēre，由 pro-（向前、预先）与 vidēre（看）组成，原义为“预先看见、预作安排”。“事先考虑需要”的含义后来发展为“备好所需之物、提供、供养”。
etymology_story.en: Provide comes from Latin providēre, formed from pro- ('ahead') and vidēre ('see'), meaning 'foresee' or 'make arrangements in advance.' The idea of anticipating needs developed into preparing supplies, making things available, and supporting others.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：provide 通常作为完整动词词基使用，不宜把 -vide 当作可自由构词的现代英语词根；pro- + vidēre 是历史分析。屈折变化为 provides、provided、providing；直接派生词有 provider（提供者）、近代常用的 provisioning 相关形式并非直接按 provide + 后缀拼成。历史同族包括 provision（供应；条款）、provisions（食品储备）、provisioning（供应配置）、provisional（暂定的）、provisionally（暂时地）、providence（天意；远见）、provident（有远虑的；节俭的）、providently（有远虑地）、improvident（缺乏远虑的）和 improvidence（缺乏远虑）；provided／providing 在 provided/providing that 中还可作条件连词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: provide normally functions as a complete verb base; -vide is not a freely productive modern English root, so pro- + vidēre is a historical analysis. Its inflections are provides, provided, and providing, and a direct derivative is provider. Historical family members include provision, provisions, provisioning, provisional, provisionally, providence, provident, providently, improvident, and improvidence; these are not all formed by simply adding a suffix to the modern spelling provide. Provided and providing also function as conditional conjunctions in provided/providing that.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: supply（供应）常强调持续或成量地满足物资需求；offer（提供；提出）强调让对方可以接受，并不保证对方实际获得或使用；furnish（提供；配备）较正式，常表示提供所需资料或设备。provide 是适用范围很广的中性词，关注使所需之物可用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Supply often emphasizes meeting material needs regularly or in quantity; offer makes something available for acceptance without implying that it is accepted or used; furnish is more formal and often concerns necessary information or equipment. Provide is a broad, neutral word focused on making something needed available.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑：向前看见需求 → 提前备好 → 提供；provide for＝把生活或未来所需安排好。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical logic: see a need ahead → prepare for it → provide; provide for means arrange what someone or a future situation will need.

etymology_story.zh: small 来自古英语 smæl，早期含有“窄、细、纤小”的意思，与其他日耳曼语言中表示狭窄的词同源。它后来成为表示尺寸、数量或程度较小的通用词，并引申出“不重要、使人感到卑微”等意义。
etymology_story.en: Small comes from Old English smæl, which included meanings such as 'narrow,' 'slender,' and 'little,' and is related to Germanic words for narrowness. It became a general word for limited size, quantity, or degree and developed figurative meanings involving insignificance or feeling diminished.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：small 为基本形容词，比较级 smaller，最高级 smallest；可直接转用为副词和名词。直接派生词有 smallness（小；微小程度）和 smallish（有点小的）；常见复合词有 small-scale（小规模的）、small-minded（心胸狭窄的）、small-mindedness（心胸狭窄）、smallholder（小农场主）、smallholding（小农场）和 smallpox（天花）；常见固定搭配有 small talk（闲聊）、small print（小号字条款）和 small business（小企业）。名词 smalls 在英式非正式用法中可指内衣。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: small is a base adjective, with the comparative smaller and superlative smallest; it also functions as an adverb and noun through conversion. Direct derivatives include smallness and smallish. Common compounds include small-scale, small-minded, small-mindedness, smallholder, smallholding, and smallpox; established phrases include small talk, small print, and small business. In informal British English, the plural noun smalls can mean underwear.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: little（小的）常带亲昵、怜爱或主观评价，small 更中性，适合客观描述尺寸；tiny（极小的）比 small 程度更强；minor（次要的；轻微的）主要比较重要性或严重程度，通常不表示物体尺寸小。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Little often adds affection, sympathy, or a subjective judgment, while small is more neutral for describing size; tiny means very small and is stronger; minor mainly concerns importance or seriousness rather than physical dimensions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“低于通常尺度”：尺寸小、数量少、影响小；写字也能 small，后腰的窄凹处则是 the small of the back。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor small as 'below the usual scale': less size, less quantity, or less impact. Writing can be small, and the narrow inward curve of the lower back is its small.

senses.english_definition: If you turn your attention to something, you start considering it; if you turn to someone, you ask them for help or support.
senses.collocation_en: turn your attention to; turn to someone for help
senses.collocation_zh: 把注意力转向；向某人求助
senses.sentence_en: When she needed advice, she turned to her sister.
senses.sentence_zh: 需要建议时，她向姐姐求助。

senses.meaning_en: to reach a particular age
senses.english_definition: When someone turns a particular age, they reach that age on their birthday.
senses.collocation_en: turn eighteen; turn sixty
senses.collocation_zh: 年满十八岁；年满六十岁
senses.sentence_en: My daughter turns six next month.
senses.sentence_zh: 我女儿下个月满六岁。

senses.meaning_en: to become sour or unfit to eat or drink
senses.english_definition: If milk or another food turns, it becomes sour or goes bad.
senses.collocation_en: the milk has turned; turn sour
senses.collocation_zh: 牛奶已经变质；变酸
senses.sentence_en: The milk had turned in the heat.
senses.sentence_zh: 天气炎热，牛奶已经变质了。

senses.meaning_en: a rotating movement, a change of direction, or a bend
senses.english_definition: A turn is a movement around a centre, a change in direction, or a place where a road changes direction.
senses.collocation_en: a sharp turn; a quarter turn
senses.collocation_zh: 急转弯；四分之一圈
senses.sentence_en: Give the handle a quarter turn.
senses.sentence_zh: 把手转动四分之一圈。

senses.meaning_en: someone's opportunity to do something in an agreed order
senses.english_definition: Your turn is the time when you can or should do something because others have already done it or are waiting to do it.
senses.collocation_en: take turns; wait your turn
senses.collocation_zh: 轮流；等着轮到自己
senses.sentence_en: It's your turn to choose the film.
senses.sentence_zh: 这次轮到你选电影了。

senses.meaning_en: a change in events, circumstances, or someone's condition
senses.english_definition: A turn in a situation is a change in the way it develops.
senses.collocation_en: an unexpected turn; a turn for the better
senses.collocation_zh: 意想不到的转折；好转
senses.sentence_en: The discussion took an unexpected turn.
senses.sentence_zh: 讨论出现了意想不到的转折。

senses.meaning_zh: 世纪、年份等的交替时期
senses.meaning_en: the period when one century, year, or other period ends and another begins
senses.english_definition: The turn of a century or year is the time around its beginning or the change from the previous one.
senses.collocation_en: the turn of the century; the turn of the year
senses.collocation_zh: 世纪之交；岁末年初
senses.sentence_en: The house was built around the turn of the twentieth century.
senses.sentence_zh: 这栋房子建于十九世纪与二十世纪之交。

senses.meaning_en: an action that helps someone
senses.english_definition: If you do someone a good turn, you do something helpful for them.
senses.collocation_en: do someone a good turn; return a good turn
senses.collocation_zh: 帮某人一个忙；回报别人的帮助
senses.sentence_en: You did me a good turn by finding my keys.
senses.sentence_zh: 你帮我找到了钥匙，真是帮了我一个忙。

senses.meaning_en: a short performance, especially as part of a larger show
senses.english_definition: A turn is a short performance by an entertainer in a show with several performers.
senses.collocation_en: a comedy turn; a star turn
senses.collocation_zh: 喜剧节目；明星表演或精彩表演
senses.sentence_en: Her comedy turn was the highlight of the evening.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的喜剧表演是当晚最精彩的节目。

etymology_story.zh: turn 源于古英语 turnian，并受到古法语 torner 的影响，最终可追溯至拉丁语 tornare，意为“在车床上加工”。从围绕轴心转动这一具体动作，逐渐发展出改变方向、改变状态以及轮流等意义。
etymology_story.en: Turn comes from Old English turnian, reinforced by Old French torner, ultimately from Latin tornare, meaning 'to shape on a lathe.' The physical idea of rotation developed into changes of direction or condition and opportunities that pass from person to person.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 turn 是不可再作常用词缀拆分的自由词根，名词与动词同形。屈折形式：turns、turned、turning；主要派生词及复合词：turner（车工；翻动物品的工具）、turning（转弯处；转动）、turnover（营业额；人员流动率；翻转）、turnout（出席人数；投票率）、turnaround（好转；周转）、turntable（转盘；唱机转盘）、turning point（转折点）、upturn（回升）、downturn（下滑）、overturn（推翻；翻倒）、return（返回；归还）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, turn is a free base without a productive internal affix division; its noun and verb have the same form. Inflections: turns, turned, turning. Major derivatives and compounds include turner, turning, turnover, turnout, turnaround, turntable, turning point, upturn, downturn, overturn, and return.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rotate（旋转）强调绕轴或中心运动；change（改变）泛指任何变化；become（变得）强调进入某种状态。turn 既可表示具体转动，也常表示颜色、性质或局面的变化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rotate emphasizes movement around an axis or centre; change covers alterations generally; become emphasizes entering a state. Turn combines physical movement with common uses for changes in colour, nature, or circumstances.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“转”：物体转动，方向转弯，状态转变，机会轮转。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a turn: an object rotates, a traveller changes direction, a condition changes, and an opportunity passes to the next person.

senses.meaning_en: the condition of someone or something at a particular time
senses.english_definition: The state of someone or something is the condition they are in at a particular time.
senses.collocation_en: a state of mind; in good state of repair
senses.collocation_zh: 心态；保养状况良好
senses.sentence_en: The building is in a poor state of repair.
senses.sentence_zh: 这栋建筑年久失修。

senses.meaning_en: a politically organized country or its government and institutions
senses.english_definition: A state is an independent country, and the state is the government and public institutions that govern a country.
senses.collocation_en: an independent state; head of state
senses.collocation_zh: 独立国家；国家元首
senses.sentence_en: The state provides free education for all children.
senses.sentence_zh: 国家为所有儿童提供免费教育。

senses.meaning_en: a political division of a country with a federal system
senses.english_definition: A state is one of the areas with its own government that together form a country such as the United States or Australia.
senses.collocation_en: state boundaries; across state lines
senses.collocation_zh: 州界；跨越州界
senses.sentence_en: California is the most populous state in the United States.
senses.sentence_zh: 加利福尼亚州是美国人口最多的州。

senses.meaning_en: to express information or an opinion clearly, especially formally
senses.english_definition: If you state something, you say or write it clearly and directly, often in a formal situation.
senses.collocation_en: state your reasons; clearly state
senses.collocation_zh: 说明理由；明确说明
senses.sentence_en: Please state your name and address.
senses.sentence_zh: 请说明您的姓名和地址。

senses.meaning_zh: 国家的；政府提供或管理的；州的
senses.meaning_en: provided, controlled, or organized by a national or state government
senses.english_definition: State services or institutions are provided or controlled by a government; state matters may also relate to a particular state within a country.
senses.collocation_en: state education; state government
senses.collocation_zh: 公立教育；州政府
senses.sentence_en: Most children in the area attend state schools.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个地区的大多数孩子就读于公立学校。

etymology_story.zh: state 经古法语 estat 进入中古英语，最终源于拉丁语 status，意为“站立、位置或状况”，与 stare“站立”有关。“所处状况”进一步发展出社会地位、政治组织和国家等意义，动词则表示把情况明确说出来。
etymology_story.en: State entered Middle English through Old French estat, ultimately from Latin status, meaning 'standing, position, or condition,' related to stare, 'to stand.' The idea of a condition developed into social and political standing, organized government, and the verb meaning 'to express explicitly.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 state 是整体词根；动词可看作由名词转类而来，前置修饰用法也常被归为名词定语。屈折形式：states、stated、stating；主要词族：state + -ment → statement（陈述；声明），re- + state → restate（重述），restatement（重述），misstate（误述），misstatement（不实或错误陈述），understate／understatement（轻描淡写；低估），overstate／overstatement（夸大），statehood（独立国家或州的地位），stateless／statelessness（无国籍的／无国籍状态），statewide（全州的／地），statesman／stateswoman（政治家），statesmanship（政治才能）。
morphology_enriched.en: State is a single modern base; the verb can be understood as conversion from the noun, and its use before another noun is also often classified as attributive noun use. Inflections: states, stated, stating. Major family members include statement, restate, restatement, misstate, misstatement, understate, understatement, overstate, overstatement, statehood, stateless, statelessness, statewide, statesman, stateswoman, and statesmanship.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: condition（状况）侧重身体、物品或环境的实际情形；declare（宣布；声明）比动词 state 更公开或郑重；nation（民族；国家）更强调具有共同身份的人民，而 state 更强调政治组织和治理机构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Condition emphasizes the actual circumstances of a person, object, or environment; declare is more public or emphatic than the verb state; nation emphasizes a people with a shared identity, whereas state emphasizes political organization and government.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“站立的位置”联想“所处状态”；政治上站稳成为国家，把情况说清就是陈述。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect historical 'standing' with a present condition: political standing suggests a state, and putting a situation into clear words means stating it.

translation: 安全检查后，实验将开始。

senses.meaning_en: to start doing or happening, or to have a particular starting point
senses.english_definition: When you begin something, you start doing it; when something begins, it starts happening or has its first part at a particular place or time.
senses.collocation_en: begin work; begin with
senses.collocation_zh: 开始工作；以……开始
senses.sentence_en: The lesson begins with a short conversation.
senses.sentence_zh: 这节课以一段简短的对话开始。

etymology_story.zh: begin 源于古英语 beginnan，原义就是“开始”，由历史前缀 be- 与表示“开始”的日耳曼语词干构成。它的核心意义长期保持稳定，后来广泛用于活动、事件及时间或空间上的起点。
etymology_story.en: Begin comes from Old English beginnan, already meaning 'to start,' formed with the historical prefix be- and a Germanic stem meaning 'begin.' Its central meaning has remained stable while extending across activities, events, and starting points in time or space.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 begin 作为整体词根学习；be- + 历史词干的拆分属于词源分析，不能把 gin 当作现代英语中表示“开始”的自由词根。屈折形式：begins、began、begun、beginning；主要词族：begin + -er → beginner（初学者，双写 n），begin + -ing → beginning（开始；开端；初级的，双写 n）；beginnings 常指起源或早期阶段。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat begin as a whole base in modern English; its historical division into be- and an older stem does not make gin a modern free base meaning 'start.' Inflections: begins, began, begun, beginning. The main derivatives are beginner and beginning, both with doubled n; beginning also functions as a noun and adjective, and beginnings often means origins or early stages.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: start（开始）最通用，口语中尤其常见，也可表示启动机器；commence（开始）较正式，常见于公告或仪式；initiate（发起）强调主动促成某个过程。begin 语气中性，可自然表示活动开始或文本、时段的起点。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Start is very general and especially common in conversation, and it can also mean activating a machine; commence is formal and common in announcements or ceremonies; initiate emphasizes deliberately setting a process in motion. Begin is neutral and naturally describes both starting an activity and the opening of a text or period.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“第一步”：begin 是迈出第一步，beginner 是刚起步的人，beginning 是起点。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'the first step': begin is taking it, a beginner is someone just starting, and a beginning is the starting point.

senses.meaning_en: to move quickly on foot
senses.english_definition: When you run, you move quickly using your legs, with both feet leaving the ground between steps.
senses.collocation_en: run fast; run a marathon
senses.collocation_zh: 跑得快；跑马拉松
senses.sentence_en: She ran to catch the bus.
senses.sentence_zh: 她跑着去赶公共汽车。

senses.meaning_en: to manage or be in charge of something
senses.english_definition: If you run a business, organization, or household, you manage it and make decisions about how it works.
senses.collocation_en: run a business; run a household
senses.collocation_zh: 经营企业；操持家务
senses.sentence_en: They run a small hotel by the sea.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们在海边经营一家小旅馆。

senses.meaning_en: to function or make a machine or system function
senses.english_definition: If a machine or system runs, it works; if you run it, you make it work.
senses.collocation_en: run smoothly; run on electricity
senses.collocation_zh: 运转顺畅；靠电力运行
senses.sentence_en: The engine is running smoothly.
senses.sentence_zh: 发动机运转顺畅。

senses.meaning_zh: 执行程序；开展测试或检查
senses.meaning_en: to execute a computer program or carry out a test or check
senses.english_definition: If you run a program, test, or check, you start it and allow it to carry out its tasks.
senses.collocation_en: run a program; run a test
senses.collocation_zh: 运行程序；进行测试
senses.sentence_en: The technician ran a test to find the fault.
senses.sentence_zh: 技术人员进行了一项测试，以查找故障。

senses.meaning_en: to flow, or to cause water to flow
senses.english_definition: When liquid runs, it flows somewhere; if you run water, you let it flow from a tap.
senses.collocation_en: run the tap; tears run down someone's face
senses.collocation_zh: 打开水龙头放水；泪水顺着某人的脸流下
senses.sentence_en: Tears ran down his cheeks.
senses.sentence_zh: 泪水顺着他的脸颊流了下来。

senses.meaning_en: to extend in a particular direction or along a particular route
senses.english_definition: If a road, line, or boundary runs somewhere, it extends in that direction or follows that route.
senses.collocation_en: run parallel to; run along the coast
senses.collocation_zh: 与……平行延伸；沿海岸延伸
senses.sentence_en: A narrow path runs through the woods.
senses.sentence_zh: 一条狭窄的小路穿过树林。

senses.meaning_en: to continue for a period of time
senses.english_definition: If an event, course, show, or agreement runs for a period, it continues throughout that period.
senses.collocation_en: run for six weeks; run from Monday to Friday
senses.collocation_zh: 持续六周；从周一持续到周五
senses.sentence_en: The exhibition runs until the end of November.
senses.sentence_zh: 展览将持续到十一月底。

senses.meaning_zh: 定期开行；提供交通服务
senses.meaning_en: to travel regularly on a route or provide a transport service
senses.english_definition: If buses or trains run, they operate on a route; if an organization runs them, it provides that service.
senses.collocation_en: buses run every ten minutes; run a shuttle service
senses.collocation_zh: 公共汽车每十分钟一班；提供接驳服务
senses.sentence_en: Trains run every half hour on Sundays.
senses.sentence_zh: 星期日火车每半小时一班。

senses.meaning_en: to compete in an election for a political position
senses.english_definition: If someone runs for a political position, they try to be elected to it.
senses.collocation_en: run for office; run for president
senses.collocation_zh: 竞选公职；竞选总统
senses.sentence_en: She plans to run for mayor next year.
senses.sentence_zh: 她计划明年竞选市长。

senses.meaning_en: to publish or broadcast something
senses.english_definition: If a newspaper, website, or broadcaster runs a story or advertisement, it publishes or broadcasts it.
senses.collocation_en: run a story; run an advertisement
senses.collocation_zh: 刊登或播出报道；刊登或播放广告
senses.sentence_en: The newspaper ran the story on its front page.
senses.sentence_zh: 报纸在头版刊登了这篇报道。

senses.meaning_en: for colour to spread or come out of fabric when wet
senses.english_definition: If a colour runs, it spreads beyond its original area or comes out of fabric when the fabric gets wet.
senses.collocation_en: colours run; the dye runs
senses.collocation_zh: 颜色渗开或衣物掉色；染料遇水渗开
senses.sentence_en: Wash the shirt separately in case the colours run.
senses.sentence_zh: 这件衬衫要单独洗，以防掉色染到其他衣物。

senses.meaning_zh: 达到某种数额、长度或水平
senses.meaning_en: to reach a particular amount, length, or level
senses.english_definition: If a cost or document runs to a particular amount or length, it reaches that amount or length.
senses.collocation_en: costs run to thousands; run to several pages
senses.collocation_zh: 费用达到数千；长达数页
senses.sentence_en: The repair bill could run to several thousand pounds.
senses.sentence_zh: 维修费可能高达数千英镑。

senses.meaning_zh: 使快速掠过或穿过；沿着移动
senses.meaning_en: to move something quickly or smoothly along or through something else
senses.english_definition: If you run your hand or another object over, along, or through something, you move it smoothly in that direction.
senses.collocation_en: run your fingers through your hair; run your hand over a surface
senses.collocation_zh: 用手指梳理头发；用手抚过表面
senses.sentence_en: She ran her fingers through her hair.
senses.sentence_zh: 她用手指梳理了一下头发。

senses.meaning_en: an occasion or period of running
senses.english_definition: A run is a period of moving quickly on foot, often for exercise.
senses.collocation_en: go for a run; a morning run
senses.collocation_zh: 去跑步；晨跑
senses.sentence_en: I went for a short run before breakfast.
senses.sentence_zh: 早餐前我出去跑了一小会儿。

senses.meaning_zh: 固定路线上的行程；一趟运送或接送
senses.meaning_en: a journey along a regular route or for a particular practical purpose
senses.english_definition: A run is a journey made regularly or to collect, deliver, or transport someone or something.
senses.collocation_en: the school run; a delivery run
senses.collocation_zh: 接送孩子上下学的行程；一趟送货
senses.sentence_en: We take turns doing the school run.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们轮流接送孩子上下学。

senses.meaning_en: a continuous period or series of similar events
senses.english_definition: A run of something is a series of similar events or a period during which a particular situation continues.
senses.collocation_en: a run of bad luck; a winning run
senses.collocation_zh: 接连走霉运；连胜
senses.sentence_en: The team has had a run of five consecutive wins.
senses.sentence_zh: 这支球队已经取得五连胜。

senses.meaning_zh: 一次生产、印刷或运行；连续演出期
senses.meaning_en: a production batch, an execution of a process, or a period of performances
senses.english_definition: A run is one complete operation of a process, a batch produced together, or a period when a show is performed.
senses.collocation_en: a print run; a production run
senses.collocation_zh: 一次印刷的印量；一个生产批次
senses.sentence_en: The book sold out its first print run.
senses.sentence_zh: 这本书的首印册数已经售罄。

senses.meaning_en: a unit of scoring in cricket or baseball
senses.english_definition: A run is a point scored in cricket or baseball.
senses.collocation_en: score a run; a home run
senses.collocation_zh: 得一分；本垒打
senses.sentence_en: The batter hit a home run in the final inning.
senses.sentence_zh: 击球手在最后一局打出了一记本垒打。

senses.meaning_zh: 集中争购；集中提取；挤兑
senses.meaning_en: a sudden period when many people try to buy or withdraw the same thing
senses.english_definition: A run on something happens when many people suddenly try to obtain it, especially when customers try to withdraw money from a bank.
senses.collocation_en: a run on the bank; a run on supplies
senses.collocation_zh: 银行挤兑；物资抢购
senses.sentence_en: The rumour triggered a run on the bank.
senses.sentence_zh: 这则传言引发了对该银行的挤兑。

senses.meaning_zh: 供动物活动的围栏场地；滑雪道
senses.meaning_en: an enclosed area for animals to move about in, or a route for skiing
senses.english_definition: A run is an enclosed outdoor area for animals, or a prepared slope or route used by skiers.
senses.collocation_en: a chicken run; a ski run
senses.collocation_zh: 围栏养鸡场；滑雪道
senses.sentence_en: The resort has several ski runs suitable for beginners.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个度假区有几条适合初学者的滑雪道。

senses.meaning_zh: 丝袜等针织物上的抽丝破洞，主要用于美式英语
senses.meaning_en: a line of damaged stitches in stockings or similar knitted clothing, mainly in American English
senses.english_definition: A run is a long damaged area in knitted clothing where stitches have come undone.
senses.collocation_en: a run in your stockings; a run in your tights
senses.collocation_zh: 长筒袜上的抽丝破洞；连裤袜上的抽丝破洞
senses.sentence_en: She noticed a run in her tights.
senses.sentence_zh: 她发现连裤袜上有一道抽丝的破洞。

etymology_story.zh: run 源于古英语 rinnan 等相关日耳曼语形式，早期已兼有“奔跑”和“流动”的意义。由持续移动这一核心概念，逐渐扩展出机器运转、事务经营、路线延伸以及事件持续等用法。
etymology_story.en: Run descends from Old English rinnan and related Germanic forms, with early meanings including both running and flowing. The idea of continuing movement expanded into machines operating, businesses being managed, routes extending, and events continuing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 run 是自由词根，名词由动词转类而来。屈折形式：runs、ran、run、running；主要词族及复合词：runner（跑步者；参赛者）、running（跑步；运行；连续的）、runnable（可运行的；适合跑步的）、rerun（重播；重新运行）、overrun（超过；泛滥）、outrun（跑得比……快；超过）、runaway（逃跑者；失控的）、runny（稀的；流液的）、runoff（径流；决选）、run-up（助跑；前期阶段）、rundown（概要；衰退）、run-through（排练；完整演练）、runtime（运行时间）、runway（跑道）、runner-up（亚军）。runner、running、runny 中双写 n。
morphology_enriched.en: Run is a free modern base, with the noun formed by conversion from the verb. Inflections: runs, ran, run, running. Major family members and compounds include runner, running, runnable, rerun, overrun, outrun, runaway, runny, runoff, run-up, rundown, run-through, runtime, runway, and runner-up. The final n doubles in runner, running, and runny.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jog（慢跑）强调较慢、稳定的锻炼性跑步；operate（运行；操作）对应机器或系统工作；manage（管理）对应经营和组织事务。run 的共同特点是使身体、机器或事务持续运作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jog means running at a slow, steady pace, usually for exercise; operate matches the functioning or control of machinery and systems; manage matches directing a business or activity. Run connects these meanings through continued movement or activity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“持续动起来”：人跑、水流、机器转、企业经营、路线延伸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'keep moving': people run, water flows, machines operate, businesses function, and routes continue.

translation: 维修以来，信号一直稳定。
usage_note: since 在本课用于时间起点；只按句子中的当前义项判断。

senses.meaning_en: from a specified past time until a later time, usually now
senses.english_definition: If something has happened since a particular time, it happened or continued during the period from that time until now or another reference time.
senses.collocation_en: since childhood; since last year
senses.collocation_zh: 自童年以来；自去年以来
senses.sentence_en: We have lived here since 2018.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们从2018年起就一直住在这里。

senses.meaning_en: from the time when something happened
senses.english_definition: You use since to introduce an event that marks the beginning of a period continuing until now or another reference time.
senses.collocation_en: ever since we met; since I was a child
senses.collocation_zh: 自从我们相识以来；自我小时候起
senses.sentence_en: She has felt happier since she changed jobs.
senses.sentence_zh: 自从换了工作，她就感觉更开心了。

senses.meaning_en: because or given that
senses.english_definition: You use since to introduce a reason, often one that is already known or accepted.
senses.collocation_en: since you ask; since we are here
senses.collocation_zh: 既然你问了；既然我们已经在这里
senses.sentence_en: Since everyone is here, let's begin.
senses.sentence_zh: 既然大家都到了，我们开始吧。

senses.meaning_en: from that time onwards or at some later time
senses.english_definition: You use since without a following noun or clause to refer to the period after a previously mentioned time or to something that happened later.
senses.collocation_en: ever since; long since
senses.collocation_zh: 从那以后一直；早已
senses.sentence_en: He left in June, and I haven't seen him since.
senses.sentence_zh: 他六月份离开了，此后我就没再见过他。

etymology_story.zh: since 来自中古英语 sithens 等形式，最终源于古英语 siþþan，意为“在那之后”。表示时间先后的用法后来发展出说明原因的用法，即把一个已知情况作为后续判断的依据。
etymology_story.en: Since developed from Middle English forms such as sithens, ultimately from Old English siþþan, meaning 'after that.' Its temporal use later developed a causal use, introducing a known circumstance as the basis for a conclusion.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 since 是不可再拆分的功能词，无屈折变化，也没有常用的直接派生词族；词尾 -ce 不是现代后缀。同一词形可作介词、连词和副词；常用固定组合有 ever since（从那以后一直）、long since（早已）和 since then（从那时起）。
morphology_enriched.en: Since is an indivisible modern function word with no inflections and no common directly derived word family; final -ce is not a modern suffix. The same form functions as a preposition, conjunction, and adverb. Common fixed combinations include ever since, long since, and since then.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: from（从）标记起点，本身不保证一直延续到现在；because（因为）直接说明原因，尤其适合回答 why；as（由于）也可引出背景性原因，但更容易与时间或方式意义混淆。since 表时间时连接过去起点与参照时间，表原因时常把理由视为已知信息。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: From marks a starting point without itself implying continuation to the present; because directly states a reason and is especially suitable for answering why; as can introduce a background reason but is more easily confused with time or manner meanings. Temporal since links a past starting point to a reference time, while causal since often treats the reason as established information.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 时间线：从那一点到现在；推理线：既然这一点成立，就有后面的结论。
mnemonic_anchor.en: On a timeline: from that point onwards. In reasoning: given that starting fact, the conclusion follows.

senses.meaning_zh: 早期的；靠近开始阶段的
senses.meaning_en: near the beginning of a period, process, or development
senses.english_definition: An early event or stage happens near the beginning of a particular period or process.
senses.collocation_en: early childhood; the early stages
senses.collocation_zh: 幼儿时期；初期阶段
senses.sentence_en: The disease is easier to treat in its early stages.
senses.sentence_zh: 这种疾病在早期阶段更容易治疗。

senses.meaning_zh: 时间早的；提前的；早于通常或预定时间的
senses.meaning_en: happening before the usual or expected time
senses.english_definition: If someone or something is early, they arrive or happen before the usual or expected time.
senses.collocation_en: an early arrival; an early start
senses.collocation_zh: 提前到达；提早开始
senses.sentence_en: We were ten minutes early for the meeting.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们比会议开始时间早到了十分钟。

senses.meaning_zh: 在早期；在较早时候；提前
senses.meaning_en: near the beginning of a period or before the usual or expected time
senses.english_definition: If you do something early, you do it near the beginning of a period or before the usual or expected time.
senses.collocation_en: get up early; arrive early
senses.collocation_zh: 早起；提前到达
senses.sentence_en: We left early to avoid the traffic.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们提前出发，以避开交通拥堵。

etymology_story.zh: early 源于古英语形容词 ǣrlic 和副词 ǣrlīce，均以表示“先前、较早”的 ǣr 为基础。它从“在较早时候”的时间概念发展出“处于初期”和“早于预期”等现代用法。
etymology_story.en: Early comes from the Old English adjective ǣrlic and adverb ǣrlīce, both based on ǣr, meaning 'before' or 'earlier.' This time-related foundation underlies its modern uses for an initial stage and for something happening ahead of expectations.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 early 通常作为整体词学习，不能拆成 ear（耳朵）＋-ly；其形容词和副词形式相同。主要词族：early（早的；早地）→ earlier（更早的；更早地）→ earliest（最早的；最早地）；earliness（早；提前的状态）；非正式派生词 earlyish（比较早的；比较早地）。历史上的 -ly 与古英语构词有关，不表示这个现代词只能作副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, early is normally treated as a whole word, not as ear + -ly; its adjective and adverb forms are identical. Its main family includes early, comparative earlier, superlative earliest, the noun earliness, and informal earlyish, meaning 'fairly early.' Its historical -ly formation does not restrict the modern word to adverb use.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: initial 强调起始阶段；premature 强调早于适当时机，常暗示不成熟或不合宜；ahead of time 表示早于预定时间。early 本身较中性，既可指初期，也可指时间提前。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Initial emphasizes the beginning stage; premature means earlier than is appropriate and often suggests insufficient development; ahead of time means before a scheduled time. Early is more neutral and can refer either to an initial stage or to timing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心锚点：在时间线上“靠前”——靠近开头是“早期”，先于预定点是“提前”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a position toward the front of a timeline: near its beginning means 'at an early stage,' and before an expected point means 'ahead of time.'

etymology_story.zh: money 经古法语 moneie 传入英语，最终源于拉丁语 moneta。Moneta 是罗马女神朱诺的称号；由于罗马铸币厂设在她的神庙附近，这一名称逐渐用于指铸币厂、铸币以及货币。
etymology_story.en: Money entered English through Old French moneie, ultimately from Latin moneta. Moneta was a title of the Roman goddess Juno; because Rome's mint was located by her temple, the name came to refer to the mint, coinage, and money.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：money 是不可再作常用词根、词缀切分的整体名词，通常不可数。主要派生及复合词：moneyed（富有的）、moneyless（无钱的）、moneywise（在金钱方面）、moneymaker（赚钱的人或事物）、moneymaking（赚钱的；赚钱）、moneylender（放贷人）、moneylending（放贷）、money-saving（省钱的）、money-saving tips（省钱窍门）、money-spinning（很赚钱的，尤用于英式英语）。monies 和 moneys 是正式语体中表示“多笔款项”的复数形式；monetary（货币的）属于相关词族，但并非直接给 money 添加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: money is a whole-word noun without a useful current root-and-affix division, and it is normally uncountable. Major derivatives and compounds include moneyed, moneyless, moneywise, moneymaker, moneymaking, moneylender, moneylending, money-saving, and chiefly British money-spinning. Monies and moneys are formal plurals referring to separate sums or funds. Monetary belongs to the related lexical family but is not formed simply by adding a suffix to money.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cash 强调现金，也可指随时可用的资金；currency 强调某国或地区使用的货币体系或货币单位；funds 强调用于特定目的或可供使用的资金。money 是最宽泛、最日常的说法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cash emphasizes physical money or immediately available funds; currency refers to the money system or monetary units used in a country or region; funds emphasizes money available or allocated for a purpose. Money is the broadest everyday term.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 朱诺神庙旁的铸币厂 → 铸出的硬币 → 买东西和办事情所用的钱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Juno's temple-side mint → minted coins → the money used to buy things and fund activities.

senses.meaning_zh: 很少的；几乎没有的；a few 表示“几个；一些”
senses.meaning_en: a small number of; with a, some rather than none
senses.english_definition: You use few before a plural countable noun to say that there are not many, and a few to say that there are some.
senses.collocation_en: very few people; a few days
senses.collocation_zh: 极少的人；几天

senses.meaning_en: a small number of people or things, understood from the context
senses.english_definition: You use few or a few without a following noun to refer to a small number of people or things, and the few to refer to a particular minority.
senses.collocation_en: few of us; a few of them
senses.collocation_zh: 我们当中很少的人；他们或它们当中的几个
senses.sentence_en: We invited twenty people, but only a few could come.

etymology_story.zh: few 源于古英语 fēawe，意为“数量不多的”，与其他日耳曼语言中表示“少”的词同源。其核心数量意义一直保留至今，而 few 与 a few 在现代英语中分别形成了偏重“少得近乎没有”和“虽少但有一些”的表达差别。
etymology_story.en: Few comes from Old English fēawe, meaning 'not many,' and has relatives in other Germanic languages. Its basic numerical meaning has survived, while modern few and a few differ in emphasis: scarcity versus the presence of some.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：few 为整体词，不能进一步作常用词根、词缀拆分。词族：few → fewer（更少的；更少的人或物）→ fewest（最少的；最少的人或物）；fewness（数量少，较少用）。a few、quite a few（相当多）和 few and far between（少而分散；罕见）是短语，不是派生词；few 通常用于可数名词复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: few is a whole word without a productive internal division. Its family includes comparative fewer, superlative fewest, and the uncommon noun fewness. A few, quite a few, and few and far between are phrases rather than derivatives. Few normally applies to plural countable nouns.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: not many 与 few 最接近，直接强调数量不多；a handful of 强调只有屈指可数的几个；several 表示几个，通常比 a few 显得略多，但没有固定数字界限。few 常带不足之意，a few 则强调仍有一些。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Not many is the closest neutral paraphrase of few; a handful of emphasizes a very small, countable number; several suggests a number that is often somewhat larger than a few, without a fixed numerical boundary. Few often emphasizes scarcity, whereas a few emphasizes that some exist.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: few：少得让人注意“缺”；a few：虽然少，仍然“有几个”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Few draws attention to how little is there; a few draws attention to the fact that some are there.

senses.meaning_zh: 带来；带到；把人或物带到说话者、听话者或相关目的地
senses.meaning_en: to take someone or something to the speaker, listener, or another relevant destination

senses.collocation_en: bring a friend; bring something with you

senses.meaning_zh: 带来；造成；使达到某种状态
senses.meaning_en: to cause a result, provide something, or make someone or something reach a particular state
senses.english_definition: If something brings a result or brings someone to a particular state, it causes that result or state.
senses.collocation_en: bring good news; bring something to an end

senses.collocation_en: bring charges against someone; bring a lawsuit

etymology_story.zh: bring 源于古英语 bringan，意为“带来、携来”，与德语 bringen 等词同源。由把人或物带到某处的具体动作，它发展出“带来结果、使进入某种状态”等抽象用法。
etymology_story.en: Bring comes from Old English bringan, meaning 'bring' or 'carry here,' and is related to German bringen. Its concrete meaning of carrying someone or something to a destination extended to causing results and producing changes of state.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bring 是整体动词词根。屈折变化：bring—brings—bringing—brought—brought，其中 brought /brɔːt/ 同时是过去式和过去分词；派生词 bringer 表示“带来某事物的人或事物”。主要短语动词有 bring about（导致）、bring along（带来；带上）、bring back（带回；使恢复）、bring down（使下降；推翻）、bring forward（提出；提前）、bring in（引入；赚得）、bring out（推出；使显现）、bring up（养育；提出话题）；upbringing 表示“养育；教养”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: bring is a whole verb root. Its inflectional forms are bring, brings, bringing, brought, and brought; brought /brɔːt/ serves as both past tense and past participle. The derivative bringer means someone or something that brings something. Major phrasal verbs include bring about (cause), bring along (take with you), bring back (return or restore), bring down (reduce or overthrow), bring forward (propose or move earlier), bring in (introduce or earn), bring out (release or reveal), and bring up (raise a child or mention a topic). The related noun upbringing refers to how a child is raised.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: take 通常从当前参照点把人或物带走，bring 通常朝向说话者、听话者或相关目的地；carry 强调搬运或携带的动作；fetch 强调先去某处取来，再带回来。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Take usually describes movement away from the current reference point, while bring usually describes movement toward the speaker, listener, or a relevant destination. Carry emphasizes the act of transporting something. Fetch means to go and get something and then return with it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把某物“带到这里”：带到眼前是携来，带到生活中是引起，带到法庭上是提起诉讼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bring something to a destination: to a person means deliver it, into a situation means cause it, and before a court means initiate legal proceedings.

senses.meaning_en: a place or event where people buy and sell goods
senses.english_definition: A market is a place or event where people buy and sell goods, often at separate stalls.

senses.meaning_zh: 购买需求；消费群体；销路

senses.english_definition: A market for a product or service consists of the people who want to buy it or the demand that exists for it.
senses.collocation_en: a target market; a growing market for something

senses.meaning_zh: 营销；推广；向目标客户推销

senses.collocation_en: market a product; market something as something

senses.meaning_zh: 出售；经销；将产品投放市场

etymology_story.zh: market 经古北法语 market 传入英语，最终源于拉丁语 mercatus，意为“贸易、市场”，与 mercari（做买卖）有关。其含义从实际买卖场所扩展到交易体系、消费需求，并进一步形成表示“营销、销售”的动词。
etymology_story.en: Market entered English through Old Northern French market, ultimately from Latin mercatus, meaning 'trade' or 'market,' related to mercari, 'to trade.' Its meaning expanded from a physical trading place to commercial systems and consumer demand, and it also developed the verb meanings 'promote' and 'sell.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：market 是整体词，可作名词，也可零派生为动词；market price（市场价格）中的 market 通常分析为作定语的名词。主要词族：markets（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、marketed（过去式及过去分词）、marketing（营销；动词现在分词）、marketer（营销人员或企业）、marketeer（市场经营者；见于 free marketeer“自由市场支持者”）、marketable（适销的；可出售的）、marketability（适销性）、unmarketable（难以销售的）、remarket／remarketing（再次营销／再营销）、marketize／marketise（使市场化）、marketization／marketisation（市场化）。常用复合词包括 marketplace（市场；交易平台）、supermarket（超市）、hypermarket（大型综合超市）、aftermarket（售后市场）、upmarket（高端的；向高端市场）和 downmarket（面向低端市场的；向低端市场）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: market is a whole word functioning as a noun and, through conversion, as a verb; market in market price is normally analyzed as an attributive noun. Its main family includes markets, marketed, marketing, marketer, marketeer, marketable, marketability, unmarketable, remarket, remarketing, marketize or marketise, and marketization or marketisation. Common compounds include marketplace, supermarket, hypermarket, aftermarket, upmarket, and downmarket.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bazaar 主要指由多个摊位组成的集市，有时带地域文化色彩；sell 强调售出或提供出售；promote 强调宣传和吸引关注。market 作名词时可超出实体集市，作动词时常涵盖产品定位、推广及销售安排。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bazaar mainly refers to a market with many stalls and may carry cultural associations. Sell emphasizes offering something for sale or completing a sale. Promote emphasizes publicity and attracting interest. As a noun, market extends beyond a physical trading place; as a verb, it often includes positioning, promotion, and sales arrangements.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“买卖发生的地方”出发：场所是集市，参与者和需求构成市场，让商品进入其中就是营销或销售。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'where buying and selling happen': the place is a market, its buyers and demand form a market, and getting products into it means to market them.

senses.meaning_zh: 信息；消息；资料，通常为不可数名词
senses.meaning_en: Facts or details about someone or something; normally uncountable
senses.english_definition: Information is facts or details that you learn, receive, or provide about someone or something.
senses.collocation_en: provide information; reliable information
senses.collocation_zh: 提供信息；可靠的信息
senses.sentence_en: The website provides useful information about local transport.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个网站提供有关当地交通的实用信息。

etymology_story.zh: 经古法语进入英语，源自拉丁语 informatio，原指赋予形式、构想或教导，与 informare（塑造；教导）有关。词义后来集中于通过告知或学习获得的知识、事实和资料。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Old French from Latin informatio, referring to forming, conception, or instruction, and related to informare, meaning to shape or instruct. Its meaning later centered on knowledge, facts, and details obtained through communication or learning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系：inform（告知）+ -ation（名词后缀）→ information（信息），属于带有词干读音变化的词族关系；不要拆成现代英语的 in + formation。常用词族：inform（告知）、informed（知情的；有根据的）、uninformed（不了解情况的）、informative（提供有用信息的）、informativeness（信息丰富程度）、informational（信息的）、informant（提供消息者）、informer（告密者）、misinform（误告）、misinformation（错误信息）、disinformation（蓄意散布的虚假信息）。表达数量用 a piece of information（一条信息），通常不用 an information 或 informations。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern word-family relationship: inform + the noun suffix -ation → information, with a change in the pronunciation of the stem; do not analyze it as modern English in + formation. Common family members are inform, informed, uninformed, informative, informativeness, informational, informant, informer, misinform, misinformation, and disinformation. Information is normally uncountable: use a piece of information, rather than an information or informations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: facts（事实）强调真实、可核实的具体内容；data（数据）强调供记录、处理或分析的材料；knowledge（知识）强调通过学习或经验形成的认识。information 范围更广，指传递或获得的消息、事实和细节，本身不保证内容真实。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Facts are specific things accepted or established as true; data are material recorded or collected for processing or analysis; knowledge is understanding gained through learning or experience. Information is the broader term for communicated or acquired facts and details, and the word itself does not guarantee their truth.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: inform 是“告知”，information 就是“告知你的内容”；词源中的“塑造”可联想到信息塑造理解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Inform means to tell; information is what you are told. The historical idea of shaping also suggests how information shapes understanding.

etymology_story.zh: 借自拉丁语 area，原指空地、庭院或开阔的平地。英语中的意义由有边界的地面空间扩展为面积，再引申为研究、工作等抽象领域。
etymology_story.en: Area was borrowed from Latin area, meaning an open space, courtyard, or level piece of ground. In English, the idea of a bounded space developed into a measure of surface extent and extended to abstract fields of work or study.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 area 是不可再作常用词素拆分的单纯词，不是 a- + -rea。常用形式与派生：areas（复数）、areal（区域的；面积的）、areally（按区域地，较专业）；常见复合词有 area-wide（覆盖整个区域的）、area-based（以区域为基础的）。area code（电话区号）、surface area（表面积）是词组；aerial（空中的）不是其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, area is a simple base without a useful division into smaller productive parts; it is not a- + -rea. Forms and derivatives include areas, areal, and the more technical adverb areally. Common compounds include area-wide and area-based. Area code and surface area are phrases; aerial is not a derivative of area.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: region（地区）通常指较大的地理范围，常有共同特征；zone（区域）强调由功能、规定或条件划出的范围；field（领域）主要对应知识或活动范围。area 最中性，既可指实体空间，也可指抽象方面。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Region usually denotes a relatively large geographical part with shared characteristics; zone emphasizes a space defined by function, rules, or conditions; field chiefly denotes a branch of knowledge or activity. Area is more neutral and can refer to either physical space or an abstract aspect.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象圈出一块地：它的位置是“区域”，大小是“面积”，抽象化就是“领域”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a patch of ground inside a boundary: its location is an area, its size is its area, and an abstract patch becomes an area of study.

senses.meaning_en: To change position or cause something to change position
senses.english_definition: If someone or something moves, or you move them, their position changes.

senses.meaning_zh: 进展；推动；转入新的阶段或话题

senses.meaning_en: To cause someone to feel a strong emotion

senses.meaning_zh: 促使；使改变看法或立场

etymology_story.zh: 经盎格鲁法语和古法语的 mover 等形式进入英语，源自拉丁语 movere（移动）。从物理位置变化，逐渐引申出推动事情、改变立场和触动情感等意义；名词义由动词发展而来。
etymology_story.en: Move entered English through Anglo-French and Old French forms such as mover, from Latin movere, meaning to move. Physical movement extended to advancing events, shifting opinions, and stirring emotions, while the noun developed from the verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代基础词为 move，动词与名词同形，名词可视为零派生。常用屈折形式：moves、moved、moving；加 -ing 时去掉词尾不发音的 e。常用派生：mover（搬运者；推动者）、movement（移动；运动）、moving（感人的；移动中的）、movingly（感人地）、moved（受感动的）、unmoved（无动于衷的）、unmoving（静止的）、movable／moveable（可移动的）、movability／moveability（可移动性）、immovable（不可移动的；坚定不移的）、immovably（坚定不移地）、immovability（不可移动性）。常见组合有 moving company（搬家公司）、house-moving（搬家）；motion、motive、motor 在历史上同源，但不能当作简单的现代 move + 后缀构词。
morphology_enriched.en: Move is a modern base used as both a verb and a noun, with the noun representing conversion without an added suffix. Inflected forms are moves, moved, and moving; the final silent e is dropped before -ing. Common derivatives include mover, movement, moving, movingly, moved, unmoved, unmoving, movable or moveable, movability or moveability, immovable, immovably, and immovability. Common combinations include moving company and house-moving. Motion, motive, and motor are historically related but are not simple modern formations of move plus a suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shift（挪动；转移）常强调较小的位置变化或方向、重点的改变；relocate（搬迁）明确指迁往新地点，语体较正式；touch（使感动）常指温柔、亲切的情感触动。move 的范围最广，可涵盖身体移动、搬迁、行动和强烈的情感影响。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shift often suggests a smaller change of position or a change in direction or emphasis; relocate specifically means to move to a new place and is more formal; touch often describes a gentle or affectionate emotional effect. Move has the broadest range, covering physical motion, relocation, action, and strong emotional influence.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“从原来的位置动起来”：身体动是移动，住处动是搬家，事情动是推进，内心动是感动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a change from the original position: a body moves, a household moves home, a project moves forward, and an experience moves your feelings.

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 bisigness，由表示“忙碌、专注”的形容词加名词后缀构成，早期包含忙碌、操心和事务等意思。词义后来发展为职业活动及商业经营；现代 busyness 则专门表示“忙碌的状态”。
etymology_story.en: Business comes from Old English bisigness, formed from an adjective meaning busy or occupied plus a noun suffix, with early meanings including occupation, concern, and affairs. It later developed the senses of professional activity and commerce, while modern busyness specifically denotes the state of being busy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词为 busy + -ness，拼写中 y 变 i，但现代 business 已词汇化，读作 /ˈbɪznəs/，不能按拼写逐音节读作 busy + ness。常用形式及词族：businesses（企业，复数）、businesslike（务实干练的）、businessperson／businesspeople（商界人士）、businessman／businessmen（男商人）、businesswoman／businesswomen（女商人）；常见复合词有 business-to-business／B2B（企业对企业的）和 business-to-consumer／B2C（企业对消费者的）。busy（忙碌的）、busily（忙碌地）、busyness（忙碌）属相关词族，但 busyness 与 business 意义不同。business school（商学院）等表达中的 business 通常是名词作定语，不必另列为普通形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, business is busy + -ness, with y changing to i, but the modern word is lexicalized and pronounced /ˈbɪznəs/, rather than as the full spoken sequence busy + ness. Common forms and family members include businesses, businesslike, businessperson or businesspeople, businessman or businessmen, and businesswoman or businesswomen. Common compounds include business-to-business or B2B and business-to-consumer or B2C. Busy, busily, and busyness belong to the related family, but busyness and business have different meanings. In expressions such as business school, business normally functions as a noun modifier rather than a separate ordinary adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: commerce（商业；贸易）侧重商品和服务的交换，语体较正式；company（公司）指具体的商业组织，不能代替不可数的商业活动义；trade（贸易；生意）侧重买卖，也可特指某个行业。business 可同时指商业活动、经营实体以及需要处理的事务。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Commerce is a more formal term for the exchange of goods and services; company denotes a particular commercial organization and cannot replace uncountable business meaning commercial activity; trade emphasizes buying and selling and may refer to a particular industry. Business can denote the activity, an enterprise, or matters requiring attention.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 busy“忙”出发：让人忙的“事务”，发展为谋生的“业务”和经营的“生意”；纯粹“忙碌”写 busyness。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with busy: the things that occupy you are your affairs, and earning a living develops into business. The simple state of being busy is busyness.

etymology_story.zh: 经古法语 servise 等形式进入英语，最终源自拉丁语 servitium（奴役；仆役的工作），与 servus（奴隶；仆人）有关。词义逐渐扩展为替他人履行职责、提供帮助及公共服务，之后又产生设备维护和偿付债务等动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Service entered English through Old French forms such as servise, ultimately from Latin servitium, meaning slavery or a servant's work, related to servus, meaning slave or servant. Its meaning broadened to performing duties and providing help or public services, and it later developed verbal uses for maintaining equipment and making debt payments.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 service 可作为完整词基使用；名词转作动词属于零派生，不宜机械拆为 serve + -ice，因为 -ice 在这里不是能产的现代后缀。常用形式与派生：services（复数或第三人称单数）、serviced（过去式；过去分词）、servicing（检修；债务偿付）、servicer（服务提供者；贷款管理服务机构）、serviceable（可用的；尚可的）、serviceability（可用性）、unserviceable（不能使用的）、disservice（损害；帮倒忙）、self-service（自助服务）、full-service（提供全套服务的）。serve（服务；供应；发球）、server（服务员；服务器）、servant（仆人）属于相关历史词族，并非都由现代 service 直接派生。service industry（服务业）中的 service 通常是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, service functions as a complete base; its use as a verb is conversion from the noun. Avoid mechanically analyzing it as serve + -ice, since -ice is not a productive modern suffix here. Common forms and derivatives include services, serviced, servicing, servicer, serviceable, serviceability, unserviceable, disservice, self-service, and full-service. Serve, server, and servant belong to the historically related family but are not all direct modern derivatives of service. In service industry, service normally functions as a noun modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: assistance（帮助）强调协助解决具体问题，不一定涉及商业或固定制度；maintenance（维护）强调让设备持续正常运作，对应 service 的保养义；serve（服务；供应）适用于为人工作、供餐或发球，而 service 作动词更常用于检修设备、提供专业服务或偿付债务。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Assistance emphasizes help with a particular need and need not involve commerce or an organized system; maintenance emphasizes keeping equipment working and matches the upkeep sense of service; serve covers working for people, supplying food, or starting play with a serve, whereas the verb service more often concerns equipment maintenance, professional provision, or debt payments.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“为对象持续履行所需工作”：为人做是服务，为机器做是保养，为债务做是按期偿付。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of regularly doing what something or someone needs: for people, provide service; for machines, carry out maintenance; for debts, make the payments due.

etymology_story.zh: government 经古法语 governement 进入英语，历史上由表示“治理”的动词加名词后缀构成；其动词源头可追溯至拉丁语 gubernare，最终来自表示“掌舵”的希腊语 kybernan。“掌舵、引导”的意象发展为治理国家，government 也从治理行为发展出执政机构的含义。
etymology_story.en: Government entered English through Old French governement, historically formed from a verb meaning “to govern” and a noun-forming suffix; the verb ultimately traces through Latin gubernare to Greek kybernan, meaning “to steer.” The image of steering developed into governing a state, and government came to denote both the activity and the governing body.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：govern（治理）+ -ment（表示行为、结果或机构的名词后缀）→ government。词族包括 govern、governed、governing、governance（治理）、governor（州长；总督；调节器）、governorship（州长等的职位或任期）、governmental（政府的）、governmentally（在政府层面）、governable（可治理的）、ungovernable（难以控制的）、governability（可治理性）、misgovern（治理不善）、misgovernment（恶政；治理不善）、self-government（自治）、intergovernmental（政府间的）和 nongovernmental（非政府的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: govern + -ment, a noun suffix expressing an activity, result, or institution, → government. The family includes govern, governed, governing, governance, governor, governorship, governmental, governmentally, governable, ungovernable, governability, misgovern, misgovernment, self-government, intergovernmental, and nongovernmental.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: administration 常指某位领导人任内的执政班子；state 强调具有持续性和主权的国家及其机构；regime 指某种统治体制或执政集团，常带批评色彩。government 是指政府或治理制度的常用中性词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Administration often means the executive team serving under a particular leader; state emphasizes the enduring sovereign entity and its institutions; regime denotes a ruling system or group and often carries criticism. Government is the usual neutral term for the governing body or system.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: govern 是“掌舵治理”，-ment 把它变成“治理这件事”或“负责治理的机构”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Govern means to steer or direct; -ment turns that action into the activity of governing or the body that governs.

senses.meaning_en: something that is true or has actually happened
senses.english_definition: A fact is something that is true or has really happened, rather than something imagined or merely believed.
senses.collocation_en: an established fact; the fact that

senses.meaning_en: a piece of accurate information about a subject
senses.english_definition: Facts are accurate pieces of information that help you understand a subject or situation.

etymology_story.zh: fact 源自拉丁语 factum，原意是“做成的事、行为”，来自 facere（做）的过去分词。英语中的意义从“实际发生的事”发展为“可以确认为真的事实或信息”。
etymology_story.en: Fact comes from Latin factum, meaning “something done” or “a deed,” from the past participle of facere, “to do.” Its English meaning developed from an actual deed or occurrence into something established as true.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fact 是独立词根，不能在现代英语中继续拆成有意义的常用词缀。词族包括 facts（复数）、factual（事实的）、factually（从事实角度；如实地）、factuality（事实性）、counterfactual（反事实的；反事实假设）、counterfactually（以反事实方式）、counterfactuality（反事实性），以及复合词 fact-based（基于事实的）、fact-check（核查事实）、fact-checker（事实核查员）和 fact-checking（事实核查）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: fact is a free base with no productive internal division in present-day English. Its family includes facts, factual, factually, factuality, counterfactual, counterfactually, counterfactuality, and the compounds fact-based, fact-check, fact-checker, and fact-checking.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: truth 强调真实性或真实情况；reality 强调实际存在的状态，与想象相对；information 泛指信息，未必经过核实。fact 通常指一个具体、真实且原则上可核实的事项。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Truth emphasizes what is true; reality emphasizes what actually exists, as opposed to imagination; information is broader and may be unverified. A fact is usually a specific true item that can, in principle, be checked.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从历史上的“已经做成或发生的事”，记住今天的“事实”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the historical idea “something actually done”: a fact is something actually true.

senses.meaning_zh: 议题；值得讨论的重要事项
senses.meaning_en: an important subject for discussion or consideration
senses.english_definition: An issue is an important subject that people discuss, debate, or need to make a decision about.
senses.collocation_en: a key issue; raise an issue
senses.collocation_zh: 关键议题；提出一个议题
senses.sentence_en: Housing was a key issue in the election.
senses.sentence_zh: 住房是这次选举中的一个关键议题。

senses.meaning_zh: 问题；困难；令人担忧的情况
senses.meaning_en: a problem or difficulty that needs attention
senses.english_definition: An issue is a problem or difficulty that affects someone or something and may need to be resolved.
senses.collocation_en: a technical issue; resolve an issue
senses.collocation_zh: 技术问题；解决一个问题
senses.sentence_en: We are working to resolve an issue with the payment system.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们正在解决支付系统的一个问题。

senses.meaning_en: one edition of a newspaper, magazine, or journal
senses.english_definition: An issue of a newspaper, magazine, or journal is the complete set of material published together on one occasion.
senses.collocation_en: the latest issue; a special issue
senses.collocation_zh: 最新一期；特刊
senses.sentence_en: Her article appears in the latest issue of the journal.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的文章刊登在该期刊的最新一期上。

senses.meaning_zh: 发行；发放；发行的一批证券、邮票等
senses.meaning_en: the act of officially supplying something, or a batch made available
senses.english_definition: An issue is the official release or supply of something, such as shares, stamps, or equipment, or the items released together.
senses.collocation_en: a share issue; standard issue
senses.collocation_zh: 股票发行；标准配发品
senses.sentence_en: The company raised money through a new share issue.
senses.sentence_zh: 公司通过发行新股筹集了资金。

senses.meaning_en: to officially give or supply something to someone
senses.english_definition: If an organization issues something to someone, it officially gives or supplies it to them.
senses.collocation_en: issue a passport; issue someone with equipment
senses.collocation_zh: 签发护照；向某人配发装备
senses.sentence_en: Each employee was issued with a security pass.
senses.sentence_zh: 每位员工都获发了一张安保通行证。

senses.meaning_en: to formally announce or make something publicly available
senses.english_definition: If a person or organization issues a statement, warning, or order, they formally make it known.
senses.collocation_en: issue a statement; issue a warning
senses.collocation_zh: 发表声明；发布警告
senses.sentence_en: The weather service issued a warning about strong winds.
senses.sentence_zh: 气象部门发布了大风警告。

senses.meaning_en: to release publications, recordings, currency, or securities
senses.english_definition: If an organization issues a publication, recording, or financial product, it releases it for people to obtain.
senses.collocation_en: issue shares; issue bonds
senses.collocation_zh: 发行股票；发行债券

senses.meaning_zh: 流出；冒出；发出，常用于正式文体
senses.meaning_en: to flow or come out of a place, especially in formal writing
senses.english_definition: If smoke, liquid, sound, or light issues from somewhere, it comes out of that place.
senses.collocation_en: smoke issues from; a sound issues from
senses.collocation_zh: 烟从……冒出；声音从……传出
senses.sentence_en: Smoke issued from a crack in the wall.
senses.sentence_zh: 烟从墙上的一道裂缝中冒了出来。

etymology_story.zh: issue 经古法语 issue（出去；出口）进入英语，源自表示“出去”的动词，最终可追溯至拉丁语 exire。“向外出来”的核心意象发展出流出、发放和出版等含义，也经“结果、争议的结点”等意义发展为议题或问题。
etymology_story.en: Issue entered English from Old French issue, meaning “a going out” or “an exit,” ultimately from Latin exire, “to go out.” This outward movement developed into flowing out, distributing, and publishing, while meanings involving an outcome or point of dispute led to the modern sense of a topic or problem.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：issue 是不可再作常规词缀切分的独立词根，可直接作名词和动词，两种词性没有重音变化。词族包括 issues（复数或第三人称单数）、issued（过去式及过去分词）、issuing（现在分词）、issuer（发行人；签发机构）、issuance（发行；签发）、reissue（重新发行；再版）、reissued、reissuing、reissuance（重新发行或签发）、nonissue（不值得争论的问题）及 issue-based（围绕具体议题的）；/ˈɪsjuː/ 也是英式英语中的读音变体。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: issue is a free base without a productive internal affix division. It functions directly as both noun and verb without a stress change. Its family includes issues, issued, issuing, issuer, issuance, reissue, reissued, reissuing, reissuance, nonissue, and issue-based; /ˈɪsjuː/ is also a British pronunciation variant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: problem 明确指需要解决的困难，而 issue 也可以是中性的讨论事项；topic 只是谈论的主题，通常不暗示争议或决策；release 与动词 issue 相近，但使用范围更广，issue 更常见于正式发布、签发和配发。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Problem explicitly identifies a difficulty, whereas issue can be a neutral matter for discussion; topic simply names a subject and need not imply debate or a decision; release overlaps with the verb issue but is broader, while issue commonly describes formal announcements, authorization, or distribution.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“向外出来”：烟冒出来，文件发出来，杂志出一期，问题被提出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “coming out”: smoke comes out, documents are sent out, a magazine comes out, and a matter comes up for discussion.
