etymology_story.zh: century 源自拉丁语 centuria，意为“一百个组成的一组”，与 centum（一百）有关；centuria 也用于古罗马的军事和公民编组。英语后来把它用于一百年的时间跨度，并在板球中用于一百分的得分。
etymology_story.en: Century comes from Latin centuria, a group of one hundred, related to centum, meaning 'one hundred'; centuria also named Roman military and civic divisions. English later applied the word to a hundred-year period and, in cricket, to a score of one hundred runs.

morphology_enriched.zh: century 在现代英语中通常作为完整词基使用；复数将 y 改为 i 后加 -es：century → centuries。常见复合词和组合有 mid-century（世纪中叶的）、turn-of-the-century（世纪之交的）、half-century（半个世纪；板球五十分）和 quarter-century（二十五年）。历史同根词有 centennial（一百周年的；一百周年纪念）和 centenarian（百岁老人），不宜把 century 生硬拆成 cent + -ury。
morphology_enriched.en: Century normally functions as a whole base in modern English; its plural changes y to i and adds -es: century → centuries. Common compounds and combinations include mid-century, turn-of-the-century, half-century, and quarter-century. Historically related words include centennial and centenarian; century should not be mechanically divided into cent + -ury.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: a hundred years 与 century 在时长上相同，但 century 还可指按历法编号的世纪；era 指由显著特征界定的时代，长度不固定；age 也指具有某种特征的历史时期，常用于 the Stone Age 等固定名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A hundred years equals a century in duration, but century can also identify a numbered calendar period. Era means a period defined by distinctive features and has no fixed length. Age likewise describes a characteristic historical period and often occurs in established names such as the Stone Age.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 锁定“一百”：时间里是一百年，板球里是一百分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep one hundred at the centre: one hundred years in time, one hundred runs in cricket.

etymology_story.zh: society 经古法语 société 源自拉丁语 societas（伙伴关系、联盟、交往），后者来自 socius（伙伴、盟友）。伙伴之间的联系逐渐扩展为有组织的团体、共同生活的社会，以及特定社交阶层。
etymology_story.en: Society came through Old French société from Latin societas, meaning partnership, association, or fellowship, derived from socius, a companion or ally. Connections among companions broadened into organized associations, communities living together, and particular social circles.

morphology_enriched.zh: society 在现代英语中通常作为完整词基使用；复数 society → societies。直接相关的形容词是 societal（社会的），副词是 societally（从社会层面看）。共享历史词根的常用词族包括 social（社会的；社交的）、socially（在社会上；在社交方面）、sociable（合群的）、sociability（合群；善交际）、unsociable（不合群的）、socialize/socialise（交往；使社会化）、socialization/socialisation（社会化）、socialism（社会主义）、socialist（社会主义者；社会主义的）、antisocial（反社会的；不爱交际的）和 sociology（社会学）；这些词不能一概视为由现代词 society 直接加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Society normally functions as a whole base in modern English; its plural is societies. Directly related forms include societal and societally. Common members sharing its historical root include social, socially, sociable, sociability, unsociable, socialize/socialise, socialization/socialisation, socialism, socialist, antisocial, and sociology. These should not all be treated as words formed by directly adding suffixes to modern society.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: community 强调共同地域、身份或归属感；association 强调为共同目的正式组成的组织，对应 society 的“协会”义；the public 强调作为整体的普通民众，而 society 更突出人与人之间的关系、制度和共同生活。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Community emphasizes shared location, identity, or belonging. Association emphasizes a formally organized group with a common purpose and overlaps with the organizational sense of society. The public emphasizes ordinary people collectively, while society gives more weight to relationships, institutions, and shared life.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“伙伴相联”理解：共同生活形成社会，共同兴趣组成协会，特定名流圈子构成上流社会。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with companions connected together: shared life forms a society, shared interests form a society or association, and elite social circles form high society.

etymology_story.zh: analysis 经拉丁语进入英语，源自希腊语 analysis，原义为“解开、拆解”，由表示“向上、回溯”的 ana- 和表示“松开”的 lysis 构成。把整体拆成各部分以便理解，逐渐发展为现代的“分析”。
etymology_story.en: Analysis entered English through Latin from Greek analysis, meaning a loosening or breaking apart, formed from ana-, meaning up or back, and lysis, meaning loosening. The idea of separating a whole into parts developed into the modern meaning of detailed examination.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 analysis 通常作为整体词学习；其希腊语历史构造不宜当作可自由套用的现代英语构词规则。复数为 analyses /əˈnæləsiːz/，即词尾 -sis 变为 -ses；主要词族包括 analyse（英式）／analyze（美式，分析）、analyst（分析人员）、analytic／analytical（分析的）、analytically（以分析方式）、analysable／analyzable（可分析的）、analyser／analyzer（分析器）及 reanalysis（重新分析）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, analysis is normally learned as a whole word; its historical Greek elements are not a freely productive English formation pattern. Its plural is analyses /əˈnæləsiːz/, with -sis changing to -ses; the main family includes analyse (British) or analyze (American), analyst, analytic, analytical, analytically, analysable or analyzable, analyser or analyzer, and reanalysis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: examination（检查、审查）侧重仔细查看；assessment（评估）侧重判断价值、质量或影响；interpretation（解释、解读）侧重说明意义。analysis 特别强调研究组成部分及其相互关系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Examination emphasizes careful inspection; assessment emphasizes judging value, quality, or impact; interpretation emphasizes explaining meaning. Analysis particularly emphasizes studying components and the relationships between them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心画面：把复杂整体“解开”，看清各部分及其联系，就是 analysis。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture loosening a complicated whole into parts: seeing the parts and their connections is analysis.

etymology_story.zh: limit 经古法语源自拉丁语 limes 的词干 limit-，原指“边界、界线”。空间上的边界后来引申为数量、能力或行为不能超出的限度，并发展出动词“限制”。
etymology_story.en: Limit came through Old French from Latin limes, with the stem limit-, meaning a boundary or border. A physical boundary developed into a boundary on quantity, ability, or action, and the word also became a verb meaning to impose such a boundary.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代基本词为 limit，兼作名词和动词；名词、动词之间不加词缀即可转换。主要词族：limit + -ed → limited（有限的）；limit + -ing → limiting（起限制作用的）；相关名词 limitation（限制、局限）；limit + -less → limitless（无限的）；un- + limited → unlimited（不受限制的）；另有 limitless + -ness → limitlessness（无限性）及 self-limiting（自限的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Limit is a modern base used as both noun and verb through conversion without an added affix. Its main family includes limit + -ed → limited, limit + -ing → limiting, the related noun limitation, limit + -less → limitless, un- + limited → unlimited, limitless + -ness → limitlessness, and the compound self-limiting.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 作为名词，boundary（边界）突出分隔线，ceiling（上限）突出允许或可能达到的最高值；作为动词，restrict（限制）突出缩小自由或范围。limit 兼指界限本身和设定界限的动作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: As nouns, boundary emphasizes a dividing line, while ceiling emphasizes the highest permitted or possible level. As a verb, restrict emphasizes reducing freedom or scope. Limit can name a boundary or describe the act of setting one.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先画一条边界线：这条线是 limit，让事物不越线就是 to limit。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Draw a boundary: the line is a limit, and keeping something within it is to limit it.

senses.meaning_zh: 证据；依据；表明某事的迹象，通常不可数
senses.meaning_en: Facts, information, or signs that support a belief or help establish what is true.
senses.english_definition: Evidence is information, facts, or signs that give you a reason to believe that something is true or has happened.
senses.collocation_en: strong evidence; evidence of damage
senses.collocation_zh: 有力的证据；受损的迹象
senses.sentence_en: There is strong evidence that regular exercise improves sleep.
senses.sentence_zh: 有充分证据表明，经常锻炼能改善睡眠。

senses.meaning_zh: 表明；证明；作为……的证据，正式用语
senses.meaning_en: To show that something exists or is true, used formally.
senses.english_definition: If something is evidenced by a fact or observation, that fact or observation shows that it exists or is true.
senses.collocation_en: as evidenced by; be clearly evidenced
senses.collocation_zh: 正如……所表明的；得到明确证明
senses.sentence_en: Demand is growing, as evidenced by the increase in sales.
senses.sentence_zh: 销量的上升表明，需求正在增长。

etymology_story.zh: evidence 经法语源自拉丁语 evidentia，原义为“清楚、明显”，与 evidens（明显的）及 videre（看见）同源。词义从“显而易见的状态”发展为使事实显明、支持判断的“证据”。
etymology_story.en: Evidence came through French from Latin evidentia, meaning clearness or obviousness, related to evidens, meaning apparent, and videre, meaning to see. Its meaning developed from the quality of being apparent to information that makes a fact clear or supports a judgment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 evidence 可作为整体名词，并通过零派生兼作动词；不能把它拆成普通英语词 eve + -dence。主要相关词族：evident（明显的）、evidently（明显地、显然）、evidential（证据的）、evidentially（从证据上看）、evidentiary（证据的，常用于法律语境）；动词形式为 evidences、evidenced、evidencing；复合词 evidence-based 表示“以证据为基础的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, evidence functions as a whole noun and also as a verb through conversion; it should not be divided into ordinary English elements such as eve + -dence. Its main related family includes evident, evidently, evidential, evidentially, and evidentiary, the last especially in legal contexts; verb forms are evidences, evidenced, and evidencing, and evidence-based is a compound meaning based on evidence.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: proof（确凿证明）通常表示足以确立结论的证据；indication（迹象）只是提示某事可能成立；testimony（证词）特指证人提供的陈述。evidence 是范围更广的总称，本身未必足以证明结论。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Proof usually means evidence sufficient to establish a conclusion; an indication merely suggests that something may be true; testimony specifically means statements supplied by a witness. Evidence is the broader term and may not establish a conclusion by itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把事实“显明”出来：evident 是“明显的”，evidence 是让判断有依据的“证据”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of making a fact visible: evident means apparent, and evidence gives you grounds for seeing a claim as true.

senses.english_definition: In chemistry, if a substance reduces another substance, it causes the other substance to gain electrons or undergo an equivalent decrease in oxidation state.
senses.collocation_en: reduce iron oxide; be chemically reduced
senses.collocation_zh: 还原氧化铁；被化学还原
senses.sentence_en: Carbon monoxide reduces iron oxide to iron.
senses.sentence_zh: 一氧化碳将氧化铁还原成铁。

etymology_story.zh: reduce 源自拉丁语 reducere，历史上由 re-（向后、回来）与 ducere（引领、带领）构成，原义是“带回”。英语词义后来发展为使事物回落到较小、较低或较简单的状态。
etymology_story.en: Reduce comes from Latin reducere, historically formed from re-, meaning back, and ducere, meaning to lead, with the original sense of bringing back. In English, it developed meanings involving bringing something down to a smaller, lower, or simpler state.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代基本词为 reduce；re- + ducere 是历史来源，不能把 reduce 理解为现代英语中“再次做 duce”。词形变化：reduces、reduced、reducing，添加 -ing 时去掉词尾 e；主要词族包括 reduction（减少、还原）、reducible（可减少的、可化简的）、irreducible（不可再简化的）、reducibility（可约性）、reductive（过度简化的、还原的）、reductively（以简化或还原方式）、reductionism（还原论）、reductionist（还原论者；还原论的）、reducer（减速器、还原剂等）及 reductant（还原剂）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern base is reduce; re- + ducere describes its history, not a modern formation meaning to do duce again. Inflections are reduces, reduced, and reducing, with final e dropped before -ing; the main family includes reduction, reducible, irreducible, reducibility, reductive, reductively, reductionism, reductionist, reducer, and reductant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: decrease（减少）侧重数量或程度下降，可及物也可不及物；lower（降低）突出位置、水平或数值下降；diminish（减弱、缩小）常强调重要性、强度或影响减小。reduce 通常强调使某物变少，也可表示化简、收浓或还原。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Decrease focuses on a fall in quantity or degree and can be transitive or intransitive; lower emphasizes bringing down a position, level, or value; diminish often emphasizes a loss of importance, intensity, or influence. Reduce commonly emphasizes making something less and also has specific mathematical, cooking, and chemical uses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史核心是“带回”：把数量往低处带，就是减少；把复杂式子带回简单形式，就是化简。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the historical idea of bringing back: bring an amount down to reduce it, or bring a complex expression back to a simpler form.

senses.meaning_en: To deliberately pay attention to sounds or speech.
senses.english_definition: If you listen, you pay attention to a sound or to what someone is saying.
senses.collocation_en: listen carefully; listen to music
senses.collocation_zh: 仔细听；听音乐
senses.sentence_en: She listened carefully as he explained the problem.
senses.sentence_zh: 他解释问题时，她仔细地听着。

senses.meaning_en: To take someone's advice, requests, or opinions seriously.
senses.english_definition: If you listen to someone or their advice, you consider what they say seriously and may act on it.
senses.collocation_en: listen to advice; listen to reason
senses.collocation_zh: 听取建议；听从劝告
senses.sentence_en: If you had listened to my advice, you could have avoided this mistake.

senses.meaning_zh: 听一下，常用于 have a listen 等口语表达
senses.meaning_en: An act or short period of listening, used informally.
senses.english_definition: If you have a listen to something, you spend a short time listening to it.
senses.collocation_en: have a listen; give it a listen
senses.collocation_zh: 听一下；听听看
senses.sentence_en: Have a listen to this recording and tell me what you think.
senses.sentence_zh: 听一下这段录音，告诉我你的看法。

etymology_story.zh: listen 源自古英语 hlysnan，意思是“听、留意”，与表示“听觉、倾听”的 hlyst 同源。这个词长期保留主动关注声音的含义，并引申为认真听取或听从别人的话。
etymology_story.en: Listen comes from Old English hlysnan, meaning to listen or attend, and is related to hlyst, meaning hearing or listening. It has retained the idea of actively attending to sound and developed the related sense of taking someone's words seriously.

morphology_enriched.zh: listen 是现代不可再作实用拆分的基本词，字母 t 不发音。主要词形和词族：listens（第三人称单数）、listened（过去式、过去分词）、listening（现在分词；听力、倾听）、listen + -er → listener（听众、倾听者）、listener + -ship → listenership（听众群体、听众规模）；口语名词 listen 由动词零派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Listen is a modern base with no useful smaller productive division, and its t is silent. Its main forms and family are listens, listened, listening as a participle or an activity noun, listen + -er → listener, and listener + -ship → listenership; the informal noun listen is formed from the verb by conversion.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hear（听见）强调声音被感知，不一定有意；pay attention（注意）强调集中注意力，范围不限于声音；heed（听从、留意）强调认真对待并据此行动。listen 强调主动倾听，后接倾听对象时通常用 to。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hear emphasizes perceiving sound, which may happen unintentionally; pay attention emphasizes focusing and is not limited to sound; heed emphasizes taking something seriously and acting accordingly. Listen emphasizes active attention to sound and normally takes to before the person or thing being listened to.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把注意力主动交给耳朵，就是 listen；把别人的话听进去，就进一步成为“听取、听从”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Direct your attention through your ears to listen; let someone's words guide your thinking to listen to their advice.

senses.meaning_en: on most occasions or in most circumstances
senses.english_definition: If something usually happens, it happens on most occasions, although there may be exceptions.
senses.collocation_en: usually go; usually take
senses.collocation_zh: 通常去；通常需要或花费
senses.sentence_en: I usually walk to work, but I take the bus when it rains.
senses.sentence_zh: 我通常步行上班，但下雨时会乘公共汽车。

etymology_story.zh: usually 由 usual 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；usual 经古法语源自拉丁语 usualis，最终与表示“使用、惯例”的 usus 有关。其含义从“按照惯常方式”发展为“多数时候如此”。
etymology_story.en: Usually was formed from usual and the adverb suffix -ly; usual came through Old French from Latin usualis, ultimately related to usus, meaning use or custom. The meaning connects acting according to custom with what happens on most occasions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：usual（通常的）+ -ly（副词后缀）→ usually（通常）。主要词族：usual（通常的）、unusual（不寻常的）、unusually（异常地；不同寻常地）、usualness（通常性，较少用）、unusualness（不寻常性，较少用）；usually 本身没有屈折变化。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: usual + the adverb suffix -ly → usually. The main word family includes usual, unusual, unusually, and the less frequent nouns usualness and unusualness; usually itself has no inflected forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: normally（通常；正常情况下）更突出正常条件或常态；generally（一般而言；通常）可概括总体规律；often（经常）只强调频率较高，不一定表示大多数时候。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Normally emphasizes normal conditions or an expected pattern; generally can summarize a broad pattern; often indicates frequent occurrence without necessarily meaning on most occasions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: usual 是“惯常的”，加 -ly 就是“按惯常情况”：通常如此，允许例外。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Usual means customary; -ly turns it into happening in the customary way: most times, with room for exceptions.

senses.meaning_en: to be in a horizontal or resting position
senses.english_definition: When a person or thing lies somewhere, they are in a horizontal or resting position there.
senses.collocation_en: lie down; lie flat
senses.collocation_zh: 躺下；平躺或平放
senses.sentence_en: She lay on the sofa and closed her eyes.
senses.sentence_zh: 她躺在沙发上，闭上了眼睛。

senses.meaning_en: to be situated in a particular place or direction
senses.english_definition: If a place or object lies somewhere, it is situated in that position.
senses.collocation_en: lie to the north of; lie between
senses.collocation_zh: 位于……以北；位于……之间
senses.sentence_en: The village lies between the mountains and the sea.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个村庄位于群山与大海之间。

senses.meaning_en: to remain in a particular condition
senses.english_definition: If something lies empty, unused, or hidden, it remains in that condition.
senses.collocation_en: lie empty; lie dormant
senses.collocation_zh: 空置着；处于休眠或潜伏状态
senses.sentence_en: The house lay empty for several years.
senses.sentence_zh: 这栋房子空置了好几年。

senses.meaning_en: to be found in something as its cause, basis, or essential feature
senses.english_definition: If the reason, difficulty, or value of something lies in a particular thing, that is where it is found.
senses.collocation_en: the problem lies in; the answer lies in
senses.collocation_zh: 问题在于；答案在于
senses.sentence_en: The problem lies in the way the data was collected.
senses.sentence_zh: 问题在于数据的收集方式。

senses.meaning_en: to belong to someone as a responsibility or decision
senses.english_definition: If responsibility or a decision lies with someone, that person is responsible for it or has the authority to decide.
senses.collocation_en: responsibility lies with; the decision lies with
senses.collocation_zh: 责任由……承担；决定权在……手中
senses.sentence_en: The final decision lies with the director.
senses.sentence_zh: 最终决定权在主管手中。

senses.meaning_zh: 说谎；故意说不真实的话
senses.meaning_en: to deliberately say something that is not true
senses.english_definition: If someone lies, they say something they know is untrue in order to make another person believe it.
senses.collocation_en: lie to someone; lie about something
senses.collocation_zh: 对某人说谎；就某事说谎
senses.sentence_en: He lied to me about where he had been.
senses.sentence_zh: 他对我谎报了自己去过的地方。

senses.meaning_zh: 谎言；故意编造的不实之词
senses.meaning_en: a deliberately false statement intended to deceive
senses.english_definition: A lie is something someone says that they know is untrue and want another person to believe.
senses.collocation_en: tell a lie; a blatant lie
senses.collocation_zh: 说谎；明显的谎言
senses.sentence_en: His claim that he had never met her was a lie.
senses.sentence_zh: 他声称自己从未见过她，这是一句谎话。

senses.meaning_zh: 所处位置或状态，尤指高尔夫球的球位；地势
senses.meaning_en: the position in which something rests, especially a golf ball, or the shape of the ground
senses.english_definition: The lie of something is the position in which it rests, especially a golf ball, or the way the ground slopes.
senses.collocation_en: a good lie; the lie of the land
senses.collocation_zh: 有利的球位；地势，也可比喻事态
senses.sentence_en: Her ball had a good lie on the fairway.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的球落在球道上，球位很好。

etymology_story.zh: lie 的“躺卧”义来自古英语 licgan，后来扩展为“位于、处于某状态”；表示位置的名词也属于这一支。“说谎”义来自另一古英语动词 lēogan，名词“谎言”则承接古英语 lyge，不能把这两组同形词视为同一来源。
etymology_story.en: Lie meaning recline comes from Old English licgan and later extended to location and states; the noun describing a position belongs to this branch. Lie meaning speak falsely comes from the separate Old English verb lēogan, while the noun falsehood continues Old English lyge, so the two groups have distinct origins.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：两个 lie 都是不可再作生产性拆分的基本词。“躺、位于”一支：lie—lies—lay—lain—lying；“说谎”一支：lie—lies—lied—lied—lying，二者的 -ing 形式都将 ie 改为 y。主要词族及组合：liar（说谎者）、lying（说谎的；说谎行为）、lie-in（睡懒觉）、white lie（善意的谎言）；两种名词的复数均为 lies。lay（放置；下蛋）是另一个动词，其变化为 lay—laid—laid，不等于 lie 的完整变化。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: both verbs are basic words without a productive internal breakdown. The recline/location branch inflects lie—lies—lay—lain—lying; the falsehood branch inflects lie—lies—lied—lied—lying, with ie changing to y before -ing in both. Main family members and combinations include liar, lying as an adjective or noun, lie-in, and white lie; both nouns have the plural lies. Lay meaning put or produce eggs is a separate verb with lay—laid—laid, and should not be confused with the full paradigm of lie.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: recline（斜倚；躺靠）主要对应身体姿势，常带舒适或向后靠的意味；be situated（位于）只对应位置义，语气较正式；fib（说小谎；小谎）对应说谎义，通常暗示谎言较轻微。各义项之间不能直接互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Recline refers to bodily posture and often suggests leaning back comfortably; be situated matches the location sense and is more formal; fib matches the falsehood sense and usually suggests a relatively minor lie. These alternatives are not interchangeable across the different senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分成两条线记：身体“躺着”→东西“位于”；话语“失真”→说谎。再配变化：躺是 lay/lain，谎是 lied/lied。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two tracks: a body lies down, then things lie somewhere; an untrue statement is a lie. Pair the forms: reclining takes lay/lain, falsehood takes lied/lied.

etymology_story.zh: foot 来自古英语 fōt；复数 feet 保留了历史上的元音变异，这种变化与早期复数词尾中的元音有关。“底部”和长度单位义由身体部位义扩展而来，foot the bill 则通常被解释为与在账单底部合计金额的旧用法有关。
etymology_story.en: Foot comes from Old English fōt; its plural feet preserves a historical vowel mutation associated with a vowel in an earlier plural ending. The base and measurement senses developed from the body part, while foot the bill is commonly connected with an older use involving totaling an account at its foot.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：foot 是基本词，复数为 feet；动词变化为 foots—footed—footing。主要派生词与复合词：footed（有……脚的；常用于复合形容词）、footless（无脚的）、footing（立足处；基础；关系地位）、footer（页脚等）、football（足球）、footprint（脚印）、footstep（脚步）、footwear（鞋类）、footpath（步行小径）、footbridge（人行桥）、footnote（脚注）、footwork（步法）、foothold（立足点）、footrest（脚凳；搁脚处）、footstool（脚凳）、barefoot（赤脚的；赤脚地）。作前置复合定语时通常用单数，如 a six-foot wall。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: foot is a basic word with the plural feet; the verb forms are foots—footed—footing. Main derivatives and compounds include footed, footless, footing, footer, football, footprint, footstep, footwear, footpath, footbridge, footnote, footwork, foothold, footrest, footstool, and barefoot. A measurement compound before a noun normally uses singular foot, as in a six-foot wall.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: base（底部；基部）与 foot 的底部义接近，但更突出支撑基础；bottom（最下部）适用范围更广，也可指容器内部最低处；pay（支付）对应动词义，用法广泛，而 foot 通常固定用于 foot the bill。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Base overlaps with the lower-part sense but emphasizes support or foundation; bottom is broader and can describe the lowest inside surface of a container; pay matches the verb sense and is widely usable, whereas foot is normally used in foot the bill.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 脚在身体最下端→山脚、底部；脚也曾用来量长度→英尺。账单一路算到底→foot the bill，承担费用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A foot is at the body's bottom, which links it to a mountain's base; feet also provided a length measure. Follow a bill down to its total to remember foot the bill.

senses.meaning_zh: 单个的；仅一个的；一个也……的

etymology_story.zh: single 经古法语 sengle 源自拉丁语 singulus，表示“一个的、各自一个的”。“一个”的核心意义后来扩展到单身、单人使用、单程，以及音乐和体育中表示一个单位的名词与动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Single came through Old French sengle from Latin singulus, meaning one or one each. Its central idea of one extended to relationship status, accommodation, one-way travel, and noun and verb uses for individual units in music and sport.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：single 是基本词，不把 -le 当作这里可自由添加的后缀；singly 的构词可记为 single 的词尾 -le 改为 -ly。主要词族：singly（单独地；逐个地）、singleness（单一；专一；单身状态）、singlehood（单身状态）、singledom（单身生活）、singleton（单个的人或物；单例）、singles（复数名词或单打名称）、singled、singling；动词加 -ed/-ing 时去掉词尾 e。常见组合：single out（挑出）、single-handed / single-handedly（独力的／独力地）、single-minded / single-mindedly / single-mindedness（专心的／专心地／专注）、single-use（一次性的）、single-parent（单亲的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: single is a basic word, with no freely productive suffix -le in this word; singly can be remembered by replacing final -le with -ly. Main family members include singly, singleness, singlehood, singledom, singleton, singles, singled, and singling; the verb drops final e before -ed and -ing. Common combinations include single out, single-handed / single-handedly, single-minded / single-mindedly / single-mindedness, single-use, and single-parent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sole（唯一的）强调没有其他人或物，如 sole owner；individual（单个的；个别的）强调把群体成员分别看待；unmarried（未婚的）只说明婚姻状态，而 single 在日常交往中还可表示没有恋爱伴侣。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sole emphasizes that no other person or thing is involved, as in sole owner; individual treats members of a group separately; unmarried describes marital status, while single can also mean having no romantic partner.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“一个”：一个物件、一个住客、一个方向；single out 就是从一群中挑出一个。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to one: one item, one guest, one direction; single out means picking one from a group.

senses.sentence_en: The two organizations are working toward a common goal.

senses.meaning_zh: 普通的；平民的；不特殊的
senses.meaning_en: ordinary and without special rank or distinction

senses.collocation_en: the common people; the common man
senses.collocation_zh: 普通民众；普通人
senses.sentence_en: The reforms were intended to improve the lives of the common people.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些改革旨在改善普通民众的生活。

senses.meaning_zh: 粗俗的；缺乏教养的，主要见于英式英语，含贬义
senses.meaning_en: considered vulgar or lacking socially approved manners, chiefly in British English and disapproving
senses.english_definition: If someone describes a person or their behavior as common, they mean that they consider it vulgar or lacking good manners.
senses.collocation_en: look common; sound common
senses.collocation_zh: 显得粗俗；听起来粗俗
senses.sentence_en: She thought his loud jokes sounded common.
senses.sentence_zh: 她觉得他大声讲的那些笑话显得很粗俗。

senses.meaning_zh: 公地；公共草地，尤见于英国
senses.meaning_en: an area of open land available for public use or subject to common rights, especially in Britain
senses.english_definition: A common is an area of open land that local people can use, often for walking or recreation.
senses.collocation_en: the village common; walk across the common
senses.collocation_zh: 村庄公地；走过公共草地
senses.sentence_en: Families gathered on the village common for a picnic.
senses.sentence_zh: 各家各户聚集在村里的公共草地上野餐。

etymology_story.zh: common 经古法语 comun 源自拉丁语 communis，意为“共有的、公共的、一般的”。“大家共有”的概念后来扩展为“广泛存在、普通”，名词则用于表示共同使用的土地。
etymology_story.en: Common came through Old French comun from Latin communis, meaning shared, public, or general. The idea of being shared broadly extended to being widespread or ordinary, while the noun came to denote land used in common.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：common 在现代英语中通常作为整体词干，不拆成虚构的 com + mon。主要词族：common + -ly → commonly（通常；普遍地），common + -ness → commonness（普遍性；普通），un- + common → uncommon（不常见的），以及 uncommonly（异常地；少见地）、uncommonness（少见；不寻常性）、commonality（共同特征；共性）、commoner（平民）。常见复合词：commonplace（普通的；平常事）、commonplace book（摘录簿）、commonwealth（联邦；共同体）、common-sense（常识性的）；比较形式为 commoner/commonest 或 more/most common，名词 commoner“平民”需与比较级区别。commons 还可作为相关名词表示共有土地或共同资源。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: common is normally treated as a whole stem, not divided into an invented com + mon. Main family members are commonly, commonness, uncommon, uncommonly, uncommonness, commonality, and commoner meaning a person without noble rank. Common compounds include commonplace, commonplace book, commonwealth, and common-sense. Comparative forms are commoner/commonest or more/most common; the comparative commoner must be distinguished from the noun. The related noun commons can refer to shared land or shared resources.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: frequent（频繁的）主要强调发生次数多；widespread（广泛存在的）强调分布或影响范围大；shared（共有的）对应共同拥有或共同具备的含义，不表示发生频繁。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Frequent emphasizes how often something happens; widespread emphasizes how broadly it is distributed or how far its effects extend; shared matches common ownership or possession of a feature, without implying frequent occurrence.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“大家共有”出发：很多人都有→普遍、普通；大家共用的一块地→公地。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with shared by many: what many people have becomes widespread or ordinary; land shared by a community is a common.

senses.meaning_en: room or an available area

senses.sentence_en: There isn't enough space for another chair.

senses.meaning_en: a gap, an available place, or a blank
senses.english_definition: A space is an empty place between things or a place available for a particular purpose.
senses.collocation_en: a parking space; a space between words
senses.collocation_zh: 一个停车位；单词之间的空格
senses.sentence_en: Leave a space between your first name and your surname.
senses.sentence_zh: 在名字和姓氏之间留一个空格。

senses.meaning_en: the region beyond Earth's atmosphere
senses.english_definition: Space is the region beyond Earth's atmosphere where stars and planets are.

senses.sentence_en: The telescope allows us to observe distant objects in space.
senses.sentence_zh: 这架望远镜使我们能够观测太空中的遥远天体。

senses.meaning_en: a period of time
senses.english_definition: A space of time is a period during which something happens.
senses.collocation_en: in the space of a week; a short space of time
senses.collocation_zh: 在一周之内；短短一段时间

etymology_story.zh: space 经古法语 espace 进入英语，源自拉丁语 spatium，意为“空间、距离或时间跨度”。表示范围与间隔的核心意义后来扩展到太空、文字空格和数字存储空间。
etymology_story.en: Space entered English through Old French espace, from Latin spatium, meaning an extent of space, distance, or time. Its central idea of room or an interval later extended to outer space, written blanks, and digital storage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 space 是不可再按常用词缀拆分的基础词，名词可直接转作动词。常见词族及形式：spaces（复数或动词第三人称单数）、spaced（过去式及过去分词）、spacing（间距；现在分词）、spaceless（无空隙的）、spacey/spacy（恍惚的，非正式）；复合词有 spacecraft（航天器，单复数同形）、spaceship（宇宙飞船）、spaceflight（航天飞行）、spacesuit（航天服）、spacewalk（太空行走）。spatial（空间的）和 spacious（宽敞的）是历史同源词，不宜机械分析为 space 加常规后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, space is a base word without a productive internal affix breakdown, and the noun also functions as a verb by conversion. Common family members and forms include spaces, spaced, spacing, spaceless, and informal spacey/spacy. Compounds include spacecraft, whose plural is unchanged, spaceship, spaceflight, spacesuit, and spacewalk. Spatial and spacious are historical relatives rather than straightforward modern formations from space plus a regular suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: room（空间）强调够不够放置或活动，作此义时通常不可数；area（区域、面积）强调有范围的一块地方；gap（间隙）强调两个物体或位置之间的空处。space 的范围最广，还可表示太空、时间跨度及个人空间。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Room emphasizes whether there is enough capacity for something and is normally uncountable in this sense; area identifies a region or its extent; gap emphasizes an opening between things. Space is broader and also covers outer space, intervals of time, and personal freedom.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“留出一段空处”：地方是空间，字间是空格，地球大气层外是太空；作动词就是把事物隔开。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of leaving room: room around objects is space, room between words is a space, and the region beyond Earth's atmosphere is space; the verb means to put gaps between things.

etymology_story.zh: realize 由 real 与动词后缀 -ize 构成，其早期发展也受到法语 réaliser 的影响，最初的核心是“使成为真实或实际”。后来形成“在头脑中认清事实”的“意识到”义，以及使计划实现、使资产价值变成现金等意义。
etymology_story.en: Realize was formed from real and the verb suffix -ize, with French réaliser also influencing its early development; its original central idea was making something real or actual. It later developed the sense of recognizing a fact mentally, alongside achieving plans and turning asset values into cash.

morphology_enriched.zh: real（真实的）＋-ize（使成为；使具有某种状态）→ realize。realise 是常见英式拼法，realize 也用于英式英语，并是美式标准拼法。常见词族：realized/realised（已实现的；过去式及过去分词）、realizing/realising（现在分词）、realization/realisation（认识；实现；变现）、realizable/realisable（可实现的；可变现的）、unrealized/unrealised（未实现的）、unrealizable/unrealisable（无法实现的）；同属 real 词族的还有 really（真正地）、reality（现实）、unreal（不真实的）、realism（现实主义）、realist（现实主义者）、realistic（现实的）、realistically（切合实际地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Real + -ize, a verb-forming suffix meaning to make or bring into a state, gives realize. Realise is a common British spelling; realize is also used in British English and is standard in American English. Common family members include realized/realised, realizing/realising, realization/realisation, realizable/realisable, unrealized/unrealised, and unrealizable/unrealisable. The wider real family includes really, reality, unreal, realism, realist, realistic, and realistically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: recognize（认出；认识到）强调辨认或承认已经存在的事实；understand（理解）强调掌握意义、原因或关系；achieve（实现）强调通过努力达到目标。realize 可表示意识到事实或实现目标，须根据宾语区分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Recognize emphasizes identifying or acknowledging an existing fact; understand emphasizes grasping meaning, causes, or relationships; achieve emphasizes reaching a goal through effort. Realize can mean either becoming aware of a fact or fulfilling a goal, depending on its object.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 围绕 real“真实”：让目标变成真实＝实现；看清真实情况＝意识到；让资产价值成为现金＝变现。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to real: make a goal real, see what is real, or turn an asset's value into real money.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“以前的”的 former 来自中古英语，承接古英语 forma“最先的”，并带有比较级形式的改造，核心是“时间或顺序在前”。表示成型工具的名词 former 则另由 form“使成形”加 -er 构成，两者不能混作同一构词来源。
etymology_story.en: Former meaning earlier developed in Middle English from an earlier form continuing Old English forma, meaning first, with comparative reshaping. The technical noun former has a separate formation, form meaning to shape plus -er, and should not be confused with the adjective's origin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 形容词 former 在现代英语中整体学习，不拆成 form＋-er；former＋-ly → formerly（以前；从前）。技术名词 former 则可分析为 form（使成形）＋-er（执行者或工具），复数为 formers。另有 sixth-former（英国中学大学预科阶段的学生）等复合词，其中 former 来自表示年级的 form，与“以前的”这一形容词不是同一现代构词关系。
morphology_enriched.en: The adjective former is learned as a whole in modern English rather than analyzed as form + -er; former + -ly gives formerly. The technical noun former does divide into form, meaning to shape, and -er, marking an agent or instrument; its plural is formers. Compounds such as sixth-former refer to students in a school form and are also distinct from the adjective meaning previous.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: previous（先前的）强调在当前或所指事物之前；ex-（前任的，前缀）常用于过去的职位或关系；earlier（较早的）只强调时间更早。former 用于职位或身份时明确表示现在已不再担任或具有该身份，用于两项对照时表示先提到的一项。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Previous emphasizes something preceding the current or specified thing; ex- commonly marks a past role or relationship; earlier simply indicates an earlier time. Former signals that a role or status no longer applies, or identifies the first-mentioned member of a pair.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 形容词抓住“在前”：时间在前＝以前的，提及顺序在前＝前者；工具名词另记 form＋-er＝使材料成形的工具。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the adjective, think earlier in time or first in mention. For the separate tool noun, think form + -er: something that gives material a form.

senses.meaning_en: a living creature, often understood as one other than a human
senses.english_definition: An animal is a living creature such as a dog, bird, or fish; in biology, humans are animals too.

senses.sentence_en: Running a large company is a very different animal from managing a small shop.

senses.meaning_en: relating to animals or obtained from them
senses.english_definition: Animal substances or characteristics come from animals or relate to them.
senses.collocation_en: animal products; animal welfare
senses.collocation_zh: 动物制品；动物福利

senses.meaning_en: relating to basic physical instincts
senses.english_definition: Animal feelings or behaviour come from basic physical instincts rather than careful thought.
senses.collocation_en: animal instincts; animal urges
senses.collocation_zh: 动物本能；本能冲动

etymology_story.zh: animal 经法语并受拉丁语直接影响进入英语，源自拉丁语 animal“有生命的生物”，其相关形容词 animalis 意为“有生命或气息的”，与 anima“气息、生命、灵魂”有关。词义后来稳定为“动物”，并引申出强调本能、粗野行为或某类人的比喻义。
etymology_story.en: Animal entered English through French and direct Latin influence, from Latin animal, a living creature; the related adjective animalis meant having life or breath and was connected with anima, breath, life, or soul. The word developed its established sense of an animal and figurative uses involving instinct, rough behaviour, or a particular type of person.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 animal 通常作为整体词学习，不宜按普通英语单词拆成 anim＋al；animals 是其复数。常见词族包括 animalistic（兽性的；动物本能的）、animalistically（以兽性或本能的方式）、animality（动物性；兽性），另有较少用的 animalize/animalise（使兽化）。常见复合表达包括 animal-like（像动物的）、animal lover（爱动物的人）、animal welfare（动物福利）和 animal kingdom（动物界）；animate（有生命的；使活跃）与 inanimate（无生命的）属于历史相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: Animal is normally learned as a whole word in modern English rather than divided into ordinary English elements anim + al; its plural is animals. Family members include animalistic, animalistically, animality, and the less common animalize/animalise. Common compounds and combinations include animal-like, animal lover, animal welfare, and animal kingdom. Animate and inanimate are historically related words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: creature（生物；动物）突出一个有生命的个体，也可用于想象中的生物；beast（兽）常使人想到大型、凶猛或非人的动物；organism（生物体）是科学用语，范围包括动物、植物及微生物。animal 在生物分类中与植物等相区别，日常语境中则常不包括人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Creature emphasizes an individual living being and can include imaginary beings; beast often suggests a large, fierce, or nonhuman animal; organism is a scientific term covering animals, plants, and microorganisms. Animal distinguishes one biological group from plants and others, while everyday use often excludes humans.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用历史词根 anima“生命、气息”作锚点：animal 是有生命、会活动的动物，再联想到动物本能。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use historical anima, life or breath, as the anchor: an animal is a living creature, and animal instincts are its basic drives.

senses.meaning_en: as an alternative or replacement
senses.english_definition: If you do one thing instead, you do it in place of another thing.
senses.collocation_en: use something instead; instead of
senses.collocation_zh: 改用某物；代替……而……
senses.sentence_en: We didn't have any butter, so we used oil instead.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们没有黄油，所以改用了食用油。

senses.meaning_en: with a different result from the one expected
senses.english_definition: You use instead to introduce what actually happens when it differs from what was expected or intended.
senses.collocation_en: instead of getting better; instead, it got worse
senses.collocation_zh: 非但没有好转；反而变得更糟
senses.sentence_en: I thought the joke would make her laugh; instead, she looked upset.
senses.sentence_zh: 我以为这个笑话会把她逗笑，她却显得很难过。

etymology_story.zh: instead 由中古英语短语 in stede 逐渐合写而成，其中 stede 来自古英语，意为“位置、地方”。其字面逻辑是“处于另一事物的位置”，因此发展出“代替”，并可用来引出与预期不同的实际情况。
etymology_story.en: Instead developed from the Middle English phrase in stede, whose second element came from Old English and meant a place or position. The literal idea of occupying another thing's place produced the meaning of replacement and the use introducing an outcome different from what was expected.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词为 in（在……中）＋stead（位置）→ instead；现代英语中通常作为一个固定副词整体使用，没有常用的屈折变化或直接派生词。相关表达有 in someone's stead（代替某人，正式用语）和 instead of（代替；而不是）；instead of 整体具有介词功能，可接名词、代词或动名词，但不能据此把 instead 单独标为介词。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, in + stead, meaning place, gives instead; modern English normally treats it as a fixed adverb with no usual inflections or direct derivatives. Related expressions include formal in someone's stead and instead of. The expression instead of functions as a preposition and takes a noun, pronoun, or gerund, but this does not make instead alone a preposition.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alternatively presents another possible option; rather often expresses preference or correction, commonly using rather than in comparisons; in place of explicitly marks substitution for a person or thing. Instead emphasizes the replacement actually chosen or an outcome that differs from expectations.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Stead means place: a new choice takes the old choice's place, or the actual result takes the expected result's place.

etymology_story.zh: 来自法语 similaire 或中世纪拉丁语 similaris，最终源于拉丁语 similis，意为“相像的”。英语保留了这一核心含义，既可描述外观相像，也可描述性质或情况相似。
etymology_story.en: Similar comes from French similaire or Medieval Latin similaris, ultimately from Latin similis, meaning “like.” English retained this central meaning and applies it to resemblance in appearance, qualities, or circumstances.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 similar 通常作为完整词基使用，不宜强拆成有独立意义的现代词根和后缀。常用词族：similar + -ly → similarly（相似地；同样）；similar + -ity → similarity（相似性；相似之处）；dis- + similar → dissimilar（不同的；不相似的）；dissimilar + -ity → dissimilarity（差异；不相似性）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, similar normally functions as a whole base rather than as a transparent combination of a productive root and suffix. Its common family includes similar + -ly → similarly, similar + -ity → similarity, dis- + similar → dissimilar, and dissimilar + -ity → dissimilarity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alike（相像的）通常作表语，强调两者相像；comparable（可比较的；相近的）强调在某方面足够接近，因而可以比较；identical（完全相同的）表示没有差别，语义强于 similar。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alike usually appears after a linking verb and emphasizes resemblance; comparable means sufficiently close in a relevant respect to allow comparison; identical means exactly the same and is stronger than similar.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“像”的核心：similar 是有共同点，similarity 是这些共同点形成的相似性。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the word to “like”: similar things share features, and similarity is the resemblance those features create.

senses.meaning_en: therefore; as a result
senses.english_definition: You use thus to introduce a result or a conclusion that follows from what you have just said.
senses.collocation_en: thus reducing costs; thus making it possible

senses.meaning_en: in this way; in the manner described or shown
senses.english_definition: You use thus to refer to a particular way of doing something that you describe or demonstrate.
senses.collocation_en: expressed thus; arranged thus
senses.collocation_zh: 这样表达；按这种方式排列

senses.sentence_zh: 这条规则可以这样表述：每位成员有一票表决权。

senses.meaning_zh: 到如此程度；到这个时候或阶段，常用于 thus far
senses.meaning_en: to this extent or up to this point, especially in thus far
senses.english_definition: If something has happened thus far, it has happened up to the present time or the point you are discussing.
senses.collocation_en: thus far; successful thus far
senses.collocation_zh: 迄今为止；到目前为止是成功的
senses.sentence_en: Thus far, we have received no complaints.
senses.sentence_zh: 到目前为止，我们没有收到任何投诉。

etymology_story.zh: 来自古英语 þus，原义是“这样；以这种方式”，属于日耳曼语传承词。“按这种方式发生”自然可以引出“由此产生的结果”，因而发展出“因此；从而”的用法。
etymology_story.en: Thus comes from Old English þus, meaning “in this way,” and is inherited from Germanic. Referring to how something happens naturally extended to referring to its consequence, producing the meaning “therefore” or “as a result.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 thus 是不可再作实用拆分的单纯副词，没有常用的屈折变化或派生词族。thus far（迄今为止）是固定搭配；thus 的结果义不需要再加 -ly。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, thus is a simple adverb with no useful productive breakdown and no common inflectional or derivational family. Thus far is a fixed expression meaning “up to this point”; no -ly ending is needed for its result meaning.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: therefore（因此）突出逻辑推论；consequently（因此；结果）突出事件造成的后果；hence（因此；由此）简洁而正式。thus 既能表示结果，也能表示“以这种方式”，后三者通常不能直接替代这一方式义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Therefore emphasizes a logical conclusion; consequently emphasizes an outcome caused by an event; hence is concise and formal. Thus can additionally mean “in this way,” a manner meaning these alternatives generally do not replace.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“这样”推到“这样一来”：方式 → 结果；thus far 就是“到这里为止”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from “this way” to “this follows”: manner leads to result; thus far means “up to here.”

etymology_story.zh: 来自古法语 adresser，意为“使笔直；引导；指向”，最终与拉丁语 directus（笔直的）有关。把话语、注意力或邮件“指向”某人或某处，逐渐形成了“讲话”“处理问题”和“地址”等意义。
etymology_story.en: Address comes from Old French adresser, meaning “to straighten, direct, or guide,” ultimately related to Latin directus, “straight.” Directing speech, attention, or mail toward a recipient or destination produced its meanings involving speaking, dealing with matters, and locations.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 address 通常作为完整词基使用，不应按 a + dress 理解；名词与动词同形，美式名词可重读首音节，动词通常重读末音节。词族：addresses（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、addressed（过去式和过去分词）、addressing（现在分词）；address + -ee → addressee（收件人；受话人）；address + -able → addressable（可处理的；可寻址的）；addressable + -ity → addressability（可寻址性）；unaddressed（未处理的；未写地址的）；readdress（重新写地址；重新处理）；misaddress（写错地址）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, address normally functions as a whole base and should not be interpreted as a + dress. The noun and verb share their spelling; the American noun can have initial stress, while the verb normally has final stress. Its family includes addresses, addressed, addressing, address + -ee → addressee, address + -able → addressable, addressable + -ity → addressability, unaddressed, readdress, and misaddress.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: location（位置；地点）指所在之处，address 则通常指可用于识别或投递的地址信息；speech（讲话；演说）适用范围更广，名词 address 通常较正式；tackle（着手应对）强调积极处理难题，动词 address 强调给予关注并采取应对措施，不保证问题已解决。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Location identifies a place, whereas address usually supplies identifying or delivery details; speech is broader, while a noun address is typically formal; tackle emphasizes actively confronting a difficulty, while the verb address means attending to it and taking action without necessarily solving it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“指向”：信件指向地址，话语指向听众，注意力指向问题。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “direct toward”: mail toward an address, words toward an audience, and attention toward a problem.

etymology_story.zh: 可追溯至古英语 lǣdere，由表示“引导；带领”的动词加上表示施事者的后缀构成。“带领别人的人”后来也指比赛或行业中居于前列者，并产生了英国英语中“社论”和“乐队首席”等用法。
etymology_story.en: Leader goes back to Old English lǣdere, formed from the verb meaning “to guide or lead” with an agent suffix. The idea of someone who leads extended to those ahead in competition or industry and to British uses for an editorial and an orchestra's principal violinist.

morphology_enriched.zh: lead（带领，读 /liːd/）+ -er（执行动作的人）→ leader（带领者）。常用词族：lead—led—led（带领的动词变化）、leading（领先的；带领）、leader + -ship → leadership（领导能力；领导层）、leader + -less → leaderless（没有领导者的）、co-leader（共同领导者）；相关派生还有 mislead（误导）、misleading（误导性的）和 misleadingly（误导地）。这里的 lead 与表示“铅”、读 /led/ 的名词无关。
morphology_enriched.en: Lead /liːd/ + the agent suffix -er → leader, a person who leads. Its common family includes lead—led—led, leading, leader + -ship → leadership, leader + -less → leaderless, and co-leader; related formations include mislead, misleading, and misleadingly. This lead is unrelated to the noun lead /led/, the metal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chief（首领；主管）强调最高职位或权威；head（负责人）强调在组织中的正式负责地位；pioneer（先驱）强调率先开辟某个领域。leader 可侧重引导、影响力或领先地位，不一定拥有正式头衔。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chief emphasizes the highest rank or authority; head emphasizes formal responsibility for an organization; pioneer emphasizes opening up a new field. Leader can emphasize guidance, influence, or being ahead and does not always imply an official title.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lead 是“带路”，-er 是“做事的人”：带着大家走，或走在大家前面，就是 leader。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Lead means “show the way,” and -er marks the person: a leader guides others or stays ahead of them.

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 completus，即 complēre（填满；完成）的过去分词，其构成包含表示整体或强化的 com- 和表示“填满”的 plēre。从“填得满满的”发展出“完整的”，再由“使之完整”形成动词“完成”的用法。
etymology_story.en: Complete comes from Latin completus, the past participle of complēre, “to fill up or finish,” combining com-, with a collective or intensive force, and plēre, “to fill.” The idea of being fully filled developed into “whole,” while making something whole underlies the verb meaning “finish.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常以 complete 为完整词基；com- + plēre 是历史词源分析，不是可自由运用的现代英语构词公式。常用词族：completes、completed、completing；complete + -ly → completely（完全地，保留 e）；complete + -ness → completeness（完整性）；complete + -ion → completion（完成，去掉末尾 e）；in- + complete → incomplete（不完整的；未完成的），以及 incompletely（不完全地）、incompleteness（不完整性）和 uncompleted（尚未完成的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats complete as a whole base; com- + plēre describes its historical origin rather than a productive English formation. Its common family includes completes, completed, completing, complete + -ly → completely, retaining e; complete + -ness → completeness; complete + -ion → completion, dropping final e; and in- + complete → incomplete, alongside incompletely, incompleteness, and uncompleted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: finish（完成）侧重使活动结束，complete 更突出所有要求或部分均已完成；whole（完整的；全部的）强调整体没有被分割或缺失，complete 强调所需部分齐全；total（完全的；总计的）强调程度或数量达到全部，常与 complete 的加强语气用法接近。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Finish emphasizes bringing an activity to an end, while complete more strongly suggests fulfilling every requirement or part; whole emphasizes an undivided or intact entirety, while complete emphasizes having all needed parts; total emphasizes the full amount or degree and often overlaps with emphatic complete.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用“填满”串起两种词性：已经填满、没有缺口＝完整的；把最后的缺口填上＝完成。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect both parts of speech through “fill up”: having no gaps means complete; filling the last gap means to complete.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“手臂”的 arm 来自古英语 earm，后来引申为物体的臂状部分和组织分支。表示“武器”的 arms 则经古法语 armes 来自拉丁语 arma；动词 arm 的“武装”义属于这条不同的词源线，后来又引申为提供知识和使装置进入待用状态。
etymology_story.en: Arm meaning a body part comes from Old English earm and later developed meanings for projecting parts and organizational branches. Arms meaning weapons comes through Old French armes from Latin arma; the verb meaning to equip with weapons belongs to this separate history and later extended to supplying knowledge and making devices ready to operate.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，arm 是可独立使用的词基，不宜再拆成有意义的前后缀。主要词族：arm → arms、armed、arming；arm + -less → armless（无臂的）；arm + -ful → armful（一抱的量）；un- + armed → unarmed（未武装的）；dis- + arm → disarm（解除武装），并有 disarmed、disarming、disarmament（解除武装）；re- + arm → rearm（重新武装），并有 rearmament（重新武装）。相关派生词 armament / armaments 表示军备、武器。常见复合词有 armband（臂带）、armchair（扶手椅）、armrest（扶手）、forearm（前臂）、underarm（腋下的；腋下）、firearm（枪械）和 sidearm（随身佩带的枪械）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, arm is a free base and should not be divided into smaller meaningful affixes. Its main family includes arms, armed, arming; arm + -less → armless; arm + -ful → armful, an amount held in the arms; un- + armed → unarmed; dis- + arm → disarm, with disarmed, disarming, and disarmament; and re- + arm → rearm, with rearmament. Related derivatives armament and armaments refer to military equipment or weaponry. Common compounds include armband, armchair, armrest, forearm, underarm, firearm, and sidearm.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 肢体义：limb（肢体）范围更大，可指手臂或腿，arm 专指上肢。武装义：equip（配备）适用于各种装备或资源，arm 通常强调武器，也可比喻提供应对问题的知识。部门义：branch（分支）强调组织结构，arm 常强调承担某种职能的部门。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the body sense, limb is broader and can mean an arm or a leg, whereas arm specifically denotes an upper limb. For the verb, equip covers many kinds of resources, while arm usually emphasizes weapons or, figuratively, knowledge for dealing with a challenge. For organizations, branch emphasizes structure, while arm often emphasizes a particular function.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 两条线记忆：手臂向外伸 → 扶手、机械臂、组织分支；武器交到手里 → 武装、配备知识、进入待发状态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two tracks: a body arm extends outward, suggesting supports and branches; putting weapons into someone's hands suggests arming, supplying knowledge, and making something ready for action.

senses.meaning_en: a named unit of code that performs a particular task

senses.english_definition: If something functions, it works or operates in the way it is meant to.

etymology_story.zh: function 经法语进入英语，源自拉丁语 functio，意为执行、履行，相关动词 fungi 表示履行职责或完成任务。它由“履行某项工作”发展出“功能、作用”，随后形成运转、正式活动以及数学和计算机中的专门含义。
etymology_story.en: Function entered English through French from Latin functio, meaning performance or discharge of a duty, related to fungi, to perform or carry out a task. From performing a job, it developed meanings involving purpose and operation, as well as uses for formal events and specialized mathematical and computing concepts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词以完整词基 function 为核心，不应机械拆成 func + -tion。主要词族：functions、functioned、functioning；function + -al → functional（功能性的；能正常工作的）；functional + -ly → functionally（在功能上）；functional + -ity → functionality（功能；功能性）；non- + functional → nonfunctional（不起作用的）；dys- + function → dysfunction（功能障碍），并有 dysfunctional（功能失调的）和 dysfunctionally（以功能失调的方式）；mal- + function → malfunction（故障；发生故障），并有 malfunctioning（发生故障的）。另有 multifunctional（多功能的）、functionary（官员；机构工作人员）和 functionalism / functionalist（功能主义／功能主义者）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern word formation centers on the whole base function; mechanically dividing it into func + -tion is misleading. The main family includes functions, functioned, functioning; function + -al → functional; functional + -ly → functionally; functional + -ity → functionality; non- + functional → nonfunctional; dys- + function → dysfunction, with dysfunctional and dysfunctionally; and mal- + function → malfunction, with malfunctioning. Other established relatives include multifunctional, functionary, functionalism, and functionalist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: purpose（目的）强调某事物为何存在或被使用，function（功能）强调它具体做什么；role（角色、作用）强调在某个系统或情境中的位置和贡献；operate（运转、操作）作动词时常用于机器或系统，function 更侧重是否能够发挥应有作用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Purpose emphasizes why something exists or is used, while function emphasizes what it does. Role emphasizes its position and contribution within a system or situation. As a verb, operate often describes machines or systems in action, while function focuses on their ability to perform their intended work.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“履行任务”：承担的任务是功能，任务执行起来就是运转。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to performing a task: the task something performs is its function; performing that task is functioning.

senses.meaning_zh: 机会；做某事的有利时机

senses.english_definition: If you have a chance to do something, you have an opportunity to do it.

senses.sentence_en: We met by chance at the station.

senses.collocation_en: chance it; chance missing the train
senses.collocation_zh: 冒险一试；冒赶不上火车的风险
senses.sentence_en: We might get wet, but let's chance it.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们可能会淋湿，不过还是冒险试试吧。

senses.english_definition: If you chance to do something, or chance upon something, it happens or you find it unexpectedly.
senses.collocation_en: chance upon an old friend; chance to notice
senses.collocation_zh: 偶然遇见老朋友；碰巧注意到
senses.sentence_en: I chanced upon an old photograph while clearing out a drawer.
senses.sentence_zh: 我清理抽屉时偶然发现了一张旧照片。

senses.meaning_zh: 偶然的；意外发生的，通常用于名词前
senses.meaning_en: unplanned or accidental, usually used before a noun
senses.english_definition: A chance event happens unexpectedly and has not been arranged.

senses.collocation_zh: 一次偶遇；一个偶然的发现
senses.sentence_en: A chance encounter led to a lasting friendship.
senses.sentence_zh: 一次偶遇促成了一段长久的友谊。

etymology_story.zh: chance 经古法语 cheance 进入英语，远源是拉丁语 cadentia，意为“落下”，与 cadere（落下）有关。“事情如何落定”发展为偶然发生的结果，继而引申为运气、可能性和机会。
etymology_story.en: Chance entered English through Old French cheance, ultimately from Latin cadentia, meaning falling, related to cadere, to fall. The idea of how events fall or turn out developed into an accidental outcome and then into luck, possibility, and opportunity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 chance 是完整词基。屈折形式：chance + -s → chances（机会或可能性的复数；动词第三人称单数）；chance + -d → chanced（过去式、过去分词）；去掉词尾 e 再加 -ing → chancing。主要派生词：chance + -y，去 e → chancy（有风险的；结果难料的），比较级 chancier、最高级 chanciest；chancy 的 y 变 i 后加 -ness → chanciness（风险性；不确定性）；chance + -r → chancer（英式非正式用语：投机取巧的人）。常用结构包括 by chance（偶然地）、chance upon / on（偶然遇见或发现）和 chance to do（碰巧做）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chance is a whole base. Its inflections are chance + -s → chances, for the plural or third-person singular; chance + -d → chanced, for the past tense and past participle; and chance with final e removed + -ing → chancing. Main derivatives include chance + -y, dropping e → chancy, meaning risky or uncertain, with chancier and chanciest; chancy with y changed to i + -ness → chanciness; and chance + -r → chancer, an informal British word for an opportunist. Common constructions include by chance, chance upon / on, and chance to do.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: opportunity（机会）强调适合采取行动的时机，chance 还可表示可能性或偶然；possibility（可能性）强调某事有可能发生，chance 常进一步涉及发生的概率大小；luck（运气）强调不可控制的好运或坏运，chance 更中性，侧重偶然性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Opportunity emphasizes an opening for action, while chance can also mean likelihood or accident. Possibility emphasizes that something can happen, while chance often also concerns how likely it is. Luck emphasizes uncontrollable good or bad fortune; chance is more neutral and focuses on randomness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 事情怎样“落定”无法预知：可能带来机会，也可能需要冒险。
mnemonic_anchor.en: You cannot always predict how events will fall: the result may offer an opportunity or require taking a risk.

usage_note: mention something to someone 是向某人提到某事；不需要把直接宾语前加 about。

senses.meaning_en: to refer to something briefly in speech or writing
senses.english_definition: If you mention something, you say or write about it briefly without giving much detail.
senses.collocation_en: mention a problem; mention something to someone
senses.collocation_zh: 提到一个问题；向某人提起某事
senses.sentence_en: She mentioned that she might move to London.
senses.sentence_zh: 她提到自己可能会搬到伦敦。

senses.meaning_zh: 提及；简短的说起或记述
senses.meaning_en: a brief reference to something in speech or writing
senses.english_definition: A mention of something is a brief statement about it in speech or writing.
senses.collocation_en: make no mention of; a brief mention
senses.collocation_zh: 完全没有提及；简短的提及
senses.sentence_en: The report made no mention of the additional costs.
senses.sentence_zh: 这份报告完全没有提及额外费用。

senses.meaning_en: a public expression of praise or recognition
senses.english_definition: A mention can be public recognition of someone's work or achievement, especially in a competition.
senses.collocation_en: an honourable mention; deserve special mention
senses.collocation_zh: 荣誉奖；值得特别表扬
senses.sentence_en: Her photograph received an honourable mention in the competition.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的摄影作品在比赛中获得了荣誉奖。

etymology_story.zh: mention 经古法语来自拉丁语 mentio，词干形式为 mention-，表示提及、使人想起，与表示心智和思考的词源家族有关。英语先采用名词，后来由名词形成动词，核心含义一直是把某事简短地带入谈话或文字。
etymology_story.en: Mention came through Old French from Latin mentio, with the stem mention-, meaning a reference or calling to mind, and belongs to a historical word family associated with thought. English adopted the noun first and later formed the verb from it, retaining the central idea of briefly bringing something into speech or writing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语以 mention 为完整词基，名词与动词之间属于零派生，不宜把它分析为独立词根 men 加 -tion。主要词族：mentions（复数；第三人称单数）、mentioned（过去式；过去分词）、mentioning（现在分词；动名词）；mention + -able → mentionable（可提及的）；un- + mentionable → unmentionable（不宜提及的），并有 unmentionably（不宜启齿地）和 unmentionables（委婉语：内衣）；un- + mentioned → unmentioned（未被提及的）；afore- + mentioned → aforementioned（前述的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats mention as a whole base, with conversion between noun and verb; it should not be analyzed as an independent root men plus -tion. Its main family includes mentions, mentioned, mentioning; mention + -able → mentionable; un- + mentionable → unmentionable, with unmentionably and the euphemistic plural noun unmentionables, meaning underwear; un- + mentioned → unmentioned; and afore- + mentioned → aforementioned, meaning previously mentioned.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: refer to（提及、谈到）范围较广，可作简短或较详细的指涉；mention 通常强调一带而过。bring up（提出）强调主动把话题引入讨论；cite（引用、列举）强调把来源、事实或例子作为依据。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Refer to is broad and can cover brief or more extended references, while mention usually suggests little detail. Bring up emphasizes introducing a topic into a discussion. Cite emphasizes presenting a source, fact, or example as support.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把一件事带到对方脑海里，轻轻点到，就是 mention。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bring something into another person's mind with a brief reference: mention it.

usage_note: factor 是影响结果的一个条件或原因；通常不表示唯一原因；factor in 另可作动词短语。

senses.meaning_en: something that influences a result or situation
senses.english_definition: A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.
senses.collocation_en: a key factor; a contributing factor
senses.collocation_zh: 关键因素；促成因素
senses.sentence_en: Cost was a major factor in our decision.
senses.sentence_zh: 成本是影响我们决定的一个主要因素。

senses.meaning_en: a number or expression that divides another exactly
senses.english_definition: A factor of a number or expression divides it exactly, leaving no remainder.
senses.collocation_en: a prime factor; a common factor
senses.collocation_zh: 质因数；公因数
senses.sentence_en: Three is a factor of twelve.
senses.sentence_zh: 三是十二的一个因数。

senses.meaning_zh: 倍数；用于换算或调整的系数
senses.meaning_en: a multiplier used to express a ratio, change, or conversion
senses.english_definition: A factor is a number by which an amount is multiplied to obtain another amount.
senses.collocation_en: by a factor of ten; a conversion factor
senses.collocation_zh: 按十倍的比例；换算系数
senses.sentence_en: The new system increased processing speed by a factor of ten.
senses.sentence_zh: 新系统把处理速度提高到了原来的十倍。

senses.meaning_zh: 把……计入；将……纳入考虑，常用于 factor in / into
senses.meaning_en: to include something in a calculation or decision
senses.english_definition: If you factor something in, or factor it into a calculation or decision, you take it into account.
senses.collocation_en: factor in the cost; factor something into a decision
senses.collocation_zh: 把成本计入；将某事纳入决策考虑
senses.sentence_en: We need to factor delivery charges into the total cost.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们需要把运费计入总成本。

senses.meaning_zh: 将数或代数式分解为因数或因式
senses.meaning_en: to express a number or algebraic expression as a product of factors
senses.english_definition: If you factor a number or an algebraic expression, you write it as two or more factors multiplied together.
senses.collocation_en: factor a polynomial; factor out a common term
senses.collocation_zh: 将多项式分解因式；提取公因式
senses.sentence_en: You can factor six x plus nine as three times the quantity two x plus three.
senses.sentence_zh: 可以把 6x + 9 分解为 3(2x + 3)。

etymology_story.zh: factor 源自拉丁语 factor，意为“做事者、制造者”，由 facere（做、制造）形成。英语早期用它指代理人，后来在数学中指构成乘积的因数，并进一步发展出促成某个结果的“因素”义。
etymology_story.en: Factor comes from Latin factor, meaning a doer or maker, formed from facere, to do or make. Early English used it for an agent; it later acquired the mathematical sense of something making up a product and the broader sense of something contributing to a result.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语以完整词基 factor 构词，名词与动词之间可视为零派生；历史上的拉丁语构词不等于现代可自由使用的 fac + -tor。主要词族：factors、factored、factoring；factor + -able → factorable（可分解因式的）；factor + -ize / -ise → factorize / factorise（分解因式）；factorization / factorisation（因式分解）；factor + -ial → factorial（阶乘；因子的），另有 factorially（以阶乘方式）；co- + factor → cofactor（余因子；辅助因子）。常用动词结构有 factor in / into（计入）和 factor out（提取公因子；排除某因素的影响）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English builds on the whole base factor, with conversion between noun and verb; its historical Latin formation does not make fac + -tor a freely usable modern analysis. The main family includes factors, factored, factoring; factor + -able → factorable; factor + -ize / -ise → factorize / factorise; factorization / factorisation; factor + -ial → factorial, a noun for a factorial and an adjective relating to factors, with factorially; and co- + factor → cofactor. Common verb constructions include factor in / into, meaning include in a calculation, and factor out, meaning extract a common factor or remove an influence from consideration.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: element（要素）强调整体的组成部分，不一定影响结果；factor（因素）强调对结果有影响。cause（原因）更直接地解释某事为何发生，而 factor 可以只是多个促成条件之一；consideration（考虑因素）强调决策时需要权衡的事项。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Element emphasizes a component of a whole, whether or not it affects an outcome; factor emphasizes influence on an outcome. Cause more directly explains why something happens, while a factor may be only one contributing condition. Consideration emphasizes something that must be weighed when making a decision.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“参与做成结果”：数学里是组成乘积的因数，现实里是促成结果的因素。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of something that helps make a result: in mathematics it helps make a product; in everyday situations it helps shape an outcome.

translation: 课程结束后，我们仍保持联系。
usage_note: in contact with 表示与某人联系；作动词时直接说 contact someone，不加 with。

senses.meaning_en: communication or interaction with someone
senses.english_definition: If you have contact with someone, you communicate with them or meet them.
senses.collocation_en: keep in contact; lose contact with someone
senses.collocation_zh: 保持联系；与某人失去联系
senses.sentence_en: We kept in contact after leaving school.
senses.sentence_zh: 离开学校后，我们一直保持着联系。

senses.meaning_en: the state of physically touching something
senses.english_definition: Contact is the state of two people or things physically touching each other.
senses.collocation_en: direct contact; come into contact with something
senses.collocation_zh: 直接接触；接触到某物
senses.sentence_en: Avoid direct contact with the liquid.
senses.sentence_zh: 避免直接接触这种液体。

senses.meaning_zh: 联系人；可提供帮助或信息的熟人
senses.meaning_en: a person you know who can provide help or information
senses.english_definition: A contact is someone you know who can help you or give you useful information, especially in your work.
senses.collocation_en: a business contact; a useful contact
senses.collocation_zh: 业务联系人；能提供帮助的熟人
senses.sentence_en: A business contact introduced me to the company.
senses.sentence_zh: 一位业务联系人把我介绍给了这家公司。

senses.meaning_en: a conductive part that completes an electrical connection
senses.english_definition: An electrical contact is a metal part that allows electricity to flow when it touches another conducting part.
senses.collocation_en: electrical contacts; battery contacts
senses.collocation_zh: 电触点；电池触点
senses.sentence_en: Clean the battery contacts with a dry cloth.
senses.sentence_zh: 用干布清洁电池触点。

senses.meaning_zh: 隐形眼镜，通常用复数 contacts
senses.meaning_en: a contact lens, usually in the plural contacts
senses.english_definition: Contacts are small lenses that you wear directly on your eyes to help you see clearly.
senses.collocation_en: wear contacts; take out your contacts
senses.collocation_zh: 戴隐形眼镜；摘下隐形眼镜
senses.sentence_en: I usually wear contacts when I play tennis.
senses.sentence_zh: 我打网球时通常戴隐形眼镜。

senses.meaning_en: to communicate with someone
senses.english_definition: If you contact someone, you telephone them, write to them, or communicate with them in another way.
senses.collocation_en: contact customer service; contact someone directly
senses.collocation_zh: 联系客服；直接联系某人
senses.sentence_en: Please contact me if you need more information.
senses.sentence_zh: 如果你需要更多信息，请联系我。

senses.meaning_zh: 接触；触及，尤用于技术语境
senses.meaning_en: to physically touch something, especially in technical contexts
senses.english_definition: If one object contacts another, it physically touches it.
senses.collocation_en: contact the surface; contact the skin
senses.collocation_zh: 接触表面；接触皮肤
senses.sentence_en: The sensor works only when it contacts the skin.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个传感器只有在接触皮肤时才会工作。

etymology_story.zh: 经法语或直接源自拉丁语 contactus，意为“触碰、接触”，与 contingere“触及”有关，其历史构件包含 con- 的“共同”义和表示“触碰”的词根。英语先用它表示身体接触，后来扩展为人与人的联络，并发展出“联系某人”的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: The word came through French or directly from Latin contactus, meaning “a touching,” related to contingere, “to touch,” with historical elements meaning “together” and “touch.” English extended physical touching to communication between people and later developed the verb meaning “communicate with someone.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 contact 通常作为完整词基使用，不宜机械拆成现代前缀和独立单词；名词与动词通过零派生共用词形。常见屈折形式为 contacts、contacted、contacting；派生词包括 contactless（无接触的）、contactable（可联系到的）、uncontactable（联系不到的），相关复合表达包括 contact lens（隐形眼镜）、contact details（联系方式）和 contact tracing（接触者追踪）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, contact normally functions as a whole base rather than a freely separable prefix-plus-word formation; the noun and verb share their form through conversion. Common inflections are contacts, contacted, and contacting; derivatives include contactless, contactable, and uncontactable, while related compounds include contact lens, contact details, and contact tracing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: touch（触碰）侧重身体或物体直接相碰；communicate（交流、沟通）侧重信息传递，常涉及互动；get in touch（取得联系）侧重发起联络，而 contact 可直接接表示人的宾语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Touch emphasizes physical touching; communicate emphasizes the exchange or transmission of information; get in touch emphasizes initiating communication, while contact can take a person directly as its object.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“碰到一起”记起：物体碰到一起是接触，人通过信息碰到一起是联系。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “touch together”: objects touch physically, while people make contact through communication.

usage_note: response to 后接所回应的人或事；response 也可指身体或行为反应，不只是一句话。

senses.meaning_en: an answer or reply
senses.english_definition: A response is something you say or write as an answer to a question, message, or request.
senses.collocation_en: a response to a question; receive a response
senses.collocation_zh: 对问题的回答；收到答复
senses.sentence_en: I sent an email yesterday but have not received a response.
senses.sentence_zh: 我昨天发了一封电子邮件，但还没有收到答复。

senses.meaning_zh: 反应；情绪或生理上的反应
senses.meaning_en: an emotional or physical reaction
senses.english_definition: A response is a feeling or physical change caused by something that happens or affects you.
senses.collocation_en: an emotional response; an immune response
senses.collocation_zh: 情绪反应；免疫反应
senses.sentence_en: The film produced a strong emotional response in the audience.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部电影引起了观众强烈的情绪反应。

senses.meaning_en: an action taken because of an event or situation
senses.english_definition: A response is an action that someone takes to deal with an event, problem, or situation.
senses.collocation_en: an emergency response; in response to something
senses.collocation_zh: 应急响应；为应对某事
senses.sentence_en: The company increased production in response to rising demand.
senses.sentence_zh: 为应对不断增长的需求，公司增加了产量。

etymology_story.zh: 经古法语源自拉丁语 responsum，意为“回答”，它来自 respondere“回答、作出回应”。这个拉丁动词历史上由 re-“回、回应”和 spondere“郑重承诺”构成，英语中的意义后来扩展到行为、生理和情绪反应。
etymology_story.en: Response came through Old French from Latin responsum, “an answer,” derived from respondere, “to answer.” The Latin verb historically combines re-, “back,” with spondere, “to pledge solemnly,” and English later extended the noun to behavioral, physical, and emotional reactions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 response 是完整名词词基，复数为 responses；它与 respond（回应）属于同一词族，但并非通过现代规则给 respond 简单添加后缀而成。主要词族包括 responds、responded、responding、responder（应答者、救援人员）、respondent（答卷人、应诉人）、responsive（反应积极的、灵敏的）、responsively（反应积极地）、responsiveness（响应能力）、unresponsive（无反应的）和 unresponsiveness（无反应）；response 与 responsive 体现 respons- 这一共同词干。
morphology_enriched.en: Response is a whole noun base in modern English, with the plural responses; it belongs to the family of respond but is not formed by simply adding a productive modern suffix to respond. Its main family includes responds, responded, responding, responder, respondent, responsive, responsively, responsiveness, unresponsive, and unresponsiveness; response and responsive share the stem respons-.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: answer（回答、答案）侧重解决问题或提供所需信息；reply（答复）侧重对话、邮件等交流中的回话；reaction（反应）范围更广，常指情绪、生理或即时行为，未必包含有意识的答复。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Answer emphasizes supplying information or resolving a question; reply emphasizes a return message in communication; reaction covers emotional, physical, or immediate behavioral effects and need not involve a deliberate reply.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“回应回来”：问题来了给答复，刺激来了有反应，事情发生了作应对。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to “something comes back”: a question gets an answer, a stimulus produces a reaction, and an event prompts action.

senses.meaning_en: a firm or forceful request
senses.english_definition: A demand is a firm request for something that someone believes they have a right to receive.
senses.collocation_en: make a demand; a demand for an apology
senses.collocation_zh: 提出要求；要求道歉
senses.sentence_en: The workers repeated their demand for higher pay.

senses.meaning_en: the need or desire for goods or services
senses.english_definition: Demand is the amount of a product or service that people want and are willing and able to buy.
senses.collocation_en: consumer demand; supply and demand
senses.collocation_zh: 消费者需求；供给与需求

senses.meaning_zh: 对时间、精力或资源的要求，常用复数 demands

senses.english_definition: The demands of an activity are the time, effort, skills, or resources that it requires.

senses.meaning_en: to ask for something firmly or forcefully
senses.english_definition: If you demand something, you ask for it firmly because you believe you should have it.

senses.collocation_zh: 要求解释；要求退款

senses.meaning_en: to require something as necessary
senses.english_definition: If a task or situation demands something, you need that thing in order to deal with it successfully.
senses.collocation_en: demand attention; demand considerable skill
senses.collocation_zh: 需要关注；需要相当高的技能
senses.sentence_en: This kind of work demands patience and accuracy.
senses.sentence_zh: 这类工作需要耐心和准确性。

etymology_story.zh: 经古法语 demander 源自拉丁语 demandare，原意为“交托、委托”，由起加强作用的 de- 和 mandare“委托、命令”构成。词义在法语中发展为“询问、请求”，进入英语后进一步形成“坚决要求”和经济上的“需求”等意义。
etymology_story.en: Demand came through Old French demander from Latin demandare, “to entrust or commission,” combining an intensive de- with mandare, “to entrust or order.” Its meaning developed into “ask or request” in French and later included forceful requests and economic demand in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 demand 是完整词基，名词和动词通过零派生共用词形，不应按现代英语拆作 de- 加 mand。常见屈折形式为 demands、demanded、demanding；形容词 demanding 表示“要求高的、费力的”，undemanding 表示“要求不高的、轻松的”；常见复合形式包括 on-demand（按需提供的）、demand-driven（需求驱动的）和 demand-led（需求主导的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Demand is a whole modern English base used as both noun and verb through conversion; it should not be analyzed as a productive English de- plus mand formation. Common inflections are demands, demanded, and demanding; the adjective demanding means “requiring much effort or attention,” while undemanding means “requiring little effort”; common compounds include on-demand, demand-driven, and demand-led.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: request（请求）通常较礼貌，允许对方拒绝；require（需要、要求）侧重规则、条件或实际必要性；insist（坚持要求）侧重态度坚定、不肯让步，常接 on 或 that 从句。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Request is usually more polite and leaves room for refusal; require emphasizes rules, conditions, or practical necessity; insist emphasizes firmness and unwillingness to give way, commonly followed by on or a that-clause.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“非要不可”：人非要得到，就是强烈要求；任务非有不可，就是需要；市场想买，就是需求。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “must have”: a person demands something, a task demands a skill, and a market shows demand for a product.

senses.meaning_en: to be real or present
senses.english_definition: If something exists, it is real or is present in the world.
senses.collocation_en: actually exist; no longer exist
senses.collocation_zh: 确实存在；不再存在
senses.sentence_en: There is no evidence that such a creature exists.
senses.sentence_zh: 没有证据表明这种生物存在。

senses.meaning_zh: 存在于；处于某种状态或条件下
senses.meaning_en: to be present in a particular place, form, or condition
senses.english_definition: If something exists in a particular place, form, or condition, that is where or how it is present.
senses.collocation_en: exist in different forms; exist between groups
senses.collocation_zh: 以不同形式存在；存在于群体之间

senses.meaning_en: to stay alive, especially with limited resources
senses.english_definition: If someone exists on a small amount of money or food, they manage to stay alive with only that amount.
senses.collocation_en: exist on very little money; barely exist
senses.collocation_zh: 靠很少的钱生活；勉强生存
senses.sentence_en: It is difficult to exist on such a small income.
senses.sentence_zh: 靠这么少的收入很难维持生活。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 exsistere，也写作 existere，意为“显现、出现、存在”，由 ex-“向外”和 sistere“使站立、站定”构成，传入英语时也受到法语 exister 的影响。从“站出来、显现出来”逐渐发展为“确实存在”，并延伸出“维持生存”的用法。
etymology_story.en: Exist derives from Latin exsistere, also spelled existere, “to emerge, appear, or exist,” combining ex-, “out,” with sistere, “to cause to stand or take a stand,” with French exister also influencing its entry into English. The idea of emerging into view developed into actual existence and, later, maintaining life.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 exist 通常作为完整动词词基使用；ex- 与 sist- 的分析属于历史构词，sist 不是独立的现代英语单词。常见屈折形式为 exists、existed、existing；主要词族包括 existence（存在）、existent（存在的）、nonexistent（不存在的）、nonexistence（不存在）、existential（关于存在的）、existentially（从存在角度）、existentialism（存在主义）、existentialist（存在主义者或存在主义的），以及 coexist（共存）、coexistence（共存）和 coexistent（共存的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Exist normally functions as a whole modern verb base; ex- plus sist- is a historical analysis, and sist is not an independent modern English word. Common inflections are exists, existed, and existing; the main family includes existence, existent, nonexistent, nonexistence, existential, existentially, existentialism, existentialist, coexist, coexistence, and coexistent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: be（是、存在）最基本，表达存在时通常用于 there is/are 等结构；occur（发生、出现）强调事件发生或某物出现；survive（生存、幸存）强调克服危险或困难而继续活着。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Be is the most basic verb and commonly expresses existence in constructions such as there is or there are; occur emphasizes an event happening or something being found; survive emphasizes remaining alive despite danger or difficulty.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史画面是“站出来”：站出来成为现实，就是存在；艰难地继续站着，就是维持生存。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture something “standing out into reality”: it exists; if it keeps standing through hardship, it continues to live.

senses.meaning_en: to willingly receive something offered

senses.collocation_en: accept an offer; accept the terms
