etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 sang、song，与 sing“唱”同属日耳曼语历史词族。它原本指歌唱或唱出的内容，后来也广泛用于鸟类悦耳的鸣叫。
etymology_story.en: Song comes from Old English sang or song and belongs to the same historical Germanic word family as sing. It referred to singing or something sung and also came to describe the musical calls of birds.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 song 是不可再拆分的基本名词，复数为 songs。常见构词：song + writer → songwriter“歌曲创作者”；song + writing → songwriting“歌曲创作”；song + book → songbook“歌集”；song + bird → songbird“鸣禽”；song + -ster → songster“歌手、善鸣的鸟”；song + -stress → songstress“女歌手，文学用语”；另有 singsong“单调的吟唱声；集体唱歌”。sing、singer、singing、sang、sung 属于历史相关词族，并非由现代 song 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, song is a simple noun with no productive internal division; its plural is songs. Common formations include song + writer → songwriter, song + writing → songwriting, song + book → songbook, song + bird → songbird, song + -ster → songster, and song + -stress → songstress, a literary word for a female singer; singsong is another related compound. Sing, singer, singing, sang, and sung belong to the historically related family rather than being direct modern derivatives of song.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tune“曲调”侧重旋律，不一定有歌词；ballad“叙事歌谣、抒情慢歌”是一类歌曲；track“录音曲目”侧重专辑或播放列表中的一个音频项目，也可能是纯器乐。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tune emphasizes a melody and need not include words; ballad names a particular kind of song, often narrative or slow and emotional; track refers to an individual recording on an album or playlist and may be instrumental.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sing 是“唱”，song 是“唱出来的歌”；两词有历史亲缘。
mnemonic_anchor.en: You sing a song: the action and its musical result belong to the same historical family.

senses.meaning_zh: 周末；通常指星期六和星期日，有时包括星期五晚上
senses.meaning_en: the end-of-week period, usually Saturday and Sunday, sometimes including Friday evening
senses.english_definition: The weekend is the part of the week when many people do not work, usually Saturday and Sunday.
senses.collocation_en: at the weekend; on weekends
senses.collocation_zh: 在周末，常见于英式英语；每逢周末，常见于美式英语
senses.sentence_en: We usually visit our grandparents at the weekend.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们通常在周末去看望祖父母。

senses.meaning_en: to spend a weekend somewhere
senses.english_definition: If you weekend somewhere, you spend the weekend there.
senses.collocation_en: weekend in the country; weekend at the coast
senses.collocation_zh: 在乡下度周末；在海滨度周末
senses.sentence_en: They often weekend in the country during the summer.
senses.sentence_zh: 夏天，他们经常去乡下度周末。

etymology_story.zh: 由 week“星期”和 end“末尾”合成，最初按字面表示一周的末尾。随着固定周末休息制度的发展，它逐渐成为一段工作之外的休息时间的名称，并产生“度周末”的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Weekend combines week and end and originally referred literally to the end of a week. As regular time off at the end of the working week developed, it became the name of that leisure period and also acquired the verb meaning 'spend a weekend.'

morphology_enriched.zh: week + end → weekend，是名词复合词，也可通过零派生作动词。词形包括 weekends、weekended、weekending；weekend + -er → weekender“外出度周末的人；周末旅行包”。weekend job“周末工作”等结构中的 weekend 通常按名词作定语分析，无须另立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Week + end → weekend is a compound noun that also becomes a verb through conversion. Its forms include weekends, weekended, and weekending; weekend + -er → weekender means a person spending a weekend away or a bag for a short trip. In expressions such as weekend job, weekend is normally analyzed as an attributive noun rather than a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: time off“休息时间”不限于周末；break“休息、短假”强调暂时中断工作或活动；short break“短途假期”通常指短暂出游，也不一定在周末。它们均不是 weekend 的完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Time off means time away from work on any day; break emphasizes an interruption in work or activity; short break usually means a brief holiday that need not fall on a weekend. None is an exact synonym of weekend.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: week 的 end：一周到了末尾；作动词就是“在那里过周末”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The end of the week is the weekend; to weekend somewhere is to spend that period there.

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 dēad，属于与 death“死亡”和 die“死”相关的日耳曼语历史词族。由“不再活着”引申为“不运转、无生气、无感觉”，又在固定搭配中发展出“完全、正好”的强调意义。
etymology_story.en: Dead comes from Old English dēad and belongs to the Germanic historical family associated with death and die. Its meaning extended from 'no longer alive' to 'not functioning, inactive, or without feeling,' and it developed emphatic uses meaning 'completely' or 'exactly.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代 dead 是基本形容词，不是 die 的规则过去分词；die 的过去式和过去分词均为 died。常见派生：dead + -ness → deadness“死寂、无生气”；dead + -en → deaden“使减弱、使麻木”，其词形有 deadens、deadened、deadening；dead + -ly → deadly“致命的；极其”，deadly → deadliness“致命性”；un- + dead → undead“亡灵的；亡灵”。常见复合词有 deadlock“僵局”、deadlocked“陷入僵局的”、deadpan“面无表情的；面无表情地”、deadweight“自重；累赘”、deadbeat“赖账者；不负责任的人”、deadwood“枯木；冗员”、dead-end“无出路的”及 deadhead“摘除残花；空驶”。death、die、dying 属于历史相关词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern dead is a basic adjective, not the regular past participle of die; the past tense and past participle of die are both died. Common derivatives include dead + -ness → deadness; dead + -en → deaden, with deadens, deadened, and deadening; dead + -ly → deadly, with deadliness; and un- + dead → undead. Common compounds include deadlock, deadlocked, deadpan, deadweight, deadbeat, deadwood, dead-end, and deadhead. Death, die, and dying belong to the historically related family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: deceased“已故的”正式而委婉，主要用于人；lifeless“无生命的、毫无生气的”强调看不到生命或活力，有时并不表示真的死亡；defunct“不复存在或不再运作的”主要用于机构、制度或设备。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deceased is formal and respectful and mainly describes people; lifeless emphasizes an absence of visible life or energy and does not always mean literally dead; defunct usually describes an organization, system, or device that no longer exists or operates.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“生命停止”联想“运转停止、活力消失”；dead tired 则把“累”的程度推到极点。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with life stopping, then extend to machines stopping and energy disappearing; dead tired pushes tiredness to its limit.

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语借自古法语 encoragier，意为“使有勇气”，其中 courage 最终与拉丁语 cor“心”有关。由“给人勇气”扩展为支持行动、促进发展，甚至无意中助长某种结果。
etymology_story.en: Encourage entered Middle English from Old French encoragier, meaning 'give courage'; courage ultimately relates to Latin cor, meaning 'heart.' Giving someone courage broadened into supporting action, promoting development, and even unintentionally helping a result occur.

morphology_enriched.zh: en-“使具有、赋予”+ courage“勇气”→ encourage“使有勇气”。词形：encourages、encouraged、encouraging；加 -ing 时去掉词尾不发音的 e。encourage + -ment → encouragement“鼓励”，保留 e；encouraging 可作形容词“令人鼓舞的”，encouraged 可作形容词“受到鼓舞的”；encouraging + -ly → encouragingly“令人鼓舞地”；encourage + -er → encourager“鼓励者”。相关词族还包括 courage“勇气”、courageous“勇敢的”、courageously“勇敢地”、courageousness“勇敢”，以及 discourage“使泄气；劝阻”、discouragement“泄气；阻碍”、discouraged“灰心的”、discouraging“令人泄气的”、discouragingly“令人泄气地”。
morphology_enriched.en: En-, meaning 'give or cause to have,' + courage → encourage. Inflected forms are encourages, encouraged, and encouraging; the silent final e is dropped before -ing. Encourage + -ment → encouragement retains the e; encouraging and encouraged also function as adjectives; encouraging + -ly → encouragingly; encourage + -er → encourager. The related family includes courage, courageous, courageously, courageousness, discourage, discouragement, discouraged, discouraging, and discouragingly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: support“支持”强调提供帮助或认可；motivate“激励”强调产生行动的动力；reassure“使安心”强调消除担忧。encourage 侧重增强信心或推动某种行为发生。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Support emphasizes help or approval; motivate emphasizes creating a reason or drive to act; reassure emphasizes reducing worry. Encourage focuses on building confidence or making an action more likely.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: en- + courage：把勇气给出去，就能“鼓励”一个人、“促进”一件事。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Give courage: strengthen a person, then extend the idea to helping an activity develop.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 prōtegere“在前面遮盖、庇护”的词干 prōtect-，由 prō-“在前面”和 tegere“覆盖”组成。具体的“遮挡”意义后来扩展为保护人身安全、维护权利以及保护产业。
etymology_story.en: Protect comes from prōtect-, the Latin stem associated with prōtegere, meaning 'cover in front or shelter,' formed from prō-, 'in front,' and tegere, 'cover.' Physical shielding broadened into preserving safety, defending rights, and sheltering industries from competition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 protect 作为完整动词词基；历史结构可分析为 pro-“在前面”+ tect“覆盖”，但 tect 在现代英语中不是独立自由词。词形：protects、protected、protecting；protect + -ion → protection“保护”；protect + -ive → protective“保护性的”，进一步有 protectively“保护地”、protectiveness“保护欲；保护性”；protect + -or → protector“保护者；防护器”，另有 protectress“女性保护者，少用”。相关扩展包括 protectorate“保护国；受保护领地”、protectionism“贸易保护主义”、protectionist“贸易保护主义者；贸易保护主义的”、unprotected“未受保护的”、overprotect“过度保护”、overprotection“过度保护”、overprotective“过度保护的”及 overprotectiveness“过度保护倾向”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats protect as a complete verb base. Historically, it contains pro-, 'in front,' and tect, 'cover,' but tect is not an independent modern English word. Inflections are protects, protected, and protecting. Derivatives include protect + -ion → protection; protect + -ive → protective, with protectively and protectiveness; and protect + -or → protector, with the uncommon feminine form protectress. Related formations include protectorate, protectionism, protectionist, unprotected, overprotect, overprotection, overprotective, and overprotectiveness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: defend“保卫、辩护”强调抵抗攻击或指责；guard“守卫、看护”强调警戒和监护；safeguard“保障、维护”强调预防风险，常用于权利、利益和制度。protect 是使免受伤害或损失的通用词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Defend emphasizes resisting attack or criticism; guard emphasizes watching over something or controlling access; safeguard emphasizes preventing risks, often to rights, interests, or systems. Protect is the general word for keeping someone or something safe from harm or loss.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史词根图像：在前面加一层覆盖物，把伤害挡住，就是 protect。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a covering placed in front: it blocks harm and keeps what is behind it safe.

etymology_story.zh: damage 经古法语 damage 传入英语，最终源于表示“损失、损害”的拉丁语 damnum；英语动词也与同源的古法语动词有关。其意义从损失或伤害扩展到对物体、健康、声誉等的损害，复数 damages 则专指损害赔偿金。
etymology_story.en: Damage entered English through Old French damage and ultimately comes from Latin damnum, meaning “loss” or “harm”; the English verb is also connected with a related Old French verb. Its uses cover harm to objects, health, and reputation, while the plural damages developed the specialized meaning of financial compensation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 damage 是不可再作常用词缀分析的词基，不宜拆成 dam + -age。词族：damage（损害，名词和动词）；damage + -s → damages（损害赔偿金，或动词第三人称单数）；damage + -d → damaged（受损的；过去式和过去分词，保留 e）；damage 去 e + -ing → damaging（造成损害的；现在分词）；un- + damaged → undamaged（未受损的）；damaging + -ly → damagingly（有害地）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, damage is a base rather than a transparent combination of dam and -age. Family: damage (noun and verb); damage + -s → damages (compensation, or the third-person singular verb); damage + -d → damaged (past tense, past participle, and adjective, retaining e); damage minus final e + -ing → damaging (present participle and adjective); un- + damaged → undamaged; damaging + -ly → damagingly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: harm（伤害）范围最广，可涉及身体、利益或福祉；damage（损害）强调状况、价值或功能变差；ruin（毁坏）通常表示严重破坏，达到难以恢复或无法使用的程度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Harm broadly covers injury to health, interests, or well-being; damage emphasizes a reduction in condition, value, or function; ruin usually suggests destruction so severe that recovery or normal use becomes difficult.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“损失”这一历史核心：东西失去完好状态是 damage；为这种损失支付的钱是 damages。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to its historical idea of loss: damage is the loss of good condition; damages are money paid for that loss.

etymology_story.zh: imagine 经古法语 imaginer 来自拉丁语 imaginari，意为“在心中形成形象”，其基础是表示“形象、肖像”的 imago。由“形成心理图像”进一步发展出“设想、猜想”以及“误以为”的用法。
etymology_story.en: Imagine came through Old French imaginer from Latin imaginari, meaning “to form a mental picture,” based on imago, “image” or “likeness.” The idea of forming an inner image extended to considering possibilities, making suppositions, and mistakenly believing something is real.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语以 imagine 为词基，不宜拆成 im- + agine。词族：imagine + -d → imagined（想象出来的；过去式和过去分词，保留 e）；去 e + -ing → imagining（正在想象）；去 e + -ation → imagination（想象力；想象）；去 e + -able → imaginable（可以想象的）；un- + imaginable → unimaginable（难以想象的）；imaginably / unimaginably（可想象地／难以想象地）；共同词干 imagin- 构成 imaginary（虚构的）、imaginative（富有想象力的）、unimaginative（缺乏想象力的）、imaginatively（富有想象力地）、unimaginatively（缺乏想象力地）；re- + imagine → reimagine（重新构想），另有 reimagined、reimagining。image（形象；图像）是同源相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat imagine as the modern base, not as im- + agine. Family: imagine + -d → imagined (retaining e); remove final e before -ing → imagining, -ation → imagination, and -able → imaginable; un- + imaginable → unimaginable; adverbs imaginably and unimaginably. The shared stem imagin- also appears in imaginary, imaginative, unimaginative, imaginatively, and unimaginatively. Re- + imagine → reimagine, with reimagined and reimagining. Image is an etymologically related word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: picture（在脑中描绘）强调清晰的视觉形象；envisage（设想）常指对未来情景或计划的构想；suppose（猜想）强调在证据不足时作出判断，对应 imagine 的“认为”义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Picture emphasizes a visual mental image; envisage often concerns a possible future situation or plan; suppose emphasizes a tentative judgment and corresponds to imagine when it means “think something is probably true.”

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 image“图像”和 imagine“想象”连起来：在脑中放一幅图，再由这幅图去设想或猜想。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect image with imagine: put an image in your mind, then use it to picture possibilities or make a guess.

senses.meaning_zh: 下午；中午之后到傍晚之前的一段时间

etymology_story.zh: afternoon 起源于中古英语中表示“中午之后”的表达，由 after 和 noon 逐渐结合为一个词。它一直保留透明的时间意义，指中午之后、傍晚之前的时段。
etymology_story.en: Afternoon developed from a Middle English expression meaning “after noon,” with after and noon gradually combining into one word. It retains this transparent time meaning: the period after midday and before evening.

morphology_enriched.zh: 复合构词：after（在……之后）+ noon（中午）→ afternoon（下午）；afternoon + -s → afternoons（多个下午）。没有常用的派生动词或形容词；afternoon tea（下午茶）中的 afternoon 是名词作定语，Good afternoon（下午好）是问候语。
morphology_enriched.en: Compound formation: after + noon → afternoon; afternoon + -s → afternoons. There is no common derived verb or adjective; afternoon is a noun used attributively in afternoon tea, while Good afternoon is a greeting.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有与 afternoon 范围完全相同的常用单词；midday / noon（正午）指十二点或其前后的时间，evening（傍晚；晚上）指下午之后的时段，daytime（白天）则涵盖更长的日间时间。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common single-word synonym with exactly the same range: midday or noon identifies twelve o'clock or the period around it, evening follows the afternoon, and daytime covers the broader period of daylight.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: after + noon：过了正午，就是下午。
mnemonic_anchor.en: After + noon: the afternoon comes after midday.

senses.meaning_zh: 估计；估算；根据已有信息大致判断数量、价值或程度
senses.meaning_en: to judge an approximate amount, value, or extent using available information
senses.english_definition: If you estimate something, you use the information available to judge its approximate amount, value, or extent.
senses.collocation_en: estimate the cost; estimate that

senses.meaning_zh: 估计；估算结果；对数量、价值或程度作出的大致判断
senses.meaning_en: an approximate judgment of an amount, value, or extent
senses.english_definition: An estimate is an approximate judgment about how much something is or how large, valuable, or extensive it is.
senses.collocation_en: a rough estimate; a conservative estimate
senses.collocation_zh: 粗略估计；保守估计
senses.sentence_en: A rough estimate puts the crowd at around five thousand.
senses.sentence_zh: 粗略估计，现场人群约有五千人。

senses.meaning_zh: 估价；费用预估；对某项工作所需费用作出的事先估计
senses.meaning_en: an advance calculation of the likely cost of a job or service
senses.english_definition: An estimate is a statement of how much a particular job or service is likely to cost.
senses.collocation_en: get an estimate; a written estimate
senses.collocation_zh: 获取估价；书面费用预估
senses.sentence_en: The builder gave us a written estimate for the work.
senses.sentence_zh: 建筑商给了我们一份这项工程的书面费用预估。

etymology_story.zh: estimate 源于拉丁语 aestimare，意为“评估价值、估量”，英语动词的形式与其过去分词 aestimatus 有关。它从评定价值发展为大致判断数量、费用等，后来也用作表示估算结果的名词。
etymology_story.en: Estimate derives from Latin aestimare, “to value” or “to assess,” with the English verb's form reflecting the Latin past participle aestimatus. The meaning broadened from assessing worth to judging quantities and costs approximately, and the word also came to function as a noun for the resulting assessment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语以 estimate 为词基，常见词尾 -ate 在动词中读 /eɪt/，名词词尾则弱读 /ət/。词族：estimate + -d → estimated（估计的；过去式和过去分词，保留 e）；去 e + -ing → estimating（估算）；去 e + -ion → estimation（估计；评价）；去 e + -or → estimator（估算者；估算工具）；under- + estimate → underestimate（低估，名词和动词）及 underestimation（低估）；over- + estimate → overestimate（高估，名词和动词）及 overestimation（高估）；re- + estimate → reestimate / re-estimate（重新估算）及 reestimation / re-estimation（重新估算的过程）。相关词还有 estimable（值得尊敬的）、inestimable（无法估量的；极宝贵的）和 inestimably（无法估量地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat estimate as the modern base; its ending is pronounced /eɪt/ in the verb but reduced to /ət/ in the noun. Family: estimate + -d → estimated (retaining e); remove final e before -ing → estimating, -ion → estimation, and -or → estimator. Prefix formations include under- + estimate → underestimate and underestimation; over- + estimate → overestimate and overestimation; re- + estimate → reestimate or re-estimate, with reestimation or re-estimation. Related words include estimable, inestimable, and inestimably.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: assess（评估）强调综合判断价值、状况或影响；calculate（计算）强调按数字或方法求出结果，通常比 estimate 更精确；guess（猜测）所依据的信息通常比 estimate 更少。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Assess emphasizes evaluating worth, condition, or impact; calculate emphasizes working out a result through numbers or a method, usually more precisely than estimate; guess typically relies on less supporting information than estimate.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“评个大概”：动作 estimate 的结尾读 /meɪt/，估算结果这个名词的结尾弱读 /mət/。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “assess approximately”: the action ends in /meɪt/, while the noun naming the result ends in the weaker /mət/.

etymology_story.zh: photo 是十九世纪出现的 photograph 缩略形式，后来也被用作非正式动词。photograph 的构词成分源于希腊语中表示“光”和“书写、描画”的词，合起来表达“用光记录图像”的概念。
etymology_story.en: Photo arose in the nineteenth century as a shortened form of photograph and later also gained an informal verbal use. Photograph combines elements derived from Greek words for “light” and “writing” or “drawing,” expressing the idea of recording an image with light.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：photograph（照片；拍照）截短 → photo；名词转作动词，无需添加词缀。photo + -s → photos（照片的复数；不加 -es，也可作动词第三人称单数）；photo + -ed → photoed（拍了照）；photo + -ing → photoing（正在拍照）。扩展词族包括 photograph（照片；拍照）、photography（摄影）、photographer（摄影师）、photographic（摄影的）、photographically（以摄影方式）；photo album（相册）、photo editor（照片编辑工具或图片编辑人员）是常见复合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: photograph is clipped to photo; the noun also becomes a verb without an added affix. Photo + -s → photos (the noun plural, without -es, and the third-person singular verb); photo + -ed → photoed; photo + -ing → photoing. The extended family includes photograph, photography, photographer, photographic, and photographically. Common compounds include photo album and photo editor.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: photograph（照片；拍照）与 photo 基本同义，语体更正式，作动词时也更常用；picture（图片；照片）范围更广，还可指绘画等图像；snapshot（快照）强调随手、快速拍摄的照片。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Photograph has essentially the same meaning but is more formal and is also the more usual verb; picture is broader and can include paintings and other images; snapshot suggests a photograph taken quickly and casually.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: photo 是 photograph 的短版：把“用光记录的图像”压缩成日常说的“照片”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Photo is the short version of photograph: an image recorded with light becomes an everyday “photo.”

senses.meaning_zh: 上下文；帮助理解词句的前后文

senses.english_definition: The context of a word or passage is the language around it that helps you understand its meaning.

senses.meaning_en: the circumstances surrounding an event or situation
senses.english_definition: The context of an event or situation is the set of circumstances that helps explain it.

senses.sentence_en: We need to understand the historical context of the decision.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们需要了解作出这一决定的历史背景。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 contextus，原指“编织在一起、连接”，与 con-（一起）和 texere（编织）有关。词义由相互连接的文字扩展为帮助理解话语、事件或处境的周围信息。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Latin contextus, meaning a weaving together or connection, associated with con- meaning together and texere meaning to weave. Its meaning developed from connected language to the surrounding information that helps explain words, events, or situations.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 context 是整体词干，不宜把历史成分直接当作现代自由词素。词族：context + -s → contexts；context + -ual → contextual（上下文的、背景的）；contextual + -ly → contextually（结合上下文地）；contextual + -ize → contextualize（置于背景中解释），再加 -ation → contextualization（背景化）；加 de- → decontextualize（使脱离背景）、decontextualization（去背景化）；加 re- → recontextualize（置于新背景中解释）、recontextualization（重新背景化）。相关动词和名词也有 -ise、-isation 拼写。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, context functions as a whole stem; its historical components are not ordinary free-standing modern morphemes. Family: context + -s → contexts; context + -ual → contextual; contextual + -ly → contextually; contextual + -ize → contextualize, with contextualization as its noun; de- forms decontextualize and decontextualization; re- forms recontextualize and recontextualization. The corresponding -ise and -isation spellings are also used.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: background（背景）侧重先前事实和背景资料；circumstances（情况、条件）侧重事件发生时的具体条件；setting（环境、场景）侧重时间、地点或社会环境。context 强调这些周边信息如何影响理解。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Background emphasizes prior facts and supporting information; circumstances emphasizes the particular conditions surrounding an event; setting emphasizes its time, place, or social environment. Context emphasizes how surrounding information shapes interpretation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把意义“编织在一起”：词句靠上下文，事件靠背景。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Meaning is woven together: words need surrounding language, and events need surrounding circumstances.

etymology_story.zh: 由 news（新闻）和 paper（纸张、出版物）合成，17 世纪已用于指刊载新闻的印刷出版物。后来也用于指报社及其数字版新闻出版物。
etymology_story.en: The compound combines news with paper and was used in the seventeenth century for a printed publication carrying news. It later also came to denote the publishing organization and its digital publication.

morphology_enriched.zh: news + paper → newspaper，是复合名词；其中 news 虽以 -s 结尾，通常仍是不可数名词。词族：newspaper + -s → newspapers（报纸的复数）；newspaper + man → newspaperman（报人、男记者），复数 newspapermen；newspaper + woman → newspaperwoman（女报人、女记者），复数 newspaperwomen；newspapering（报业工作，较少见）。newspaper 的定语用法，如 newspaper article（报纸文章），通常仍按名词修饰名词处理。
morphology_enriched.en: News + paper → newspaper, a compound noun; news is normally uncountable despite its final -s. Family: newspaper + -s → newspapers; newspaper + man → newspaperman, plural newspapermen; newspaper + woman → newspaperwoman, plural newspaperwomen; newspapering means newspaper work and is less common. Attributive uses such as newspaper article are normally treated as noun modifiers.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: paper 是 newspaper 的常用非正式说法，也可泛指纸张或论文；journal 常指专业期刊，部分报纸也以此命名；the press 集体指报刊新闻界，不能通常用来指一份具体报纸。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Paper is a common informal equivalent of newspaper but can also mean writing material or an academic article; journal often means a specialist periodical, though some newspapers use it in their names; the press refers collectively to news publications or journalists rather than one particular newspaper.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: news 装进 paper：从纸上的新闻，联想到整份报纸及其数字版。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Put news into paper: think of the whole news publication, including its digital edition.

etymology_story.zh: 经法语 crédit，并受意大利语 credito 影响，追溯至拉丁语 creditum（借出或托付之物），其来源是 credere（相信、信任）。对偿还的信任发展出金融义，而相信某人的贡献或价值又发展出认可、功劳和署名等义。
etymology_story.en: It came through French crédit, with influence from Italian credito, ultimately from Latin creditum, something entrusted or lent, from credere, to believe or trust. Trust in repayment produced the financial meanings, while belief in someone's contribution or worth developed into recognition, praise, and acknowledgment.

morphology_enriched.zh: credit 在现代英语中是整体词干，可直接兼作名词和动词。词族：credits、credited、crediting；credit + -or → creditor（债权人）；credit + -able → creditable（值得称赞的），派生 creditably（值得称赞地）、creditability（值得称赞的性质，较少见）；credit + worthy → creditworthy（信用可靠的），再加 -ness → creditworthiness（信用可靠程度）；dis- + credit → discredit（使失去信誉；不可信），以及 discredited（名誉受损的）、discreditable（丢脸的）、discreditably（丢脸地）；un- + credited → uncredited（未署名的、未获认可的）。acc redit 不宜按任意字母拆分；相关词 accredit（认可、授权）及 accredited、accreditation 属同源词族，credible（可信的）、credibility（可信度）、credence（相信）也与拉丁语 credere 同源。
morphology_enriched.en: Credit is a whole modern stem used as both noun and verb. Family: credits, credited, crediting; credit + -or → creditor; credit + -able → creditable, with creditably and the less common creditability; credit + worthy → creditworthy, with creditworthiness; dis- + credit → discredit, with discredited, discreditable, and discreditably; un- + credited → uncredited. Accredit should not be divided into arbitrary letter sequences; accredit, accredited, and accreditation belong to the related family, while credible, credibility, and credence also share the Latin ancestor credere.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: recognition（认可）最接近“承认贡献”的名词义，但不一定包含称赞；loan（贷款）指具体借出的款项或借贷安排，credit 还可指赊购能力或额度；attribute（归因于）最接近动词的归因义，可用于好坏结果，而 credit 常带肯定贡献的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Recognition is close to the acknowledgment sense but need not imply praise; loan refers to a particular sum lent or lending arrangement, whereas credit can also mean purchasing capacity or a borrowing facility; attribute is close to the attribution verb and applies to good or bad results, while credit often recognizes a positive contribution.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“信任”：信你会还钱，就给信贷；信你有贡献，就记功劳。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with trust: trust repayment and offer credit; trust someone's contribution and give them credit.

senses.meaning_zh: 女儿；父母的女性孩子，不限年龄

etymology_story.zh: 来自古英语 dohtor，属于古老的日耳曼语亲属词，并与其他印欧语言中表示“女儿”的词同源。其亲属含义长期稳定，后来又借“由母体产生”的关系扩展到生物学和核科学术语。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Old English dohtor, an ancient Germanic kinship word related to words for daughter in other Indo-European languages. Its family meaning has remained stable, while the parent–offspring relationship later supplied technical uses in biology and nuclear science.

morphology_enriched.zh: daughter 是不可再作现代词缀分析的基本词，词尾 -er 不是表示人的后缀。词族：daughter + -s → daughters（女儿的复数）；daughter + -ly → daughterly（女儿般的）；daughter + -hood → daughterhood（女儿身份）；daughter + -less → daughterless（没有女儿的）；granddaughter（孙女、外孙女）、great-granddaughter（曾孙女、曾外孙女）、stepdaughter（继女）、goddaughter（教女）、daughter-in-law（儿媳），其复数为 daughters-in-law。
morphology_enriched.en: Daughter is a basic word without a useful modern affix breakdown; its ending -er is not an agent suffix. Family: daughter + -s → daughters; daughter + -ly → daughterly; daughter + -hood → daughterhood; daughter + -less → daughterless; granddaughter, great-granddaughter, stepdaughter, goddaughter, and daughter-in-law, whose plural is daughters-in-law.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: female child（女性孩子）可作解释性近义表达，但单独使用不一定说明亲属关系；offspring（子女、后代）不限性别，语气较正式；girl（女孩）侧重年龄或性别，不能单独表达“某人的女儿”，而 daughter 可指成年女性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Female child is an explanatory near-equivalent but does not necessarily identify a family relationship on its own; offspring is gender-neutral and more formal; girl emphasizes age or gender and does not itself mean someone's daughter, whereas daughter can refer to an adult woman.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 只抓“亲子关系”：女儿可以长大；科学中的 daughter 也表示“由母体产生”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it in the parent–child relationship: a daughter can be an adult, and a scientific daughter comes from a parent.

senses.meaning_zh: 多样性；变化；不单调的状态
senses.meaning_en: diversity or the presence of different things
senses.english_definition: Variety is the presence of different things or experiences that makes something less uniform or repetitive.
senses.collocation_en: add variety; a lack of variety
senses.collocation_zh: 增加变化；缺乏多样性
senses.sentence_en: Try different exercises to add variety to your routine.

senses.meaning_zh: 种类；品种；同一大类中具有特点的一种
senses.meaning_en: a particular type within a broader group
senses.english_definition: A variety of something is a particular type that differs in some way from other types of the same thing.
senses.collocation_en: a variety of reasons; varieties of rice
senses.collocation_zh: 各种原因；水稻品种
senses.sentence_en: This farm grows several varieties of rice.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家农场种植几个水稻品种。

senses.meaning_zh: 综艺娱乐；由歌舞、喜剧等不同节目组成的表演
senses.meaning_en: entertainment consisting of several different kinds of act
senses.english_definition: Variety is entertainment that combines different kinds of performance, such as singing, dancing, and comedy.
senses.collocation_en: a variety show; variety entertainment
senses.collocation_zh: 综艺节目；综艺娱乐
senses.sentence_en: The charity organized a variety show with music, dance, and comedy.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家慈善机构举办了一场包含音乐、舞蹈和喜剧表演的综艺演出。

etymology_story.zh: 经法语 variété 或直接借自拉丁语 varietas（多样、差异），后者来自 varius（多种多样的）。词义既可指不同事物并存的状态，也可指其中一个具体品种，后来还用于包含多类节目的娱乐形式。
etymology_story.en: It entered through French variété or directly from Latin varietas, meaning diversity or difference, from varius, meaning varied. It came to denote both diversity itself and an individual type, and later entertainment combining different kinds of act.

morphology_enriched.zh: variety 是借入的名词，现代学习可将它与 vary（变化）联系，但不宜机械写成生产性的 vary + -ety。屈折变化：variety 的 y 改为 i，再加 -es → varieties；相关词族包括 vary、varies、varied、varying；variation（变化、变体）、variant（变体；不同的）、variable（可变的；变量）、variably（变化不定地）、variability（可变性）、invariable（不变的）、invariably（一贯地）、varietal（品种的；单一品种葡萄酒）。综艺义中的 variety show 通常按名词作定语处理。
morphology_enriched.en: Variety is a borrowed noun. It can usefully be associated with vary, but should not be mechanically analyzed as productive vary + -ety. Its plural changes y to i and adds -es: varieties. The related family includes vary, varies, varied, varying; variation, variant, variable, variably, variability, invariable, invariably, and varietal, meaning relating to a variety or a wine made from a particular grape variety. In variety show, variety is normally treated as an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: diversity（多样性）强调群体或事物之间存在差异；range（范围、系列）强调可供选择的广度；type（类型）侧重某个类别。variety 既能表示多样性，也能表示具体品种，需根据可数性和语境判断。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Diversity emphasizes differences within a group or collection; range emphasizes the breadth of available options; type identifies a particular category. Variety can mean either diversity or an individual kind, with countability and context helping distinguish them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联系 vary“有变化”：变化多，就是多样性；分出来的一种，就是品种。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with vary: many differences create variety, and one distinct form is a variety.

etymology_story.zh: 来自法语 version，最终源于拉丁语 versio，意为“转动、转变”，与 vertere（转动）同源。早期的“翻译”含义体现了把文本转成另一种语言，后来扩展为事物的不同形式及对事件的不同说法。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from French version, ultimately from Latin versio, meaning a turning or transformation, related to vertere, meaning to turn. Its early translation sense involved turning a text into another language; it later broadened to alternative forms and accounts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 version 作为整体词干，不宜机械拆成 ver + sion。常用词形和构词包括 versions（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、versioned（已编定版本的；动词过去式及过去分词）、versioning（版本管理；动词现在分词）、unversioned（未编定版本的）；常见复合词有 version control（版本控制）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, version normally functions as a whole stem rather than a transparent combination of ver and sion. Common forms and formations include versions, versioned, versioning, and unversioned; a common compound is version control.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: edition（版次）侧重出版物的某次发行；variant（变体）强调与其他形式之间的差异；account（叙述）对应事件的描述。version 适用范围更广，既可指产品或作品的版本，也可指某人的说法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Edition emphasizes a particular publication or release; variant emphasizes a differing form; account means a description of events. Version has broader coverage, including forms of products or works and someone's account of what happened.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史词根的“转”：同一内容“转”成另一种形式，就是另一个版本。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical idea of turning: turn the same content into another form, and you have another version.

etymology_story.zh: 源于拉丁语 extendere，由 ex-（向外）和 tendere（伸展、拉紧）构成，基本画面是“向外拉伸”。英语由此发展出延长时间、扩大范围以及把邀请或帮助“向外递出”等含义。
etymology_story.en: Extend comes from Latin extendere, combining ex-, meaning out, with tendere, meaning to stretch. The physical idea of stretching outward developed into making time longer, increasing scope, and offering things such as invitations or help.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语以 extend 为动词词干；ex- + tend 是历史词源分析，不是完全自由的现代构词。词形有 extends、extended、extending；常用派生词有 extendable／extendible（可延长的）、extension（延长；扩展；分机）、extensible（可扩展的）、extensibility（可扩展性）；同源词族还包括 extent（程度；范围）、extensive（广泛的）、extensively（广泛地）和 extensiveness（广泛程度）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English uses extend as a verb stem; ex- plus tend describes its historical structure rather than a fully productive modern formation. Inflections are extends, extended, and extending; common derivatives include extendable or extendible, extension, extensible, and extensibility. The related historical family also includes extent, extensive, extensively, and extensiveness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lengthen（加长）主要强调长度或持续时间增加；expand（扩大）强调体积、规模或范围增加；prolong（延长）专指使时间持续更久，有时暗含拖延。extend 可兼指长度、时间、范围及给予。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lengthen mainly concerns physical length or duration; expand emphasizes greater size, scale, or scope; prolong concerns duration and can suggest an unwelcome delay. Extend covers length, time, scope, and the formal offering of something.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史构词 ex-（向外）+ tend（伸展）：把长度、期限或范围向外拉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical ex- means out and tend means stretch: pull length, time, or scope outward.

etymology_story.zh: 由动词 propose 加名词后缀 -al 构成；propose 经古法语 proposer 传入，历史上与拉丁语 proponere（放到前面、提出）有关。其核心是把想法摆到别人面前供其考虑，求婚则是提出结婚的请求。
etymology_story.en: Proposal was formed from propose with the noun suffix -al; propose came through Old French proposer and is historically connected with Latin proponere, meaning to put forward. The central idea is presenting something for consideration, with the marriage sense presenting a request to marry.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：propose 去掉不发音的词尾 e，再加名词后缀 -al → proposal；复数为 proposals。常用词族包括 propose（提议；求婚）、proposes、proposed、proposing 和 proposer（提议者；求婚者）；proposition（命题；提议）属于历史相关词，不是 proposal 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: propose drops its silent final e and takes the noun suffix -al to form proposal; the plural is proposals. The common family includes propose, proposes, proposed, proposing, and proposer. Proposition is historically related but is not directly derived from proposal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: suggestion（建议）通常较随意，也可只是一点想法；plan（计划）强调行动安排；proposition（提议；主张）常见于商业谈判或论证。proposal 强调正式提出、等待他人考虑或批准的内容。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Suggestion is often less formal and may be only an idea; plan emphasizes intended actions; proposition often occurs in business discussions or arguments. Proposal emphasizes something put forward for consideration or approval.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: propose 是“提出”，proposal 是“提出的内容”：方案或求婚请求。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Propose is the act of putting something forward; a proposal is what you put forward, whether a plan or a request to marry.

etymology_story.zh: 由 profession 加 -al 构成；profession 最终源于拉丁语 professio，意为“公开宣告”，也曾用于公开宣誓加入宗教团体。随着 profession 发展出“需要专门知识的职业”之义，professional 也获得了职业身份、领取报酬和符合专业标准等含义。
etymology_story.en: Professional was formed from profession and -al; profession ultimately comes from Latin professio, meaning a public declaration, and was also used for a public religious commitment. As profession developed the sense of a specialized occupation, professional acquired meanings involving occupational status, paid participation, and standards of skill or conduct.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：profession（专门职业）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ professional；形容词可直接转为名词，表示专业人士或职业选手。常用词族包括 profession、professionals（专业人士的复数）、professionally（专业地；在职业上）、professionalism（专业精神）、professionalize／professionalise（使职业化或专业化）、professionalization／professionalisation（职业化或专业化）、unprofessional（不专业的）、unprofessionally（不专业地）、nonprofessional（非专业的；非专业人士）及 semiprofessional（半职业的；半职业选手）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: profession plus the adjective suffix -al gives professional; the adjective also converts directly into a noun. Common family members include profession, professionals, professionally, professionalism, professionalize or professionalise, professionalization or professionalisation, unprofessional, unprofessionally, nonprofessional, and semiprofessional.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: expert（专家；精通的）强调知识或技能深度，不一定以此谋生；qualified（具备资格的）强调达到资质或能力要求；competent（胜任的）强调足以把工作做好。professional 还可特别强调职业身份、报酬或职业规范。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Expert emphasizes deep knowledge or skill without necessarily implying paid work; qualified emphasizes having the required credentials or abilities; competent emphasizes being able to do a job adequately. Professional can additionally emphasize occupational status, payment, or standards of conduct.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: profession 是“专门职业”；professional 可指“从事这一职业的人”，也可形容“达到这一职业应有的水准”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with profession: a professional works in the field, and professional behavior meets the standards expected in that field.

senses.meaning_zh: 元：美国、加拿大、澳大利亚等国的货币单位；一元硬币或纸币

etymology_story.zh: 经低地德语或荷兰语 daler 一类形式，源于德语 Taler；Taler 是 Joachimstaler 的缩略形式，原指在波希米亚约阿希姆谷铸造的银币。这个钱币名称后来用于其他银币，并成为多个国家货币单位的名称。
etymology_story.en: Dollar came through forms such as Low German or Dutch daler from German Taler, shortened from Joachimstaler, a silver coin minted in Joachimsthal in Bohemia. The name spread to other silver coins and eventually became the name of monetary units in several countries.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dollar 是不可再作常规词缀拆分的借入词；dollar + -s → dollars（复数）。派生词有 dollarize／dollarise（使采用美元；使美元化）、dollarization／dollarisation（美元化）；常见复合形式有 dollar-denominated（以美元计价的）、multimillion-dollar（价值数百万美元的）和 dollar bill（一美元纸币）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dollar is a borrowed stem with no productive internal affix breakdown; dollar plus -s forms the plural dollars. Derivatives include dollarize or dollarise and dollarization or dollarisation; common compounds include dollar-denominated, multimillion-dollar, and dollar bill.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: buck（元）是 dollar 的非正式说法，具体币种依语境而定；USD（美元）专指美国货币；greenback（美元纸币）是对美国纸币的非正式称呼。dollar 本身可指多个国家的货币单位，不能一律译成“美元”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Buck is an informal equivalent of dollar, with the currency determined by context; USD specifically identifies the US dollar; greenback informally refers to a US banknote. Dollar itself can name several countries' monetary units.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一枚山谷银币的名字，传成多国货币的“元”；看到 dollar，先看是哪一国。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A valley's silver-coin name became the dollar: remember the coin, then check which country's currency is meant.

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 sweostor，是一个历史悠久的日耳曼语亲属词；现代形式也受到古诺尔斯语同源词 systir 的影响。它从家庭中的姐妹扩展为宗教或社会群体中的女性同伴，并用于表示机构之间的密切关系。
etymology_story.en: Sister comes from Old English sweostor, an inherited Germanic kinship word; its modern form was also influenced by the Old Norse cognate systir. Its meaning extended from a female sibling to women in religious or social communities and to closely related institutions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 sister 是不可再作有效词缀拆分的词基。词族包括 sister + -s → sisters（姐妹，复数），sister + -hood → sisterhood（姐妹关系；女性团结；女修会），sister + -ly → sisterly（姐妹般的），sisterly + -ness → sisterliness（姐妹般的亲切）；常用复合词包括 stepsister（继姐妹）、half-sister（同父异母或同母异父的姐妹）和 sister-in-law（配偶的姐妹或兄弟的妻子），后者复数为 sisters-in-law。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sister is a base with no productive internal affix division. Its family includes sister + -s → sisters, sister + -hood → sisterhood (the relationship between sisters, solidarity among women, or a religious community), sister + -ly → sisterly, and sisterly + -ness → sisterliness. Common compounds include stepsister, half-sister, and sister-in-law (a spouse's sister or a sibling's wife), whose plural is sisters-in-law.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sibling（兄弟姐妹）不限定性别；nun（修女）仅对应宗教义，严格用法中与 sister 的范围不完全相同；female ally（女性盟友）强调共同目标，不一定带有 sister 所表达的亲密与认同感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sibling does not specify gender. Nun overlaps with the religious sense, although the terms have different scopes in precise religious usage. Female ally emphasizes shared aims without necessarily suggesting the closeness and shared identity conveyed by sister.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 以“家庭中的姐妹”为中心：共同的家庭延伸为共同的信仰、事业或组织关系。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a sister in a family: shared family membership extends to shared faith, causes, or organizational ties.

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语疑问代词 hwā（谁）的与格形式 hwām；随着英语格变化的简化，这一形式逐渐承担更广泛的宾格功能。现代 whom 主要保留在正式书面语和介词之后，日常口语中常由 who 代替。
etymology_story.en: Whom descends from hwām, a dative form of the Old English interrogative pronoun hwā, meaning 'who'; as English case distinctions weakened, it acquired a broader object function. It now survives mainly in formal writing and after prepositions, while everyday speech often uses who instead.

morphology_enriched.zh: whom 是 who 的宾格形式，不是 who 加现代后缀 -m；who、whom、whose 分别体现主格、宾格和所属关系。whom + -ever → whomever（无论谁，作宾语）；whoever 是相应的主格形式，具体选择取决于它在所属从句中的语法功能。
morphology_enriched.en: Whom is the object-case form of who, not who plus a modern suffix -m; who, whom, and whose express subject case, object case, and possession. Whom + -ever forms whomever, the object-case counterpart of whoever; the choice depends on its grammatical role within its own clause.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: who（谁）在非正式语体中常代替宾语 whom，但在紧接前置介词时通常仍用 whom；that（关系代词）可在部分限定性关系从句中代替 whom，但不能直接接在前置介词后；whomever（无论谁）表示不特定的任何人，不能直接替换普通疑问词 whom。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Who commonly replaces object whom in informal usage, but whom is normally retained immediately after a fronted preposition. That can replace whom in some defining relative clauses but cannot directly follow a fronted preposition. Whomever means 'any person who' in an object role and does not simply replace interrogative whom.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用 him 检查宾语位置：若对应答案是 him，正式表达通常选 whom；判断时看它在自身从句中的作用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use him as an object-case check: if him fits the corresponding answer, formal usage usually calls for whom; judge its role within its own clause.

etymology_story.zh: 经盎格鲁法语和古法语 memorie 进入英语，源自拉丁语 memoria（记忆；回想），与 memor（记得的）有关。它既表示记忆能力，也表示被记住的内容，后来又扩展到计算机的信息存储功能。
etymology_story.en: Memory entered English through Anglo-French and Old French memorie, from Latin memoria, meaning remembrance or memory, related to memor, 'mindful' or 'remembering'. It came to denote both the ability to remember and remembered content, and later the information-storage function of computers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 memory 通常作为整体词基，不宜机械拆成 mem + -ory；复数遵循辅音字母加 y 的变化：memory → memories。相关词族包括 memorize／memorise（记住；熟记）、memorization／memorisation（记忆；背记过程）、memorizer／memoriser（善于或从事记忆者）、memorable（难忘的）、memorably（令人难忘地）、memorability（令人难忘的特质）、memorial（纪念物；纪念的）、memorialize／memorialise（纪念）和 memorialization／memorialisation（纪念活动或过程）；这些相关词并非都由完整的 memory 直接加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Memory normally functions as a whole base in modern English rather than being mechanically divided into mem + -ory; its plural changes consonant + y to -ies: memory → memories. The related family includes memorize/memorise, memorization/memorisation, memorizer/memoriser, memorable, memorably, memorability, memorial, memorialize/memorialise, and memorialization/memorialisation. These related words are not all formed by adding suffixes directly to the complete word memory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: recollection（回忆）较正式，常强调回想起的具体内容；recall（回想；记忆提取能力）侧重把信息从记忆中调取出来；remembrance（追忆；纪念）常带感情色彩，尤其用于怀念逝者。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Recollection is relatively formal and often emphasizes particular remembered content. Recall focuses on retrieving information or the ability to retrieve it. Remembrance often carries emotional or commemorative associations, especially when remembering someone who has died.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“保存并重现”：人脑保存经历形成记忆，电脑保存信息形成存储。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'retain and bring back': a mind retains experiences as memories, while a computer retains information in memory.

etymology_story.zh: 物主代词 mine 源自古英语 mīn（我的），与 my 属于同一历史系统；名词 mine 则经古法语 mine（矿井；地下通道）进入英语，两者来源不同。采矿动词由矿井义发展而来，爆炸物义与早期军事地下掘进和爆破有关，后来又出现挖掘信息及加密货币“挖矿”等比喻用法。
etymology_story.en: The possessive pronoun mine comes from Old English mīn, 'my', whereas the noun entered through Old French mine, 'mine' or 'underground passage'; the two have separate origins. The extraction verb developed from the excavation sense, the explosive sense arose through military tunnelling and demolition, and later figurative uses include extracting information and mining cryptocurrency.

morphology_enriched.zh: 代词 mine 是与 my 对应的独立物主形式，不加复数 -s，也不与采矿词族作词源拆分。名词和动词词族包括 mine → mines（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、mined（过去式及过去分词）、mining（现在分词；采矿或挖矿活动），mine + -er → miner（矿工；挖矿者或设备），mine + -able → mineable／minable（可开采的），un- + mined → unmined（未开采的；未布雷的）；常用复合词包括 coalmine／coal mine（煤矿）、goldmine／gold mine（金矿；宝贵资源）、minefield（雷区）、minesweeper（扫雷舰）和 minelayer（布雷舰或布雷设备）。
morphology_enriched.en: The pronoun mine is the independent possessive counterpart of my; it takes no plural -s and is historically separate from the mining family. The noun and verb family includes mines, mined, mining, mine + -er → miner, mine + -able → mineable/minable, and un- + mined → unmined. Common compounds include coalmine/coal mine, goldmine/gold mine, minefield, minesweeper, and minelayer; miner can also denote a cryptocurrency participant or mining device.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: belonging to me（属于我的）可解释代词 mine，但句法结构不同；extract（提取；开采）强调取出材料或信息，不一定涉及矿井；excavate（挖掘）强调挖土和形成坑洞，不一定以取得矿产为目的。这些词分别对应不同义项，不能跨义项互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Belonging to me paraphrases the possessive pronoun but has a different grammatical structure. Extract emphasizes removing material or information and need not involve a mine. Excavate emphasizes digging and removing earth, without necessarily obtaining minerals. These expressions match different senses and are not interchangeable across them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分开记两个来源：代词 mine＝“我的那一个”；采矿词族 mine＝“从地下挖出价值”，再联想到挖掘数据和数字挖矿；地雷义联想地下爆破。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the origins separate: possessive mine means 'the one belonging to me'; the mining family starts with digging value from the earth and extends to data and digital mining, while explosive mines recall underground demolition.

etymology_story.zh: 由历史上表示“在……处、向……”的 a- 与 head（头；前端）组合而成，字面意思接近“在前端、向前”。空间上的“前方”随后自然扩展为时间上的“将来或提前”，以及进度和竞争中的“领先”。
etymology_story.en: Ahead combines the historical element a-, meaning 'at', 'on', or 'towards', with head in the sense of the front. Its spatial meaning extended naturally to future time, early preparation, and a leading position in progress or competition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词为 a-（在；向）+ head（前端）→ ahead；现代英语中通常整体使用，a- 不能在这里作为自由生成新词的普通前缀。ahead 本身没有常规屈折变化；相关表达包括 ahead of（在……前面；领先于）、ahead of time（提前）、go ahead（进行；请便），以及由该短语转成的 go-ahead（名词：许可；形容词：积极进取的）。head、heading、headway 属于相关词汇网络，并非 ahead 直接加后缀的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical formation is a- ('at/on/towards') + head ('front') → ahead; in modern English it is normally treated as a whole word, and this a- is not a freely productive prefix. Ahead has no regular inflected forms. Related expressions include ahead of, ahead of time, and go ahead, from which go-ahead developed as a noun meaning permission and an adjective meaning enterprising. Head, heading, and headway belong to the related lexical network rather than being suffix derivatives of ahead.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: in front（在前面）主要描述空间位置；in advance（提前）强调在某事发生或需要之前准备；forward／forwards（向前）侧重运动方向，而 ahead 还可表示未来、提前和竞争领先。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In front mainly describes spatial position. In advance emphasizes preparation before an event or need. Forward/forwards focuses on direction of movement, while ahead also covers future time, early action, and a competitive lead.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 head 想成队伍最前端：位置在前＝前方；时间在前＝提前；成绩在前＝领先。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the head of a line: ahead in space means in front, ahead in timing means early, and ahead in performance means leading.

senses.meaning_en: and not; used to connect negative alternatives or statements
senses.english_definition: You use nor to introduce another thing that is not true or does not happen, often after neither or another negative expression.
senses.collocation_en: neither A nor B; nor do I
senses.collocation_zh: 既不A也不B；我也不
senses.sentence_en: She neither called nor sent a message, nor did she explain her absence.
senses.sentence_zh: 她既没打电话，也没发消息，也没有解释自己为何缺席。

etymology_story.zh: nor 源于中古英语，是 nother（意为“两者都不”）的缩略形式，其历史与 neither 相连。它后来成为连接否定选项或补充否定陈述的连词。
etymology_story.en: Nor developed in Middle English as a shortened form of nother, meaning 'neither', and shares its history with neither. It became a conjunction connecting negative alternatives or adding a further negative statement.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 nor 是不可再分析的整体连词，不是 n- 加 or；没有常用屈折变化或派生词。常用结构：neither A nor B（既不A也不B）；否定分句 + nor + 助动词或情态动词 + 主语，表示“……也不”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, nor is an indivisible conjunction, not a productive combination of n- and or; it has no common inflected forms or derivatives. Common patterns are neither A nor B and a negative clause followed by nor + auxiliary or modal verb + subject, meaning 'and ... not either'.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: or 在否定词的作用范围内也可连接否定选项，如 not A or B；neither 表示“两者都不”，可独立使用或与 nor 配对；and ... not ... either 可表达相近意思，但 nor 连接完整分句时通常要求主语与助动词倒装。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Or can connect alternatives within the scope of a negative, as in not A or B; neither means 'not either' and can stand alone or pair with nor; and ... not ... either conveys a similar meaning, but nor normally requires subject–auxiliary inversion when it introduces a full clause.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记搭配：neither 先否定一个，nor 再否定另一个。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the pair: neither rejects one alternative; nor rejects the other.

senses.meaning_en: an act of asking formally or politely for something
senses.english_definition: A request is something that you ask someone to do or give you, usually formally or politely.
senses.collocation_en: make a request; a request for information
senses.collocation_zh: 提出请求；索取信息的请求
senses.sentence_en: We received a request for more information about the course.

senses.meaning_zh: 正式或礼貌地请求；要求
senses.meaning_en: to ask formally or politely for something or for an action
senses.english_definition: If you request something, you ask for it formally or politely.
senses.collocation_en: request permission; request assistance
senses.collocation_zh: 请求许可；请求协助
senses.sentence_en: Passengers are requested to keep their seat belts fastened.

etymology_story.zh: request 经古法语 requeste 进入中古英语，最终与拉丁语 requirere（寻找、询问、要求）有关。英语先有表示“请求”的名词，后来发展出同形动词，两者如今都常用于较正式或礼貌的表达。
etymology_story.en: Request entered Middle English through Old French requeste and is ultimately related to Latin requirere, meaning 'seek out, inquire, or ask for'. The English noun preceded the corresponding verb, and both are now common in formal or polite language.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：request 是整体词基，可通过零派生同时作名词和动词，不宜机械拆成 re- + quest。屈折形式：requests（请求；第三人称单数）、requested（过去式和过去分词）、requesting（现在分词）；常用派生词：requester/requestor（请求者、申请人）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: request is a whole base used as both noun and verb through conversion; it should not be mechanically analyzed as re- + quest. Inflected forms are requests, requested, and requesting; common derivatives are requester and the alternative spelling requestor, meaning a person who makes a request.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ask 最通用，语体中性，作动词时通常用 ask for something；appeal 强调恳切求助或呼吁支持；demand 强调坚持要求，通常带有权利主张或强硬语气。request 比 ask 正式，通常比 demand 委婉。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ask is the broadest, most neutral verb and normally takes for before the thing wanted; appeal suggests an earnest call for help or support; demand expresses an insistent requirement, often backed by authority or a claimed right. Request is more formal than ask and usually less forceful than demand.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 request 看作“正式地开口要”：a request 是一次请求，to request 是提出请求。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'ask formally': a request is the act or message; to request is to make that request.

etymology_story.zh: 现代 post 汇合了几条历史来源：“柱、桩”来自古英语 post，最终源于拉丁语 postis（门柱）；“邮政”和“岗位”则经法语分别联系到意大利语 posta 和 posto，二者都与拉丁语 ponere（放置）有关。网络“发帖”延续了公开张贴告示的意义，而表示“在……之后”的 post 来自拉丁语 post，与这些名词来源不同。
etymology_story.en: Modern post brings together several histories: the upright support comes from Old English post, ultimately Latin postis, 'doorpost', while the postal and position senses came through French from Italian posta and posto, both related to Latin ponere, 'put or place'. Online posting extends the display of public notices, whereas post meaning 'after' comes from the separate Latin word post.

morphology_enriched.zh: post 在现代英语中是整体词基，常通过零派生作名词和动词；屈折形式为 posts、posted、posting。常用相关词和复合词包括 poster（海报；发帖者）、posting（发布；帖子；派驻）、repost（转发；重新发布）、postage（邮资）、postal（邮政的）、postcard（明信片）、postcode（邮政编码）、postbox（邮筒）、postbag（邮袋；收到的邮件）、postmark（邮戳；盖邮戳）、postmaster（邮局局长）、post office（邮局）、goalpost（球门柱）、signpost（路标；指示）、gatepost（门柱）、outpost（前哨；边远据点）。另有表示“在……之后”的独立前缀 post-，如 postwar（战后的）和 postgraduate（研究生；研究生的），应与上述词基区分。
morphology_enriched.en: Post is a whole modern base, commonly used as a noun and verb through conversion; its inflected forms are posts, posted, and posting. Common related words and compounds include poster, posting, repost, postage, postal, postcard, postcode, postbox, postbag, postmark, postmaster, post office, goalpost, signpost, gatepost, and outpost. The separate prefix post-, meaning 'after', forms words such as postwar and postgraduate and should be distinguished from these noun and verb bases.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pillar 与“柱”义接近，但通常更粗大，常用于承重；mail 对应“邮件、邮政、邮寄”，尤其常见于美式英语，不能替代 post 的“岗位”等义；position 对应“职位、岗位”，意义比具体的派驻地点更宽。三个词分别对应 post 的不同义项，不能跨义项互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pillar overlaps with the support sense but usually suggests a larger, often load-bearing structure; mail corresponds to postal items, the postal system, or sending them, especially in American English; position corresponds to a job or role and is broader than a particular duty station. Each matches a different sense of post and cannot replace it across all meanings.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分线记：柱子立在固定点，人被派到岗位，信息被贴出或发出；post- 另记为“之后”。这是记忆联想，不表示这些词义都来自同一个词根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use separate memory tracks: a post stands in place, a worker is assigned to a post, and information is posted for others to receive; remember post- separately as 'after'. This is a memory link, not a claim that every sense has one origin.

etymology_story.zh: original 经法语进入英语，源于拉丁语 originalis（与起源有关的），其词根与 origo（起源）及 oriri（升起、产生）相连。“源头的、最初的”后来延伸为“原作的”，也发展出“不模仿他人、具有独创性”的意思。
etymology_story.en: Original entered English through French from Latin originalis, 'relating to an origin', connected with origo, 'origin', and oriri, 'rise or arise'. The idea of being at the source developed into the senses of an authentic original work and something independently inventive.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：origin（起源）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ original；original 通过零派生也作名词。常用词族：origin（起源）、originally（最初；原先）、originality（独创性）、unoriginal（缺乏独创性的）、unoriginality（缺乏独创性）、originate（起源；创始）、originator（创始人）、origination（发起；创始）；originals 是名词复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: origin + the adjective suffix -al forms original, which also functions as a noun through conversion. The common family includes origin, originally, originality, unoriginal, unoriginality, originate, originator, and origination; originals is the plural noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: initial 强调时间或过程中的最初阶段，不必暗示后来产生了副本；innovative 强调引入新方法或新做法，不必是最早的来源；authentic 强调真实可信、并非伪造，而 original 在原作义上强调并非复制品。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Initial emphasizes the first stage in time or a process, without necessarily implying later copies; innovative emphasizes introducing new methods or approaches, without necessarily being the earliest source; authentic emphasizes genuineness rather than forgery, while original in the artwork sense emphasizes that something is not a reproduction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 origin“源头”：时间上的源头是“最初的”，作品的源头是“原作”，想法出自自己就是“独创的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to origin: the source in time is the first version, the source of copies is the original, and an idea originating with its creator is inventive.

etymology_story.zh: female 经古法语 femelle 来自拉丁语 femella，后者是 femina（女人）的指小形式。英语拼写后来受到 male 的影响，但 female 并不是由 fe- 加 male 构成；接头等技术用法则借用了生物学上的雌雄配对概念。
etymology_story.en: Female came through Old French femelle from Latin femella, a diminutive of femina, 'woman'. Its English spelling was later influenced by male, although it is not formed from fe- plus male; technical connector senses borrow the biological pairing of female and male.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：female 是不可拆分的借词，可直接作形容词和名词；不是 fe- + male。常用词形和派生词：females（名词复数）、femaleness（女性或雌性的属性）；female-dominated（女性占主导的）和 female-led（由女性领导的）是常见复合形式。feminine（女性气质的；阴性的）、femininity（女性气质）、feminism（女权主义）和 feminist（女权主义者；女权主义的）属于历史上同源的词汇，并非直接由现代 female 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: female is an indivisible loanword used directly as both adjective and noun; it is not fe- + male. Common forms and derivatives include the plural females and the noun femaleness; female-dominated and female-led are common compounds. Feminine, femininity, feminism, and feminist belong to the historically related vocabulary but are not direct derivatives of modern female.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: woman 专指成年女性，也是日常指称成年女性时的常用名词；girl 通常指女孩或年轻女性；feminine 主要描述被视为女性化的气质、风格或语法阴性，不等同于表示性别的 female。female 作名词常见于动物、统计和科学语境，用于人时比 woman 更偏分类表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Woman specifically means an adult female human and is the usual everyday noun for one; girl usually refers to a female child or young woman; feminine describes qualities or styles associated with women, or grammatical gender, rather than simply female sex. As a noun, female is common in animal, statistical, and scientific contexts and sounds more classificatory than woman when referring to people.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: female 整体记为“女性／雌性”；接头义联想为“带接口、接纳匹配部件”，不要拆成 fe- + male。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Learn female as one unit meaning 'female person or animal'; for connectors, picture a receiving opening for a matching part, without splitting the word into fe- + male.

etymology_story.zh: 来自古英语 grēne，属于与 grow“生长”有历史联系的日耳曼语词族，基本意象是生长中的草木。由植物的颜色发展出“未成熟、缺乏经验”等义，后来又产生了现代环保义。
etymology_story.en: Green comes from Old English grēne and belongs to a Germanic word family historically related to grow, linking the colour with growing vegetation. The plant association developed into meanings such as unripe and inexperienced, followed much later by the environmental sense.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代基本词为 green，不能再拆成常用词根和词缀；同形转类可作名词和动词。主要词族：greener、greenest（比较级、最高级）；green + -ish → greenish（略绿的）；green + -ness → greenness（绿色；青涩）；green + -ery → greenery（绿植）；greening（绿化；绿色转型）；常见合成词有 evergreen（常绿的）、greenhouse（温室）、greenbelt（绿化带）、greenfield（未开发土地的）和 greenwashing（漂绿）。
morphology_enriched.en: Green is a modern base word with no productive internal division into root and affixes; conversion also makes it a noun and verb. Its main family includes greener and greenest; green + -ish → greenish; green + -ness → greenness; green + -ery → greenery; and greening. Common compounds include evergreen, greenhouse, greenbelt, greenfield, and greenwashing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: verdant 指草木茂盛、青翠，较有文学色彩；inexperienced 对应“缺乏经验”，不含颜色义；eco-friendly 对应“环保”，常强调产品或行为对环境的影响。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Verdant describes lush green vegetation and has a literary tone; inexperienced matches the lack-of-experience sense without any colour meaning; eco-friendly matches the environmental sense and often emphasizes the impact of a product or activity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 生长的草木是绿的：嫩绿联想到未成熟，保护绿意联想到环保。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Growing plants are green: young growth suggests immaturity, and protecting that greenery suggests environmental care.

senses.meaning_en: to move rhythmically to music or perform a particular dance
senses.english_definition: When you dance, you move your body rhythmically, usually to music.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 dauncen 借自古法语 dancer，后者的更早来源尚不确定。英语的动词和名词长期并用，核心意义一直围绕有节奏的身体动作，并引申为火光等轻快跳动。
etymology_story.en: Middle English dauncen was borrowed from Old French dancer, whose earlier origin is uncertain. The English verb and noun have long existed together, with rhythmic bodily movement later providing a metaphor for flickering flames and other lively motion.

morphology_enriched.zh: dance 是现代基本词，名词和动词同形。dance 去掉词尾 e 加 -er → dancer（舞者），加 -ing → dancing（跳舞；舞蹈的），加 -ed → danced（过去式、过去分词）；dance + -able → danceable（适合跳舞的）；常见合成词有 ballroom dance（交谊舞）、breakdance（跳霹雳舞）和 tap-dancing（踢踏舞）。
morphology_enriched.en: Dance is a modern base used as both noun and verb. Drop final e before -er to form dancer, before -ing to form dancing, and before -ed to form danced; dance + -able gives danceable. Common compounds include ballroom dance, breakdance, and tap-dancing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: boogie 是非正式用语，常指随流行音乐跳舞；waltz 特指跳华尔兹，也可引申为轻松自如地移动；sway 只强调身体来回摇摆，不一定构成完整舞蹈。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Boogie is informal and usually means dancing to popular music; waltz names a specific dance and can also suggest moving with easy confidence; sway describes a back-and-forth movement that need not amount to dancing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 跟着节奏动起来：动作是 dance，跳的一支舞或舞会也是 dance。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move with the rhythm: dance names both the movement and the dance or event built around it.

senses.meaning_en: images, events, and feelings experienced during sleep

etymology_story.zh: 古英语 drēam 的已知含义包括“欢乐、音乐”，而现代“睡眠中的梦”义在中古英语中确立，通常认为可能受到古诺尔斯语 draumr 的影响。两组意义之间的具体历史关系仍有争议，后来又从梦境发展出“想象中的理想生活、梦想”等义。
etymology_story.en: Recorded meanings of Old English drēam include joy and music, while the modern sleep sense became established in Middle English, possibly under the influence of Old Norse draumr. The precise historical relationship remains disputed; imagined experiences later provided the basis for hopes and ideal futures.

morphology_enriched.zh: dream 是现代基本词，名词和动词同形；过去式和过去分词均可用 dreamed 或 dreamt。主要词族：dream + -er → dreamer（做梦者；梦想家）；dream + -y → dreamy（梦幻的；心不在焉的），进一步有 dreamily（梦幻地）和 dreaminess（梦幻感）；另有 dreaming（做梦）、dreamlike（如梦的）、dreamless（无梦的）、dreamland（梦乡）、daydream（白日梦；做白日梦）和 daydreamer（爱做白日梦的人）。dream job 中的 dream 通常分析为名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Dream is a modern base functioning as both noun and verb; dreamed and dreamt are alternative past-tense and past-participle forms. Its main family includes dream + -er → dreamer; dream + -y → dreamy, followed by dreamily and dreaminess; plus dreaming, dreamlike, dreamless, dreamland, daydream, and daydreamer. In dream job, dream is normally analysed as an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aspiration 指希望通过努力实现的志向，较正式；fantasy 强调想象中的情境，可能不切实际；nightmare 专指令人恐惧的梦，也可比喻极糟糕的经历。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aspiration is a relatively formal word for an ambition pursued through effort; fantasy emphasizes an imagined situation that may be unrealistic; nightmare specifically means a frightening dream or, figuratively, a very unpleasant experience.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 脑海里的另一种生活：睡着是梦，醒着盼望实现就是梦想。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Another life in your mind: asleep it is a dream; awake it can become a future you hope to achieve.

etymology_story.zh: 经法语进入英语，源自拉丁语 observāre，由 ob- 和 servāre“看守、保存、留意”构成。历史上的“留心、遵行”发展为现代的观察、遵守、纪念以及就所见发表评论等义。
etymology_story.en: Observe entered English through French from Latin observāre, formed with ob- and servāre, meaning to watch, keep, or attend to. Its historical senses of attending to and following something developed into watching, obeying, marking occasions, and commenting on what has been noticed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 observe 通常作为整体动词词基，不宜把它机械理解为 ob- 加现代动词 serve。主要词族：observe 去 e 加 -er → observer（观察者）；去 e 加 -able → observable（可观察的），进一步有 observably（可察觉地）和 observability（可观察性）；另有 observation（观察；评论）、observational（观察的）、observationally（通过观察）、observant（敏锐的；恪守教规的）、observantly（留心地）、observance（遵守；仪式）、unobserved（未被注意到的）和 unobservant（不善观察的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, observe normally functions as a whole verb base; it should not be mechanically interpreted as ob- plus the modern verb serve. Its main family includes observer and observable, formed by dropping final e before -er and -able; observable further gives observably and observability. Related forms include observation, observational, observationally, observant, observantly, observance, unobserved, and unobservant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: watch 强调持续观看，不一定带研究目的；notice 强调察觉某事，未必经过持续观察；comply with 对应“遵守”义，强调按要求行事，而不涉及观看。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Watch emphasizes sustained looking without necessarily suggesting investigation; notice emphasizes becoming aware of something without prolonged attention; comply with matches the obedience sense and concerns following requirements rather than looking.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“留心对待”：对现象留心是观察，对规则留心是遵守，对节日留心是纪念。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of paying careful attention: attend to events by watching, to rules by following them, and to special days by marking them.

senses.meaning_en: to give someone information or tell them about something
senses.english_definition: If you inform someone of something, you tell them about it so that they know what has happened or what they need to know.
senses.collocation_en: inform someone of a decision; keep someone informed

etymology_story.zh: 经古法语 informer 来自拉丁语 informāre，由 in- 与 forma“形状”构成，原义涉及“赋予形状、塑造”。“塑造思想、教导”后来发展为“告知”，而现代“为决策提供依据”仍保留了塑造事物的意味。
etymology_story.en: Inform comes through Old French informer from Latin informāre, formed from in- and forma, meaning shape or form. The idea of shaping the mind through instruction developed into giving information, while the modern sense of shaping decisions preserves the older connection.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代通常以 inform 为整体词基；历史上的 in- 在这里不表示否定。主要词族：inform + -ed → informed（知情的；有见识的），加 -ing → informing（告知）；inform + -er → informer（告密者），另有 informant（消息提供者；线人）；information（信息）、informational（信息的）、informative（提供有用信息的）、informatively（提供信息地）和 informativeness（信息丰富程度）；加 un-、mis-、dis- 分别形成 uninformed（不了解情况的）、misinform（误导；提供错误信息）、disinform（故意提供虚假信息），并有 misinformation（错误信息）和 disinformation（故意散布的虚假信息）；常见复合形式有 well-informed（消息灵通的）和 ill-informed（了解不足的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats inform as a whole base; its historical in- is not a negative prefix. Main family members include inform + -ed → informed and inform + -ing → informing; inform + -er → informer, alongside informant; information, informational, informative, informatively, and informativeness. Prefixation produces uninformed, misinform, and disinform, with misinformation and disinformation as related nouns; common compound forms include well-informed and ill-informed.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tell 是最普通的“告诉”，适用范围最广；notify 较正式，通常指就具体事项发出通知；brief 强调向某人提供执行任务或作出决定所需的重点信息。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tell is the broadest and most ordinary word for communicating something; notify is more formal and usually concerns a specific event or official notice; brief emphasizes giving someone the key information needed for a task or decision.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑是“给思想塑形”：把信息告诉人，也让信息塑造判断。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical idea of shaping the mind: information reaches a person and helps shape their judgment.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语进入英语，源于拉丁语 communicatio，来自 communicare，意为“分享、使共同拥有”，与 communis“共同的”同源。其核心从“共同分享”发展为信息交流，也延伸指传递的消息以及通信、交通联系。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French from Latin communicatio, based on communicare, meaning 'to share or make common,' and related to communis, 'common.' The idea of sharing developed into the exchange of information, the messages exchanged, and the systems connecting people and places.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系：communicate（交流、传达，去词尾 e）+ -ion（行为或过程）→ communication；communication + -s → communications。主要词族：communicate、communicated、communicating、communicator（交流者；传播者）、communicative（善于交流的）、communicatively（善于交流地）、communicativeness（健谈；交流倾向）、uncommunicative（不爱交流的）、miscommunicate（错误传达）、miscommunication（沟通失误）、telecommunication／telecommunications（电信）；同源相关词还有 communicable（可传染的；可传达的）和 communicability（可传染性；可传达性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: communicate, with final -e removed, + -ion, marking an action or process, → communication; communication + -s → communications. Main family members include communicate, communicated, communicating, communicator, communicative, communicatively, communicativeness, uncommunicative, miscommunicate, miscommunication, and telecommunication/telecommunications. Related words from the same historical family include communicable and communicability.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 交流过程义：interaction（互动）强调双方相互影响；exchange（交换）强调信息或观点的往来。消息义：message（消息）比 communication 更日常，communication 常带正式或公务色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the process sense, interaction emphasizes reciprocal involvement, while exchange emphasizes information or ideas passing between people. For an individual item, message is more everyday; communication often sounds official or businesslike.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把信息变成“共同知道的东西”：共同分享 → 沟通 → 消息与通信。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Make information something people share: sharing leads to communication, messages, and connecting systems.

senses.meaning_zh: 发现原先未知的事物或地方

senses.english_definition: If you discover a talented person or something you enjoy, you recognize their value or begin to appreciate them.

senses.collocation_zh: 发掘新人才；发现自己热爱阅读
senses.sentence_en: The singer was discovered while performing in a small club.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位歌手在一家小俱乐部演出时被发掘出来。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自古法语 descovrir，原意是“揭开、移去覆盖物”，其中 des- 表示逆转，covrir 表示“覆盖”，后者可追溯至拉丁语。由“揭开遮盖”发展出“使隐藏之物显露”，继而形成现代的“发现、得知”义。
etymology_story.en: Discover comes from Old French descovrir, 'to uncover,' combining a reversing prefix with covrir, 'to cover,' ultimately from Latin. Removing a covering became a metaphor for revealing something hidden and then for finding or learning something previously unknown.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 dis-（逆转、除去）+ cover（覆盖）→ discover，但该词整体经法语借入，并非现代英语中新造。主要词族：discovers、discovered、discovering；discover + -er → discoverer（发现者）；discovery（发现；发现物）、discoveries（复数）；discoverable（可发现的）、discoverability（可发现性）、undiscovered（未被发现的）；re- + discover → rediscover（重新发现），并有 rediscovery（重新发现）和 rediscovered（重新发现的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analyzed today as dis-, expressing reversal or removal, + cover, although English borrowed the complete word from French. Main family members are discovers, discovered, discovering, discoverer, discovery, discoveries, discoverable, discoverability, and undiscovered. Adding re- gives rediscover, with rediscovery and rediscovered.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: find（找到）最宽泛，可指找到已知但遗失的东西；uncover（揭露）强调使隐藏的事实显现；detect（检测到；察觉）强调通过观察或仪器识别细微信号。discover 更强调某事对发现者而言此前未知。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Find is broad and can describe locating something already known but lost. Uncover emphasizes revealing hidden facts, while detect emphasizes noticing subtle signs, often through careful observation or instruments. Discover foregrounds something previously unknown to the finder.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dis- 去掉 + cover 覆盖：揭开遮盖，就“发现”了。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Reverse the cover: uncover something, and you discover it.

senses.meaning_en: to move along a particular course, or move a camera to follow a subject
senses.english_definition: If something tracks in a direction, it moves along that course; if a camera tracks someone, it moves to keep them in view.
senses.collocation_en: track eastward; the camera tracks the actor
senses.collocation_zh: 向东移动；摄影机移动跟拍演员
senses.sentence_en: The camera tracked the runner as she approached the finish line.
senses.sentence_zh: 当这名跑步者接近终点线时，摄影机移动跟拍着她。

senses.meaning_zh: 踩带入；踩得到处都是，尤指泥土
senses.meaning_en: to carry dirt into or across a place on footwear
senses.english_definition: If you track mud or dirt into a place, you carry it there on your shoes and leave marks as you walk.
senses.collocation_en: track mud into the house; track dirt across the floor
senses.collocation_zh: 把泥踩带进屋；把地板踩得到处是土
senses.sentence_en: Please take off your boots so you don't track mud into the kitchen.
senses.sentence_zh: 请脱下靴子，免得把泥带进厨房。

etymology_story.zh: 该词早期表示“足迹、留下的痕迹”，通常与法语 trac 联系起来，但更早的来源并不确定。由“移动留下的痕迹”扩展为路径、轨道和赛道，动词则表示循迹追踪；录音中的 track 也延续了“记录所占的一条路径”这一形象。
etymology_story.en: The word originally referred to a footprint or trace and is commonly connected with French trac, although its earlier origin is uncertain. A trace of movement developed into a path, railway, or racing course, while the verb came to mean following such traces; recording tracks likewise reflect the idea of a path carrying recorded information.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 track 是不能再作常用词缀分析的词根，名词可直接转为动词。屈折形式：tracks、tracked、tracking；派生词：tracker（追踪者；追踪器）、trackable（可追踪的）、untrackable（无法追踪的）、trackless（无路的；无踪迹的）、untracked（未被追踪的）。常见合成词及相关形式：backtrack（原路返回；收回说法）、sidetrack（使偏离主题）、fast-track（快速通道；加速处理）、soundtrack（电影配乐；声轨）、racetrack（赛道）、trackball（轨迹球）、trackpad（触控板）、tracksuit（运动服）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, track is a simple base with no productive internal affix division; the noun also becomes a verb without an added suffix. Inflected forms are tracks, tracked, and tracking. Derivatives include tracker, trackable, untrackable, trackless, and untracked. Common compounds and related formations include backtrack, sidetrack, fast-track, soundtrack, racetrack, trackball, trackpad, and tracksuit.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词义：trail（踪迹；小径）常指连续的线索或乡野小路。动词义：trace（追查）侧重还原来源或经过；monitor（监测）侧重持续检查状态。track 的共同重点是沿着路线或时间持续跟随。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: As a noun, trail often means a sequence of clues or a countryside path. As verbs, trace emphasizes reconstructing an origin or course, while monitor emphasizes checking conditions over time. Track centers on following a route, movement, or development.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 走过留下“痕迹”，痕迹连成“路线”；沿路线跟下去，就是“追踪”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Movement leaves marks; connected marks make a route; following that route means tracking.

senses.meaning_zh: 花园；菜园；种植花草或蔬菜的园地
senses.meaning_en: an area where flowers, vegetables, or other plants are grown
senses.english_definition: A garden is an area of land where people grow flowers, vegetables, or other plants, often beside a house.
senses.collocation_en: a vegetable garden; the back garden
senses.collocation_zh: 菜园；后花园

senses.meaning_zh: 公共花园；供游览的园林，常用复数 gardens
senses.meaning_en: a public or ornamental area with plants and paths, often used in the plural
senses.english_definition: Gardens are areas arranged with plants, lawns, and paths for people to visit and enjoy.

senses.collocation_zh: 植物园；公共花园
senses.sentence_en: We spent the afternoon walking around the botanical gardens.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们下午在植物园里散步。

senses.meaning_zh: 从事园艺；种植并照料花草蔬菜
senses.meaning_en: to grow and care for plants in a garden
senses.english_definition: If you garden, you grow plants and do the work needed to care for a garden.
senses.collocation_en: garden organically; garden in containers
senses.collocation_zh: 采用有机方式进行园艺种植；利用容器种植花草蔬菜
senses.sentence_en: She gardens for an hour most evenings.
senses.sentence_zh: 她大多数晚上都会花一个小时打理花园。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经盎格鲁法语 gardin 等形式进入英语，最终来自日耳曼语中表示“围起来的场地”的词，与 yard 有历史亲缘关系。围地常被用于种植，词义因而发展为花园、菜园，后来又由名词产生“从事园艺”的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Garden entered English through Anglo-French forms such as gardin and ultimately comes from a Germanic word for an enclosure, historically related to yard. Enclosed ground used for growing plants became a garden, and the noun later supplied the verb meaning to cultivate and care for one.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 garden 是整体词根，不应拆为 gard + -en；名词直接转为动词。主要词族：gardens、gardened、gardening（园艺；从事园艺）；garden + -er → gardener（园丁；园艺爱好者）。常见合成形式：garden centre／garden center（园艺中心）、garden shed（花园工具棚）、beer garden（露天啤酒庭院）、roof garden（屋顶花园）、garden-variety（普通的；常见的，主要用于美式英语）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, garden is a complete base, not gard + -en; it becomes a verb through conversion. Main family members are gardens, gardened, gardening, and gardener, formed with -er. Common compounds include garden centre/garden center, garden shed, beer garden, roof garden, and garden-variety, meaning ordinary or commonplace, especially in American English.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: yard（院子）强调住宅周围的室外空间，未必种植花草；plot（小块土地）强调划分出来、常供种植的一块地；park（公园）通常是更大的公共休闲空间。garden 的重点是有意栽培植物的园地。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A yard is outdoor space around a house and need not contain cultivated plants. A plot is a defined piece of land, often used for growing things. A park is usually a larger public recreation area. Garden emphasizes deliberately cultivated planting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先圈起一块地，再种上花和菜：围地 → 花园 → 打理花园。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Enclose some ground and grow plants there: an enclosure becomes a garden, and caring for it is gardening.

senses.meaning_zh: 代理机构；中介公司；提供专门服务的公司
senses.meaning_en: a business that provides a service or acts on behalf of clients
senses.english_definition: An agency is a business that provides a particular service or arranges things for other people or organizations.
senses.collocation_en: a travel agency; an advertising agency
senses.collocation_zh: 旅行社；广告公司
senses.sentence_en: We booked our holiday through a local travel agency.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们通过当地一家旅行社预订了度假行程。

senses.meaning_zh: 政府机构；承担专门职能的组织
senses.meaning_en: an organization responsible for a particular area of work, especially in government
senses.english_definition: An agency is an organization that carries out a particular kind of work, often as part of a government.
senses.collocation_en: a government agency; a law enforcement agency
senses.collocation_zh: 政府机构；执法机构
senses.sentence_en: Several government agencies are working together on the investigation.
senses.sentence_zh: 几个政府机构正在联合开展这项调查。

senses.meaning_en: the ability to make choices and act to influence events
senses.english_definition: Agency is the ability to make your own decisions and take actions that affect your life or circumstances.
senses.collocation_en: personal agency; a sense of agency
senses.collocation_zh: 个人能动性；自主掌控感
senses.sentence_en: Giving students meaningful choices can strengthen their sense of agency.
senses.sentence_zh: 让学生作出有实际意义的选择，可以增强他们的自主掌控感。

senses.meaning_zh: 作用；促成某事的力量或手段，较正式
senses.meaning_en: the action, influence, or means through which something happens
senses.english_definition: If something happens through the agency of a person or thing, it happens because of their action or influence.
senses.collocation_en: through the agency of; by the agency of
senses.collocation_zh: 通过……的作用或促成；借助……的力量
senses.sentence_en: The agreement was reached through the agency of a neutral mediator.
senses.sentence_zh: 这项协议是在一位中立调解人的促成下达成的。

etymology_story.zh: Agency 由 agent 一词发展而来；agent 最终源于拉丁语 agere“做、行动”的现在分词形式。该词早期指行动或产生作用的能力，后来扩展为代理关系及履行代理或专门职能的机构；现代社会科学中的“能动性”延续了“能够行动”的核心。
etymology_story.en: Agency developed from agent, ultimately based on the present participle of Latin agere, 'to do or act.' Early meanings concerned action or effective power, later extending to representation and organizations carrying out particular functions; the modern social-science sense preserves the idea of being able to act.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系为 agent（代理人；行动者）↔ agency（代理机构；能动性），伴随词干变化，可类比 regent ↔ regency，不宜机械拼成 agentcy。agency 的复数为 agencies，按辅音字母 + y 结尾名词的规则变 y 为 i 再加 -es。主要相关词：agent、agents、agency、agencies、agentive（施事的）、agentivity（施事性）、agentic（具有能动性的）、agential（行动者的；涉及能动性的）；后四项多见于语言学或社会科学。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family relation is agent ↔ agency, with a stem change comparable to regent ↔ regency; simply joining agent and -cy would not produce the correct spelling. The plural is agencies, changing consonant + y to -ies. Related family members include agent, agents, agency, agencies, agentive, agentivity, agentic, and agential; the last four mainly occur in linguistics or the social sciences.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 机构义：bureau（局；处）偏指行政部门或专门办事机构，organization（组织）范围更广，未必代表客户办事。能动性义：autonomy（自主权；自主性）强调不受外部控制，agency 强调作出选择并采取行动的能力。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For an institution, bureau often suggests an administrative office, while organization is broader and need not act for clients. For the capacity to act, autonomy emphasizes freedom from external control; agency emphasizes the ability to choose and take effective action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“行动”：能自己行动是能动性，替别人办事的组织是代理机构。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep 'acting' at the center: the power to act is agency, and a body that acts for others is an agency.
